f.population: Patients with posterior single-tooth implant-supported restorations on CAD-CAM abutments
f.intervention: CAD-CAM abutment emergence profile and profile angle at 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3 mm from the implant-abutment junction
f.main_result: Convex emergence profile gave greater marginal bone loss than concave or straight; profile angle correlated with bone loss within 2 mm of the junction (cut-offs about 20-34 degrees).
f.funding_coi: No competing interests declared

f.population: Participants receiving single-unit implants in healed sites
f.intervention: Definitive abutment connected at implant placement (one abutment-one time)
f.comparison: Healing abutments disconnected and reconnected three times at 8, 10 and 12 weeks
f.main_result: At 2 years cumulative bone loss was -0.61 mm (definitive abutment) vs -0.81 mm (healing abutment), no significant difference.
materials_brands: P-I Morse Taper M+N implant (Zimmer Biomet)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Results relate to one implant model and no anterior sites were included.

f.population: 21 partially edentulous posterior patients each receiving two tissue-level implants
f.intervention: Tissue-level implant with convergent transmucosal collar
f.comparison: Tissue-level implant with divergent transmucosal collar
outcomes: peri-implant bone loss on periapical radiographs
f.main_result: Convergent collar lost less bone (0.29 ± 0.34 mm) than divergent (0.60 ± 0.63 mm), P = .031.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 22 patients with 40 single-tooth implants in posterior regions
f.intervention: Customized zirconia abutments with cemented all-ceramic crowns
f.comparison: Customized titanium abutments with cemented metal-ceramic crowns
f.main_result: At 13 years technical survival of abutments and crowns was 100% in both groups, with similar biological and esthetic outcomes; implant survival was 90%.
f.sample_size: 15 patients with 21 abutments examined (13 zirconia, 8 titanium)
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest; Nobel Biocare supplied abutments

f.main_result: A biologically driven protocol: 3.5-4 mm vertical distance from implant-abutment interface to mucosal margin, polished titanium/zirconia submucosal materials, slim vertical subcritical contour, one abutment/one time.

f.population: 32 partially edentulous patients from five Italian clinics, two splinted implants each
f.intervention: Implants placed with recorded insertion torque of 30-100 Ncm, early loaded at 2 months
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone resorption at 2, 6 and 12 months
f.main_result: No correlation between insertion torque (30-100 Ncm) and bone resorption; mean resorption 0.9 mm at 12 months.

f.population: Patients treated with Nobel Biocare bone level implants by four surgeons
f.intervention: Permanent abutment placed at implant surgery (one-abutment one-time)
f.comparison: Conventional healing abutment (HA cohort)
outcomes: marginal bone loss at 3 months and longest follow-up
f.main_result: One-abutment one-time did not affect presence of MBL but reduced its magnitude by 0.300 mm where bone loss occurred (p=0.023); mean MBL 0.52 mm.
f.limitations: Cohort design limits conclusions.

f.population: Patients needing a single-tooth implant crown in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Zirconia abutment (Thommen SPI ART) with Lava zirconia crown
f.comparison: Titanium abutment (Thommen SPI EASY, CPTi grade 4)
f.main_result: Zirconia abutments showed a non-significant tendency to better aesthetics (ICAI 7.6 vs 11.3 at 1 year); two zirconia abutment fractures occurred.
f.sample_size: 38 patients recruited, 25 of 30 randomized analysed at 1 year
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by unrestricted grant from Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Sample size not sufficient to contrast outcomes.

f.population: 5 beagle dogs, 6 implants each (Branemark System)
f.intervention: Abutments of c.p. titanium, ceramic (Al2O3), gold alloy and short titanium with porcelain-fused-to-gold, followed by 6 months of plaque control
f.comparison: c.p. titanium control abutments
outcomes: mucosal attachment dimensions (junctional epithelium, connective tissue)
f.main_result: Titanium and ceramic abutments allowed a mucosal attachment of ~2 mm epithelium and 1-1.5 mm connective tissue; gold alloy and porcelain abutments showed recession and bone resorption.
f.follow_up: 6 months of plaque control after abutment connection

f.population: Partially edentulous patients with missing single or multiple teeth (review question); only in vitro studies of implant-supported FDPs were found
f.intervention: Additively manufactured (3D-printed, DLP/SLA) implant-supported fixed dental prostheses
f.comparison: Subtractively manufactured (milled) implant-supported fixed dental prostheses
f.main_result: No clinical study met the inclusion criteria and six in vitro studies gave inconclusive results on marginal/internal discrepancies and mechanical properties, so no meta-analysis was possible.
f.sample_size: 2,184 records identified; 6 in vitro studies included
f.funding_coi: Financially supported by the Clinic for Reconstructive Dentistry, University of Zurich
f.limitations: No clinical studies found (only in vitro), no grey literature search, language restriction, and incomplete material and processing data

f.population: 16 healthy volunteers wearing intraoral splints carrying discs of five implant/abutment materials
f.intervention: 24-hour intraoral biofilm formation on discs of gold-based and silver-based noble alloys, zirconia and PEKK
f.comparison: Titanium zirconium alloy (TiZr) as reference material
f.main_result: Silver-based (PA) and gold-based (EL) alloys formed least biofilm; versus PA, biofilm mass was 1.5x higher for EL, 1.7x PEKK, 2.2x TiZr and 2.4x zirconia.
f.sample_size: 16 volunteers, two runs, 15 discs per splint
f.funding_coi: Institut Straumann AG and Cendres+Métaux SA provided the test materials

f.population: Literature on biologic width around dental implants (animal histology and human clinical studies)
f.comparison: Biologic width around natural teeth
outcomes: biologic width dimensions (junctional epithelium, connective tissue, sulcus)
influence of surgical technique, loading, surface, abutment, implant position
f.main_result: Most studies report larger peri-implant biologic width than around natural teeth, with contradictory data on influencing factors.

f.population: Patients with posterior mandibular partial edentulism treated with at least two implants
f.intervention: 2 mm (Group A) or 1 mm (Group B) abutment connected at implant surgery
f.comparison: 2 mm abutment connected after 2 months in a second stage (Group C)
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone change at 3 years was 0.35, 0.60 and 0.71 mm in groups A, B and C, with a significant difference between A and C (p=0.048).
f.sample_size: 29 subjects and 59 implants at 3 years (33 subjects, 68 implants at start)
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech, Dentsply Implants)
f.funding_coi: Two authors are usual speakers for Dentsply; no financial interests declared in the products

f.population: Subjects receiving posterior single implant-supported crowns (41 subjects, 56 implants)
f.intervention: Screw-retained monolithic lithium-disilicate crowns luted to titanium bases
f.comparison: Cemented monolithic lithium-disilicate crowns on individualized titanium abutments
outcomes: biological complications (mucositis by BOP, gingival and plaque index)
f.main_result: Mucositis incidence at 12 months was 14.2% (screw-retained) vs 17.9% (cemented), marginal bone loss 0.03-0.15 mm; retention mode did not influence complication rate.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Ivoclar Vivadent; implants and metal components funded by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; two authors received honoraria from funders
f.limitations: Short 24-month follow-up, radiographs only up to 12 months, and a power analysis based on an estimated effect size

f.population: Patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Screw-retained crown on a directly veneered one-piece customized zirconia abutment (SCREW)
f.comparison: Cemented lithium disilicate crown on a one-piece customized zirconia abutment (CEM)
f.main_result: At 5 years implant survival was 100% and restoration survival 82.4% in both groups, with similar marginal bone change (median -0.23 mm CEM vs -0.15 mm SCREW) and 15.4% technical complications in each group.
f.sample_size: 34 patients with 34 single-tooth implants; 26 re-examined at 5 years
f.funding_coi: International Team for Implantology research grant 780_2011 and the University of Zurich clinic; authors report no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small sample size, relatively high drop-out rate (8 of 34), no posterior implants, strict inclusion criteria

f.population: 115 consecutive patients with a single failing molar replaced by an immediate posterior implant
f.intervention: Flapless molar extraction with immediate implant, bone graft and a custom chair-side healing abutment (Anatomic Harmony Abutment)
f.main_result: Overall implant survival was 98.26% with 3 failures in 115 implants (100% maxilla, 96.08% mandible), with follow-up up to 8 years.
f.funding_coi: No relevant financial relationship with a commercial interest declared

f.population: 19 patients edentulous from severe periodontal disease with 160 implants supporting fixed full-arch screw-retained metal-ceramic restorations
f.intervention: OsseoSpeed Astra Tech TX implants with fixed full-arch metal-ceramic restorations on uni-abutments
f.comparison: Abutment heights of 1, 2, 4 and 6 mm compared with each other
f.main_result: No implant failed in 5 years and only 14 of 160 implants (8.75%) lost more than 2 mm of bone; MBL was larger with 1 mm abutments (-0.987 mm) than 2, 4 or 6 mm.
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed Astra Tech TX implants (Dentsply Implants)
f.funding_coi: Junta de Andalucía grants; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Retrospective design with a not very large number of patients, and panoramic radiographs

f.population: 122 subjects with a single screw-retained implant restoration in the anterior or premolar region
f.intervention: Emergence angle, profile and mucosal tunnel depth of the crown measured on superimposed digital scans
f.main_result: Site-specific platform-level emergence angle, profile and mucosal tunnel depth were significantly associated with detectable plaque (p<.01) and bleeding on probing (p<.02).
f.sample_size: 122 subjects with single screw-retained implant crowns
f.funding_coi: Periodontology Research Fund of HKU Faculty of Dentistry and European Research Group on Periodontology; authors declare no conflict
f.limitations: Cross-sectional design unsuitable for chronological consistency, small sample, mixed bone- and tissue-level implants

f.population: Adults needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla (first premolar to first premolar); 54 of 60 recruited completed
f.intervention: Screw-retained CAD/CAM zirconia abutments (Atlantis) with concave transmucosal morphology, veneered with feldspathic porcelain
f.comparison: Linear divergent transmucosal abutment morphology (control)
outcomes: probing depth and bleeding on probing
f.main_result: No significant differences between concave and linear divergent abutments at 1 year; implant survival 100%, restoration survival 98.2%.
f.sample_size: 54 subjects completed (29 concave, 25 linear divergent) of 60 recruited
f.funding_coi: Partial funding from Dentsply Sirona (investigator-initiated study); two authors received lecture honoraria from Dentsply Sirona

f.population: Patients with single implant prostheses restored with titanium base abutments (6 RCTs plus 23 prospective/retrospective studies; 857 prostheses)
f.intervention: Titanium base abutments (TBA) for single-unit implant prostheses
f.comparison: Other abutments (in the six RCTs)
f.main_result: TBA restorations had an estimated 98.6% survival at 1 year (95% CI 97.9-99.4%); survival did not differ from other abutments in RCTs (OR 0.74)
f.sample_size: 857 single implant-supported prostheses with TBA; 6 RCTs in meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by the ITI Consensus Conference; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Short 1-year follow-up, heterogeneous TBA designs, and limited data on fit tolerance and geometry

f.population: Partially or completely edentulous patients with implants in RCTs comparing connection designs
f.intervention: External, internal flat-to-flat or conical implant abutment connection
f.comparison: Other connection designs (positive control connection)
f.main_result: Conical connections gave lower marginal bone loss (P=.011) and fewer prosthetic complications (P=.038) than external hexagon; no difference in survival or biologic complications
f.funding_coi: No specific grant received

f.population: Participants with posterior partial edentulism (Kennedy Class I or II)
f.intervention: Internal conus design implants (Astra Tech Fixture ST)
f.comparison: External hex design implants (Osseotite Standard)
f.main_result: Mean bone change from placement to 3 years was -0.25 mm (ICI) vs -0.5 mm (EXI); EXI had more abutment complications (11 vs 1 participants)
f.sample_size: 39 participants with 47 ICI and 46 EXI implants
f.limitations: Neither participant nor investigator was blinded

f.population: 22 patients with at least two adjacent missing teeth receiving bridges on bone level platform-switched implants
f.intervention: 3 mm definitive abutments
f.comparison: 1 mm definitive abutments
outcomes: interproximal implant bone loss at 3 and 6 months
association with patient and implant variables
f.main_result: At 6 months 1-mm abutments had greater interproximal bone loss than 3-mm abutments (0.91 vs 0.11 mm)
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by LASAK, Praha; authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 90 sets of 4.5 x 10 mm bone level implants with conical hybrid connection mounted in acrylic blocks
f.intervention: Abutment angulations of 15° and 25° and collar lengths of 2 and 4 mm, with dynamic cyclic loading
f.comparison: 0° (straight) abutment and 2 mm collar
outcomes: percentage of removal torque loss before and after cyclic loading
f.main_result: Screw loosening increased with abutment angulation and collar length after 100,000 loading cycles (post-load RTL 23.5% at 0°, 33.4% at 15°, 40.1% at 25°)
f.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
f.limitations: Results limited to this in vitro setting

f.population: 11 edentulous patients with five implants each in the anterior mandible
f.intervention: Subcrestal (1-3 mm) implant placement, immediately loaded
f.comparison: Equicrestal implant placement
f.main_result: Subcrestal placement had less crestal bone loss than equicrestal (-0.80 vs -0.99 mm at 5 years), not significant
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest
f.limitations: Wide range of subcrestal depth (1-3 mm) and small number of patients, so each depth could not be evaluated

f.population: 44 Straumann bone-level implants (22 TorcFit, 22 CrossFit connection)
f.intervention: Angled screw access channel titanium-base abutments with screw-retained crowns
f.comparison: Straight screw channel abutments (hybrid zirconia abutments with cement-retained crowns); TorcFit vs CrossFit connection
outcomes: removal torque value after 24 h and after cyclic loading
f.main_result: CrossFit connection gave higher removal torque and lower torque loss; no screw loosening during 2.4 million cycles and screw channel angle did not affect stability after loading
f.funding_coi: Buser Implant Foundation Junior Investigator Grant; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Only one implant system and two connections tested; cyclic loading without liquid medium or enamel antagonists

f.population: 120 sets of dental implants and abutments (Implacil De Bortoli), four platform/diameter groups of 30
f.intervention: Switched-platform implants (regular 4.0 mm and wide 5.0 mm) at three simulated bone insertion levels (0, 3, 5 mm loss), fracture strength tested at 30 degrees
f.comparison: Matched-platform implants of the same diameters
f.main_result: Switched-platform implants had lower fracture strength at all insertion levels but less deformation than matched-platform implants
materials_brands: Implacil De Bortoli implants and abutments

f.population: Two clinical cases (e.g. a 45-year-old woman needing replacement of a maxillary lateral incisor)
f.intervention: Customized definitive zirconia abutment fabricated in the lab from registered soft tissue contours and inserted at stage-two surgery
f.main_result: The pre-fabricated definitive abutment guides peri-implant soft tissue healing and replicates an optimal emergence profile (concept demonstrated in two cases, no controlled data)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Further histologic and clinical research and long-term follow-up are needed

outcomes: clinical and histologic characteristics of healthy peri-implant tissues
f.main_result: Healthy peri-implant mucosa is about 3-4 mm high with about 2 mm of epithelium, and roughly 60% of the intrabony implant is in contact with mineralized bone
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 80 dental implants (8 groups of 10) with an inoculated internal lumen
f.intervention: New internal conical connection with double taper principle (DAT, CSR-DAT implants)
f.comparison: Seven other internal connections (groups 1-7)
outcomes: bacterial microleakage (E. coli CFU) from inside to outside the implant-abutment assembly over 96 h
f.main_result: No contamination in the test connection in the first 6 h and none in 7 of 10 implants at 96 h, whereas all control connections were significantly contaminated (>100,000 CFU/ul) by 24 h (p<0.05).
materials_brands: DAT connection (Double Action Tight) on CSR-DAT implants

f.population: 192 bone-level implants in 119 patients
f.intervention: Implants grouped by transmucosal abutment height (>2 mm vs <2 mm) combined with restorative emergence angle (<30 vs >30 degrees)
f.comparison: Long-Gradual, Long-Abrupt, Short-Gradual and Short-Abrupt groups compared with each other
f.main_result: Short-abrupt group had 0.48 mm more MBL than Long-Gradual and about 4x greater odds of peri-implantitis than Long-Abrupt (OR 4.19); each 1 mm of abutment height cut the odds of MBL by 51%.
f.follow_up: at least 1 year between radiographs T0 (12-18 months after crown placement) and T1
f.limitations: Retrospective design; level of initial crown emergence not documented; only bone-level implants evaluated

f.population: 44 patients with single-tooth gaps in the esthetic zone (44 two-piece implants)
f.intervention: Screw-retained all-ceramic single crown (veneered zirconia abutment as one piece)
f.comparison: Cemented all-ceramic single crown (veneered lithium disilicate crown on zirconia abutment, resin cement)
f.main_result: Cemented restorations had a higher biological complication rate (36.8% vs 0.0%) and overall complication rate (68.4% vs 22.7%) than screw-retained; marginal bone levels were equal (0.4 mm).
materials_brands: IPS e.max / e.max Ceram lithium disilicate crowns
f.funding_coi: Funded by University of Zurich; authors report no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small sample (44 patients), 6.8% drop-out and implants mostly in premolar sites

f.population: 30 patients with titanium implants in the posterior mandible and maxilla (18 in per-protocol analysis)
f.intervention: Hydrophilic modMA and modMA Ti-Zr healing abutments left transmucosal for 8 weeks, then biopsied
f.comparison: Hydrophobic machined (M) healing abutments
f.main_result: Per protocol (18 patients), epithelial contact was highest at modMA2 (53.45%) then modMA1 (32.25%) and machined (23.15%); connective tissue contact followed the same order.
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant of Institut Straumann AG; authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: Fifteen edentulous sites treated with implants (posterior)
f.intervention: Titanium, zirconia and gold alloy abutments with 8-week healing, then peri-implant tissue harvested for histology
f.comparison: Titanium abutment as reference for zirconia and gold alloy
f.main_result: Titanium and zirconia had similar histological attachment percentages while gold alloy was significantly lower (P=.004), with higher inflammation.
f.funding_coi: Chulalongkorn University funding; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Tissue conditions reported after only 2 months, i.e. early soft tissue maturation

f.main_result: Gold alloys, ceramics and amino-alcohol contamination appear to promote epithelial downgrowth, whereas concave abutments, platform switching and microgrooved surfaces are believed to inhibit it.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no financial interest in companies whose products were mentioned

f.population: 16 of 24 originally recruited patients needing a single-tooth replacement in the esthetic area
f.intervention: Immediate non-occluding provisional crown on hydrophilic bone-level implant (n=7)
f.comparison: No provisional crown, definitive restoration at 16 weeks (n=9)
f.main_result: At 60 months peri-implant bone loss was similar in test (-0.42 mm) and control (-0.37 mm) groups, with high survival and success in both.
materials_brands: Straumann Bone Level RC SLActive implant
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by Institut Straumann AG
f.limitations: Small sample size does not allow statistical inference at 60 months

f.population: Partially edentulous patients treated with dental implants
f.intervention: Concave/convergent implant transmucosal profiles
f.comparison: Divergent/parallel implant transmucosal profiles
f.main_result: Concave/convergent profiles had significantly less marginal bone loss (mean difference 0.772 mm, P<.001); no significant effects for soft tissue outcomes or platform-matching connections.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 75 participants with 105 implants in molar or premolar sites
f.intervention: Implants of identical design with conical connection
f.comparison: External hexagon vs internal hexagon vs conical connection (35 implants each)
outcomes: probing depth, plaque index, bleeding on probing
f.main_result: Marginal bone level changed over time (P<.001) but did not differ between connection types (P=.152); 7 implant failures, no significant difference (P=.356).
f.funding_coi: Agreement between University of Barcelona and Avinent SA; several authors declare Avinent and other industry support

f.main_result: Implant position, implant-abutment connection, restorative material, restoration design and cleansability all influence peri-implant tissue health; malpositioned implants produce emergence profiles that limit hygiene access.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 13 included studies (in vitro, RCT, prospective and retrospective cohort) on implant-abutment connections
f.intervention: Different implant-abutment connections: external hexagon, internal hexagon, conical
f.comparison: Conical versus external and traditional internal hexagon connections
f.main_result: All connections show some micro-gap and micro-leakage, but conical connections seem to behave better, with fewer mechanical complications and probably lower marginal bone loss.
f.funding_coi: No funding, no competing interests
f.limitations: Studies used different approaches and are hard to compare; more prospective in vivo studies needed.

f.population: Axisymmetric finite element model of an axially loaded mandibular titanium implant with retention elements on the neck
f.intervention: Conical implant-abutment interface
f.comparison: Flat top implant-abutment interface
f.main_result: The conical interface lowered the peak bone-implant interfacial shear stress versus the flat top and moved it more apically, so it can theoretically resist a larger axial load.

f.population: Implants with their abutments from three systems (Nobel Replace Select, Straumann, Intra-lock), about 4.5 mm diameter
f.intervention: Toluidine blue placed inside the implant screw, abutment connected per manufacturer torque, release into distilled water measured spectrophotometrically up to 144 h
f.comparison: The three implant systems against each other
f.main_result: All three systems leaked; after 144 h about 22% of the dye was released from Intra-lock, 55% from Straumann and 100% from Replace Select.
f.funding_coi: Supported by NYU dental school research training program; implants supplied by manufacturers

f.population: 30 patients with single posterior implants
f.intervention: Convergent abutments (machined, or with ultrathin threaded micro-surface)
f.comparison: Machined divergent abutment
outcomes: vertical width of connective and epithelial tissue (histology)
connective tissue vertical width by synchrotron microtomography
f.main_result: Connective tissue was significantly taller next to convergent than divergent abutments, and the ultrathin threaded convergent surface had the greatest collagen bundle amount and density in 3D.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: The model does not reproduce cyclic masticatory loading, and synchrotron imaging cannot separate transverse from longitudinal fibers.

f.population: 18 histological animal studies (mostly dogs, also pigs and minipigs) of transmucosal implant components
f.intervention: Different abutment or transmucosal collar materials and surface modifications
f.comparison: Machined titanium transmucosal surface
f.main_result: Only 4 of 18 studies could be meta-analyzed; attachment dimensions were comparable to machined titanium except a significantly higher ajE-CBI distance for chemically modified acid-etched surfaces (SMD 1.0, 95% CI 0.22 to 1.79).
f.limitations: No study had low risk of bias in all domains; heterogeneity limited meta-analysis; animal data do not allow definitive conclusions.

f.population: 64 implants in 25 partially edentulous patients (two adjacent implants in posterior jaw)
f.intervention: 3-mm high cylindrical abutments
f.comparison: 3-mm high wide abutments
f.main_result: Cylindrical abutments gave significantly less marginal bone remodeling and loss than wide abutments over 12 months, and less bleeding on probing (p < .05).
f.funding_coi: Not funded; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Results apply only to subcrestal bone-level implants with conical internal connection, platform switching and this abutment design; evaluator could not be blinded.

f.population: 120 implants (60 external hexagon, 60 Morse taper) with straight or 15 degree angulated abutments in methacrylate blocks
f.intervention: Abutments screwed at 10, 20 or 30 Ncm, then thermal and cyclic loading
f.comparison: External vs Morse taper connection; straight vs angulated abutments; 10 vs 20 vs 30 Ncm
outcomes: marginal misfit at implant-abutment interface (SEM, micrometers)
f.main_result: Morse taper connections had the lowest misfit (0.6 µm with straight and angulated abutments at 30 Ncm), and misfit decreased as torque increased; all groups were below 3 µm.
materials_brands: Mozo-Grau MG-Osseous (external hexagon) and MG-Inhex (11 degree Morse taper) implants and abutments
f.funding_coi: Research grant from University Complutense of Madrid and Mozo Grau S.A.; no conflicts declared

f.population: 61 patients with single implant crowns after early placement in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Bone level implant neck with hydrophilic micro-rough surface and platform-switching (n=20)
f.comparison: Soft tissue level implant with machined neck and butt-joint interface (n=41)
outcomes: facial bone crest height and thickness by CBCT
f.main_result: Facial bone crest was 0.2 mm above the shoulder for bone-level versus 1.6 mm below for soft-tissue-level implants, and the saucer-like defect width was reduced by 40% with the bone-level design.
f.sample_size: 61 patients (20 bone level, 41 soft tissue level)
materials_brands: Straumann soft tissue level implant, SLA surface
Straumann bone level implant, SLActive surface
f.funding_coi: Departmental funds and a research grant from Institut Straumann AG; no conflicts declared

f.population: Four observational studies: 912 implants in 397 adult participants with restorations in function at least 3 years
f.intervention: Implant restorations with emergence angle >30 degrees (or convex profile)
f.comparison: Implant restorations with emergence angle of 30 degrees or less (or concave/straight profile)
outcomes: changes in peri-implant marginal bone level
f.main_result: Emergence angle of 30 degrees or less gave less bone level change than >30 degrees, not significant (MD 0.80, p=0.09); convex profiles had higher peri-implantitis (57.8% vs 21.3%, RR 2.32).
f.funding_coi: None of the included studies had external funding (review's own funding not stated in text)
f.limitations: Evidence is of low to moderate certainty; included studies did not adjust for within-patient clustering.

f.population: 25 patients each receiving two 4-mm implants in the posterior mandible
f.intervention: Platform-switching implant (3.3-mm platform)
f.comparison: Standard-platform implant (4-mm platform), within-patient
f.main_result: At 3 years mean bone loss was 0.69 mm with platform switching and 0.74 mm with standard platform (difference 0.05 mm, 95% CI -0.19 to 0.29); no effect of platform type (p = .363).

f.population: 32 anterior monolithic screw-retained zirconia crowns on two-piece ceramic or titanium-zirconium implants (in vitro)
f.intervention: Straight (0°) vs angulated (25°) screw-channel titanium bases under fatigue loading, on ceramic implants
f.comparison: Two-piece titanium-zirconium implants (control) and straight screw-channel bases
f.main_result: Mean bending moments were 241 N cm (Ti-Zr, 0°), 303 (Ti-Zr, 25°), 326 (ceramic, 0°) and 434 N cm (ceramic, 25°); angulated bases and ceramic implants gave significantly higher values; all survived fatigue.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant; implants and abutments provided by Straumann; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Deviation from the ISO 14801 standard test setup

f.population: 60 titanium implants placed in edentulous mandibular areas of five foxhounds
f.intervention: Implants with SLA surface all the way to the top (no machined collar), microgap placed at different heights relative to the bone crest
f.comparison: Implants with a 1.8 mm machined collar (control)
outcomes: crestal bone level (distance from microgap to first bone-to-implant contact) on non-decalcified histology
f.main_result: At the same microgap level, machined-collar implants lost significantly more crestal bone than SLA-to-top implants (A vs E P=0.034; C vs D P<0.001).
f.sample_size: 60 implants (30 machined, 30 SLA collar) in 5 foxhounds
materials_brands: Institut Straumann cp grade IV titanium implants, SLA surface (control with machined collar; test fully SLA)
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grants; Hermann, Buser and Cochran received research funding from Institute Straumann, which supplied the implants

f.population: 27 implant-abutment connections (9 designs, 3 each) from Southern Implants, Straumann, Ankylos and Neodent, inoculated with E. coli endotoxin
f.intervention: Endotoxin placed in the implant lumen, abutment connected, implant submerged in pyrogen-free water and sampled up to 168 h (LAL test)
f.comparison: External vs internal connection designs and different systems
outcomes: endotoxin leakage (EU) at 0 min, 10 min, 3 h, 24 h, 168 h
f.main_result: All 6 external connections leaked; of 21 internal, 9 did not leak and 12 did; mean log endotoxin was higher for external than internal (p=0.015); Straumann Synocta, Cross-fit and Ankylos showed no measurable leakage.
materials_brands: Straumann Synocta, Straumann Bone Level Tapered Cross-fit, Dentsply Ankylos, Neodent Drive CM, Southern Implants connections
f.funding_coi: Implants, abutments and accessories sponsored by the manufacturers; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Sample size was convenient, based on research questions and cost constraints

f.population: 145 patients with 273 implants placed by a single clinician (retrospective chart and panoramic radiograph data)
f.intervention: Prosthetic abutment height (customized abutments) as exposure
f.comparison: Abutment height groups: <2 mm, 2 to <3 mm, >=3 mm
f.main_result: Prevalence and mean marginal bone loss decreased as abutment height increased (Spearman rho -0.178, P=.006); abutment height should not exceed 4 mm.
f.funding_coi: National Health Insurance Service grant; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Smoking (and periodontitis) not evaluated

f.population: 36 partially edentulous patients with 72 bone-level implants (2 per patient) restored with 2- to 4-unit screw-retained prostheses
f.intervention: Screw-retained prosthesis connected directly to the implant shoulder (no intermediate abutment)
f.comparison: Prosthesis connected through a 3-mm standardised intermediate abutment
f.main_result: At 12 months marginal bone loss was 0.17 ± 0.24 mm (direct, test) vs 0.09 ± 0.15 mm (with abutment, control), not significantly different.
materials_brands: Ticare Inhex implants (Mozo-Grau), RBM TC surface, platform-switching, tapered
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by Ticare, Mozo-Grau; one author conducts grant research with Ticare

f.population: 60 internal conical connection implants (4.3 mm, Conelog) with abutment-crown restorations, in vitro
f.intervention: Monolithic lithium disilicate, zirconia or PICN abutment-crowns bonded to titanium bases, or lithium disilicate crown on customized titanium abutment, after thermo-mechanical aging
f.comparison: Porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns on gold abutments
f.main_result: Survival ranged from 100% (titanium abutment + lithium disilicate; titanium base + lithium disilicate) to 58.3% (titanium base + PICN); PICN had significantly lower bending moments.
f.follow_up: Aging of 1,200,000 chewing cycles with thermocycling
f.funding_coi: Grant from the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; manufacturers supplied materials

f.population: Finite element model of a 12-mm ITI solid-screw implant with a 6-degree, 7-mm abutment
f.intervention: 8-degree Morse taper implant-abutment connection modelled under axial and off-axis loading
f.comparison: Hypothetical butt joint connection
outcomes: stress distribution in screw threads and joint
maximal thread tension at 30 degree off-axis load
f.main_result: Axial preload was 53.2 N for the taper vs 358.6 N for the butt joint; at 30 degree off-axis load maximal thread tension was 1,176 MPa (taper) vs 1,403 MPa (butt joint), indicating superior mechanics of conical connections.
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (Institut Straumann) solid-screw implant with solid abutment
f.funding_coi: Two authors are affiliated with Institut Straumann AG; no funding statement

f.population: 20 sterile Morse taper implant-abutment assemblies (10 Bicon, 10 Ankylos)
f.intervention: Tapped-in (Bicon) vs screwed-in (Ankylos) Morse taper abutments, inner implant inoculated with Streptococcus sanguinis
f.comparison: Bicon vs Ankylos
outcomes: bacterial leakage along the implant-abutment interface (solution cloudiness over 14 days)
f.main_result: Bacterial leakage occurred in 2 of 10 assemblies of each system (20%), with no significant difference between them.
materials_brands: Bicon implants and abutments (Bicon Dental Implant)

f.population: 40 patients with metal-ceramic cemented bridges on at least two healthy implants loaded for 5 years
f.intervention: Four implant-abutment connections (external hex, double internal hex, internal hex with external collar, conical) sampled for bacteria by real-time PCR
f.comparison: External hexagon connection (control group)
outcomes: absolute bacterial load (10 species and total count)
f.main_result: All connections were contaminated after 5 years; connection design may influence bacterial levels, with conical and internal-hex-with-collar connections showing significantly lower total bacterial counts.
f.follow_up: At least 5 years of functional loading

f.population: 64 conical connection implants with their abutments (in vitro)
f.intervention: CAD-CAM milled, laser-sintered and cast Co-Cr abutments and milled zirconia abutments, after chewing simulation and thermocycling, immersed in P. gingivalis methylene blue solution
f.comparison: Cast Co-Cr abutments and other fabrication techniques/materials
f.main_result: 47% (30/64) of implant-abutments leaked; lowest bacterial counts in milled Co-Cr (5.17E+02 CFU/ml) then zirconia (7.70E+03), higher in cast (9.39E+03) and laser-sintered Co-Cr (2.4E+05).
f.funding_coi: Partly funded by Spanish Society of Prosthodontics Research Scholarship; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 30 included in vitro and human studies on implant-abutment connections
f.intervention: Different implant-abutment connections (external hexagon, internal hexagon, Morse taper) under static or dynamic loading and various torques
f.comparison: Between connection types, loading conditions, torque values and titanium vs zirconia abutments
f.main_result: Nearly all studies showed some microleakage at the interface; Morse taper implants leaked much less than other connections and leakage rose under dynamic loading.
f.follow_up: Included studies: five minutes to five years

f.population: 20 Sweden & Martina implants with prosthetic components (in vitro)
f.intervention: Inoculation of the inner implant with E. faecalis or A. actinomycetemcomitans, 14-day broth turbidity check, and SEM measurement of the implant-abutment microgap
f.comparison: Group 1 Kohno Straight implants vs Group 2 Kohno TG DES implants (both Morse taper)
f.main_result: No leakage occurred in either connection (0/10 each); microgap differed significantly (0.0199 vs 0.6329 μm mean, p<0.01).

f.population: A 45-year-old patient with partially edentulous maxilla and previous prosthodontic treatment failure
f.intervention: Implant-supported restoration with multi-unit abutments and a definitive prosthetic construction six months after osseointegration
f.main_result: Authors conclude multi-unit abutments give surgical flexibility (tilted posterior implants avoiding sinus grafting) and prosthetic benefits; no measured results reported in the available text.

f.population: 92 patients at seven international centers receiving single-tooth Brånemark implant restorations
f.intervention: Single Brånemark system implants supporting single crowns
outcomes: abutment screw loosening and other complications
f.main_result: After 3 years 82 of 92 patients remained, no further implants failed, cumulative success 97.2% and marginal bone loss about 0.1 mm annually.
f.sample_size: 107 implants in 92 patients (95 implants in 82 patients at 3 years)

f.population: Patients requiring implant-supported single-unit restorations (25 studies, mostly in vitro)
f.intervention: CAD/CAM monolithic implant-supported ceramic restorations bonded to titanium inserts or bases
f.comparison: Traditional screw-retained implant-supported restorations
f.main_result: No clinical studies were found; laboratory studies suggest Ti inserts improve fracture strength, protect the connection from wear and give better marginal fit than full-zirconia abutments.
f.limitations: No clinical studies exist and the in vitro studies were heterogeneous, so no meta-analysis was possible.

f.population: 33 patients with thin peri-implant mucosa (≤2 mm) receiving 66 platform-switched bone-level implants
f.intervention: 3 mm abutments with implants placed 2 mm subcrestally
f.comparison: 1 mm abutments with equicrestal implant placement
outcomes: interproximal peri-implant bone loss at 3, 6 and 12 months
f.main_result: Mean interproximal bone loss at 12 months was 0.95 mm with 1 mm abutments versus 0.12 mm with 3 mm abutments (significant at every time point).
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by LASAK; authors declare no conflict of interest.
f.limitations: Results apply only to bone-level platform-switched implants with internal-connection abutments placed with the one abutment-one time protocol.

f.population: 40 participants aged 20 to 50 receiving single-tooth maxillary anterior and premolar implants
f.intervention: Titanium-supported PEEK abutments (group PEEK, n=20), both groups restored with pressed lithium disilicate crowns
f.comparison: Two-piece zirconia abutments (group ZIR, n=20)
outcomes: probing pocket depth, plaque control record, bleeding on probing
peri-implant mucosa color difference and crown discoloration
f.main_result: At 5 years both PEEK and zirconia abutments had 100% survival and statistically similar biologic, bone-level and esthetic outcomes.
f.sample_size: 40 participants (20 per group); 3 dropouts at 5 years
f.funding_coi: Supported by Government of Kerala (facilities) and King Khalid University research group grant; no COI statement in text.
f.limitations: Authors note long-term clinical trials are still needed to establish longevity.

f.population: 64 patients receiving 98 two-piece implants with fixed restorations
f.intervention: S1: OsseoSpeed TX (Astra Tech, Dentsply Sirona) implants with fixed restorations
f.comparison: S2: Straumann Bone Level SLActive implants
f.main_result: At 8 years patient-level survival was 97.6% (S1) vs 97.2% (S2); median marginal bone change was a 0.21 mm gain (S1) vs 0.24 mm loss (S2), clinically negligible.
f.sample_size: 98 implants in 64 patients; 49 patients re-examined at 8 years
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Clinic of Reconstructive Dentistry; some authors received research support and lecture fees from Straumann and Dentsply Sirona.
f.limitations: No sample size calculation (convenience sample) and wide inclusion criteria.

f.population: Edentulous patients with implant-supported full-arch prostheses, assessed through six systematic/narrative reviews
f.intervention: Fixed and removable implant-supported full-arch rehabilitations of the edentulous maxilla and mandible
f.comparison: Fixed versus removable prostheses
f.main_result: Edentulous patients are frequently affected by peri-implant disease; fixed and removable prostheses both reach high survival (93.3-100% and 96.9-100%) with no prosthetic material of choice, and technical complications are unavoidable.
f.limitations: Several areas lack data (esthetic outcomes, interarch space, opposing dentition, short implants in edentulous maxilla).

f.population: 16 articles (12 evaluated): 3 human, 3 animal and 6 in vitro studies on abutment soft tissue response
f.intervention: Abutment materials and surface topographies/macrodesign (laser-ablated, hydrophilic, oxidized titanium, zirconia)
f.main_result: Human histology showed perpendicular fibroblast insertion into laser-ablated, hydrophilic and oxidized titanium abutment surfaces; epithelial cells slightly favored zirconia and polished titanium.
f.sample_size: Preliminary pool of 206 articles, 12 evaluated plus 4 systematic reviews
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of designs, statistics and results precluded meta-analysis.

f.intervention: Design of subgingival (critical and subcritical) and supragingival contours of the implant restorative emergence profile
f.main_result: No convincing evidence on ideal emergence profile design; contours should mimic tooth/root shape but depend on implant position and phenotype, and a decision tree is proposed.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no direct financial interests
f.limitations: Authors note lack of convincing evidence and consensus on ideal emergence profile design

f.population: 100 consecutive systemically healthy partially edentulous patients with subcrestally placed implants
f.intervention: Xenograft grafting of the gap between bone crest and implant coronal aspect (Group A)
f.comparison: Subcrestal implants without grafting material (Group B)
f.main_result: Mean marginal hard-tissue loss was 0.11 mm in Group A and 0.08 mm in Group B with no significant difference between groups.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; some authors received lecture stipends from DENTSPLY Friadent

f.population: In vitro studies of implant-abutment connections
f.intervention: Different implant-abutment connection types tested for preload, deformation and microleakage
f.main_result: Conical connections gave fewer mechanical complications and higher torque preservation; all connections showed some microleakage.
f.sample_size: 19 in vitro studies and 1 systematic review
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Studies used varied approaches and are difficult to compare

f.population: Clinical trials, in vitro studies and reviews on implant-abutment connections
f.intervention: Different implant-abutment connection types and their bacterial leakage
f.main_result: All connections showed micro-gap and bacterial micro-leakage, though conical and mixed connections seemed to behave better.
f.follow_up: In vitro mean 10.5 days; in vivo about 3 years
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Differences in study protocols, unspecified bacteria, mixed in vivo and in vitro designs, heterogeneous follow-up

f.population: 54 implants in esthetically demanding sites of 41 patients
f.intervention: Experimental concave (gingivally converging) titanium and zirconia abutments
outcomes: vertical soft tissue level changes at the facial aspect
f.main_result: Vertical augmentation or no recession in 87% of situations and no recession greater than 0.5 mm; gingival level stable at 12-24 months; esthetic rating 4.5/5.
f.funding_coi: Implant components provided by Nobel Biocare AB

f.population: 10 healthy patients with two implants each at healed posterior sites
f.intervention: Concave circular macro-grooved titanium study abutments, immediately provisionalized
f.comparison: Conventional convex control abutments
f.main_result: Concave macro-grooved abutments did not give superior soft tissue development; control sites had higher PES values and marginal bone levels did not differ.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Tapered Groovy implants
Nobel Biocare Curvy Esthetic titanium abutment

f.population: 20 edentulous patients with two experimental abutments each in the interforaminal mandible
f.intervention: Experimental healing abutments of titanium, zirconia, feldspar-veneered zirconia and PEEK with 3 months open healing
f.comparison: Titanium abutments
f.main_result: The four abutment materials showed no significant differences in clinical, microbiological, cytokine or bone outcomes; feldspar-veneered zirconia had fewer mononuclear inflammatory cells than titanium.
f.funding_coi: Schilli Implantology Circle (SIC); Cendres+Métaux (C+M)
f.limitations: Short observation period and small sample size

f.population: 70 partially edentulous patients with one implant each in two groups by vertical mucosal thickness (thin vs thick)
f.intervention: Prosthetic abutments 1 mm (short) or 3 mm (long) randomly assigned
f.comparison: Long (3 mm) vs short (1 mm) abutments, in thin vs thick mucosa
f.main_result: Short abutments gave greater marginal bone loss (0.59-0.80 mm) than long abutments (0.28-0.37 mm) at 12 months, irrespective of mucosal thickness.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Vertical mucosal thickness measurement method could be questioned due to soft tissue deformability

f.main_result: Surgical trauma and periosteal elevation have not been shown to cause early implant bone loss; the pattern is more vertical than horizontal and surgical causes remain undetermined.

f.population: 30 ITI solid abutments on fixture analogs with cast base metal crowns (in vitro specimens)
f.intervention: Abutment surface roughening by sandblasting (50-µm aluminum oxide) or diamond bur, crowns cemented with TempBond
f.comparison: Untreated abutments (control)
f.main_result: Bur-treated abutments had the highest mean tensile strength (91.37±7.19 N) vs sandblasted 64.38±8 and control 58.61±1.93; sandblasted did not differ from control.
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Dental Research Center and Vice Chancellor for Research of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences

f.population: Patients with dental implants (12 randomized trials included)
f.intervention: Abutments made of materials other than titanium (alloys), mainly zirconia and alumina
f.comparison: Titanium (alloy) abutments
f.main_result: No difference in marginal bone level or probing depth between titanium and zirconia or alumina abutments at 1 or 5 years (zirconia MBL MD -0.24 mm, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.16).
f.funding_coi: France Lambert receives research grants, lecturing and/or consulting fees from Straumann Group, Nobel Biocare, ITI
f.limitations: Search limited to studies from January 2000, English only, and transmucosal components made of mixed materials excluded

f.population: 40 dental implants with internal Morse-taper connection (in vitro)
f.intervention: Dynamic loading in a chewing simulator (500 000 cycles of 50 N) while immersed in E. coli solution
f.comparison: Unloaded implants in the same bacterial solution
outcomes: E. coli colonization of fixture-abutment interface (implants colonized, CFU)
f.main_result: E. coli colonized the microgap in 1/20 unloaded vs 4/20 loaded implants (not significant by Fisher), with significantly higher CFU in the loaded group (mean 19.2 vs 3, P<.05).
materials_brands: Implant One fixtures with standard abutment (Custom Dental Implants)
f.funding_coi: Funded by Custom Dental Implants; authors declare no commercial relationships
f.limitations: Within the limits of the study; only minimal penetration to threaded part observed with a single bacterial species

f.population: 20 patients with 36 two-part implants with gingivally convergent (tapered) abutments, one specialist center
f.intervention: Implants restored with gingivally tapered/convergent abutment connection (Shelta XA)
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone change one year after loading was -0.18 ± 0.72 mm with bone level staying above the platform (+1.16 ± 0.91 mm) and 100% survival.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: 36 two-piece implants in the mandibles of six dogs
f.intervention: Placement at bone crest, 1.5 mm subcrestal or 3.0 mm subcrestal
f.comparison: Equicrestal placement (0 mm)
f.main_result: Both subcrestal groups lost significantly less crestal and marginal bone than equicrestal implants, and the 3-mm group had the most bone-to-abutment contact; BIC was about 60% in all groups.
f.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest

f.population: Literature on transmucosal components (abutments) and peri-implant tissues, mostly animal and some human studies
f.intervention: Abutment type, composition, design, mobility, repeated disconnection and platform switching
f.main_result: Severe lack of clinical information on the impact of implant type, connection and abutment composition on peri-implant bone remodelling; only one clinical study suggests one abutment-one time preserves bone.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; supported by University of Liège and CHU de Liège
f.limitations: Studies on platform switching are extremely heterogenous with controversial results

f.population: Six partially edentulous patients with Brånemark implants
f.intervention: Four titanium abutments with different surface roughness randomly placed
f.comparison: Abutments of differing roughness compared within each patient
outcomes: probing depth, recession, bleeding on probing
f.main_result: Smoothing below a roughness threshold had no major effect on microbiologic composition; spirochetes appeared only around the roughest abutments, which showed 0.2 mm attachment gain vs >0.8 mm loss for others.
f.funding_coi: Supported by the National Fund for Scientific Research (NFWO, Brussels)
f.limitations: Long-term clinical observations are needed

f.population: 167 posterior single-tooth implant restorations with CAD-CAM abutments (84 subcrestal, 83 equicrestal)
f.intervention: Profile angle measured from implant platform or adjacent bone crest in subcrestally placed implants
f.comparison: Equicrestally placed implants
f.sample_size: 167 implants (84 subcrestal in 76 patients, 83 equicrestal in 73 patients)
f.funding_coi: Yonsei-Dentium research grant; no competing interests declared

f.population: Literature on prosthetic factors and peri-implant disease
f.intervention: Prosthetic variables: implant position, abutment height, residual cement, splinting, occlusal forces
f.main_result: Implant spatial positioning, abutment height, residual cement and splinting are associated with peri-implant disease pathogenesis; occlusal forces mainly affect prosthetic complications.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Narrative review; too few randomized trials for a systematic review or meta-analysis

f.intervention: Hybrid abutment design: feather-edge on buccal side and chamfer finish line on lingual side
f.comparison: Traditional chamfer abutment design
f.main_result: Proposes a hybrid abutment combining buccal feather-edge and palatal chamfer; no published data yet, a 5-year retrospective analysis is underway.
f.limitations: Transfer of feather-edge results to implant abutments is not supported by published data

f.population: Six Labrador dogs with implants placed in the mandibular premolar region
f.intervention: Implants with abutments of titanium, zirconia or Au/Pt-alloy placed in randomized order, 5-month plaque control, histological analysis
f.comparison: Titanium abutments compared with zirconia and gold-platinum alloy abutments
f.main_result: Soft tissue dimensions at Ti and zirconia abutments stayed stable from 2 to 5 months, while Au/Pt-alloy abutments showed apical shift of barrier epithelium and marginal bone with less collagen and fibroblasts and more leukocytes.
f.sample_size: 6 dogs, 47 remaining implant sites (one implant lost)
f.follow_up: 5 months of healing (2 and 5 months assessed)

f.population: 20 patients with a single missing maxillary central (10) or lateral (10) incisor treated with bone-level implants
f.intervention: Soft tissue conditioning with a screw-retained implant provisional crown (dynamic compression technique), then digital volumetric analysis of the emergence profile
f.comparison: Initial profile of the standardized circular healing abutment
outcomes: linear mesial-distal and buccal-lingual profile change
number of appointments and treatment time
f.main_result: Supraimplant emergence profile extended by a mean 41.9 mm3 at central and 25.8 mm3 at lateral incisor sites, more than double the initial healing-abutment profile.
materials_brands: Straumann Bone Level implants (RC 4.1 mm, NC 3.3 mm)
f.funding_coi: Financial support from Institut Straumann AG; no conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: IOS accuracy for volumetric soft tissue measurement not tested exhaustively; histologic studies needed.

f.population: 407 patients with 1482 implants who attended the 10-year recall
f.intervention: Implant therapy with Osseospeed implants, followed 10 years; early bone loss thresholds as predictor
f.comparison: Implants with early bone loss above vs below thresholds of 0.5, 1 and 2 mm
f.main_result: Implants with early bone loss of 0.5 mm or more in year one had 5.43 times higher odds of peri-implantitis; 10-year implant survival was 94.74% and peri-implantitis 11.8% of implants.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: 31.5% dropout; maintenance compliance unclear

f.population: 20 different implant systems (13 conical, 6 flat, 1 gable-like connection), 5 implants each
f.intervention: Dynamic and static loading up to 200 N in a chewing simulator with high-speed X-ray recording of gap length and width
f.comparison: Conical versus flat implant-abutment connections
f.main_result: Eight implant systems with conical connections showed no measurable gaps at 200 N, while all flat connection systems showed measurable gaps under dynamic and static loading.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: In vitro design; clinical studies needed to state superiority of a connection type

f.main_result: About 1.5 to 2.0 mm of bone loss occurs around bone-level butt-joint implants with a contaminated interface, not seen around implants with no interface, and platform-switched connections show less bone resorption.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI Foundation; no conflicts of interest

f.population: 29 subjects with two non-adjacent implants in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Experimental curved abutment with circumferential groove plus temporary restoration
f.comparison: Conventional divergent titanium abutment (control), split-mouth randomization
outcomes: marginal mucosa level change at 6 weeks
f.main_result: Grooved and conventional abutments did not differ significantly in marginal recession or unseating force at 6 weeks, while angled abutments elicited labial recession.
f.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare provided implants and abutments free of charge

f.population: 26 subjects with two non-adjacent missing teeth in the esthetic zone (52 implants)
f.intervention: Curved (concave) titanium abutment with circumferential groove
f.comparison: Conventional divergent titanium abutment, randomized within each patient
outcomes: maximum bone level between implant and adjacent root
f.main_result: No significant difference in papilla fill between concave and conventional abutments (P = 0.25); papilla fill rose with maximum interproximal bone height.
f.funding_coi: Grant from Smile Care, Mumbai; Nobel Biocare provided implants and abutments free
f.limitations: Many radiographic measurements excluded because of overprojection or distortion

f.population: Hydroxyapatite powder (in vitro chemical model)
f.intervention: MDP functional monomer reacted with hydroxyapatite for 5 min to 24 h, analysed by 31P CP-MAS NMR and powder XRD
f.main_result: MDP leached Ca from HAp to form a MDP-calcium salt layered structure at short term, with CaHPO4·2H2O precipitating on it after longer reaction (up to 24 h).
f.funding_coi: Grant-in-Aid from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and Medical-Techno-Okayama funds

f.population: Adults with non-carious cervical lesions restored with composite resin (29 RCTs in meta-analysis)
f.intervention: Self-etch adhesive strategy
f.comparison: Etch-and-rinse adhesive strategy
f.main_result: Self-etch and etch-and-rinse showed similar postoperative sensitivity and retention (RR 1.04), but etch-and-rinse gave less marginal discoloration at 18 months to 2 years (RR 1.51) and 4 to 5 years (RR 1.81).
f.sample_size: 29 RCTs in the meta-analysis (42 included in the review)
f.limitations: Review did not differentiate self-etch with mild versus strong acid

f.main_result: Resin bond to silica-based ceramics is well documented (HF etching plus silane), whereas bonding to alumina and zirconia ceramics is less predictable and needs different methods such as airborne abrasion with phosphate-modified resin cement.
f.sample_size: 68 articles on silica-based, 8 on alumina, 3 on zirconia ceramics
f.limitations: Few in vitro studies on high-strength ceramics; clinical trials needed

f.main_result: Opinion paper recommending a 3-step full etch-and-rinse route and a 3-step selective enamel etch plus 2-step self-etch route as gold standards, and appraising universal adhesives and self-adhesive restoratives.

f.population: Edentulous patients (410 jaws, 371 patients) treated with bridges on osseointegrated titanium fixtures
f.intervention: Osseointegrated titanium fixtures supporting bone-anchored bridges in edentulous jaws
f.main_result: In the 5-9 year group, 81% of maxillary and 91% of mandibular fixtures remained stable; marginal bone loss was 1.5 mm in the first year, then 0.1 mm annually.
f.sample_size: 2768 fixtures in 410 edentulous jaws of 371 patients
f.follow_up: 1-15 years (10-15 years for the development group)

f.main_result: After 1.2 million wear cycles BruxZir showed barely detectable wear (1 ± 1 µm) versus 54 ± 22 µm for Ceramco 3.
f.funding_coi: Wear test sponsored by Glidewell Laboratories (manufacturer)

f.population: Four healthy non-smoking adults aged 45-74 with severely worn dentition
f.intervention: Digital CAD/CAM chairside full-mouth rehabilitation protocol
f.main_result: All four patients maintained the result at two years with almost 100% cumulative survival; one veneer chipped.

f.population: 30 patients with totally edentulous mandible at three Italian centers
f.intervention: Five inter-foraminal 6-mm-short implants with screw-retained full-arch prosthesis with distal cantilevers
f.comparison: Five 11-mm-long implants with the same prosthesis
f.main_result: No implant or prosthesis loss; MBLc at 3 years -0.10 mm (6 mm) vs 0.02 mm (11 mm), not significantly different
f.sample_size: 30 patients, 150 implants (28 patients, 140 implants at 3 years)
f.limitations: Non-standardized radiographs and short 3-year follow-up

f.population: 25 consecutively treated fully edentulous patients (both jaws)
f.intervention: Immediately loaded bimaxillary screw-retained metal-resin prostheses on two mandibular and three maxillary flapless-placed implants
f.main_result: No prosthesis or implant failed and no patient dropped out at 6 months; three complications in two patients, all treated
materials_brands: Syra and Syra SL implants (Sweden & Martina)
f.funding_coi: Self-financed, no financial support
f.limitations: Short follow-up and single operator

f.population: 10 edentulous patients (average age 68), 58 implants
f.intervention: Implant-supported hybrid full-arch restorations with CAD/CAM-milled titanium frameworks (seven) and composite or ceramic veneering
f.comparison: Cast chromium-cobalt frameworks (four designs); composite versus ceramic veneering
f.main_result: 100% implant success at 40 months; prosthetic complications (screw fracture/loosening, chipping, debonding) only in cast restorations, none in milled ones

f.population: One 55-year-old male with severely worn dentition
f.intervention: Full-mouth reconstruction with PFM crowns after seating condyles in centric relation to gain restorative space without changing VDO
f.main_result: Seating the condyles in centric relation gained 2.38 mm of anterior space without altering VDO
f.funding_coi: Author declares no financial interest in any product

f.population: 48 fully edentulous patients (24 maxillae, 24 mandibles) in 6 centres
f.intervention: Immediately loaded metal-resin screw-retained cross-arch prosthesis on three implants (fixed-on-3)
f.comparison: Same prosthesis on four implants (fixed-on-4)
f.main_result: Implant and prosthesis failures did not differ significantly; at 1 year Fo3 implants lost 0.22 mm bone vs 0.40 mm for Fo4 (P=0.006)
f.sample_size: 48 patients (24 per group), 72 implants in Fo3
materials_brands: Syra and Syra SL tapered implants (Sweden & Martina)
f.limitations: Preliminary 1-year results; longer follow-up needed

f.intervention: CAD/CAM titanium bar and acrylic hybrid denture at abutment level, delivered over six appointments
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare CT protocol / NobelClinician software

f.intervention: Straight and angled (17 or 30 degree) multi-unit abutment placement with closed-tray and open-tray abutment-level impressions
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Multi-unit Abutment (NobelReplace, Conical Connection, Branemark System)

f.population: Patients with implant-supported fixed complete-arch prostheses in 93 included studies (maxilla and mandible)
f.intervention: Fewer than five implants per arch supporting a complete-arch fixed prosthesis
f.comparison: Five or more implants per arch
f.main_result: No significant difference in implant or prosthesis survival between fewer than five and five or more implants per arch (p > 0.05), median follow-up 8 years

f.intervention: Clear thermoformed co-polyester comfort bite splint (hard, or hard with soft inner surface) made on stone models with an open construction bite
Thermoforming technique for dental appliances (splints, trays, mouthguards, retainers, templates) with Erkodent materials and the Occluform device

f.population: U-shaped polyurethane model simulating mandibular bone with two implants (3.75 mm)
f.intervention: Cantilevered frameworks in CoCr or PdAg loaded at 5, 10 or 15 mm of cantilever arm
f.comparison: CoCr versus PdAg alloy at the same cantilever distances
f.main_result: CoCr showed larger compression than PdAg at equal cantilever distances, and deformation increased with cantilever length (Pearson correlation).
f.sample_size: Six groups, two implants in one polyurethane model, eight strain gauges
f.funding_coi: FAPESP grants
f.limitations: Conclusions drawn under the limited conditions of this in vitro study

f.population: Six dogs with chronic ridge defects
f.intervention: Collagen matrix (CM) augmentation of chronic ridge defects
f.comparison: Autogenous subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) and sham-operated control
outcomes: soft tissue volume change at 28 and 84 days (optical scan of casts)
f.main_result: At 84 days CM gained 1.4 mm and SCTG 1.4 mm in volume per area versus a 0.3 mm loss in controls (p<0.001).
materials_brands: Prototype collagen matrix of porcine collagen (Geistlich)
f.funding_coi: Funded by Swiss CTI, Geistlich Pharma AG and University of Zurich; two authors are Geistlich employees
Workshop supported by an unrestricted grant from Geistlich AB; authors disclose Geistlich, Straumann, Nobelbiocare and others

f.population: 16 patients with bilateral Miller Class I/II gingival recessions
f.intervention: Acellular dermal matrix allograft (ADMA)
f.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG), split-mouth
f.main_result: At 5 years complete root coverage was 20.0% (ADMA) versus 13.3% (SCTG) with no significant difference; both showed significant relapse.
f.funding_coi: Supported by Dental Research Center of Tehran University of Medical Sciences; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Within the limitations of this study (not specified further)

f.population: 300 patients undergoing extraction of one maxillary tooth (anterior, premolar, molar strata)
f.intervention: Buccal infiltration of 0.6 mL 4% articaine
f.comparison: Buccal infiltration of 0.6 mL 2% lidocaine
f.main_result: Buccal infiltration achieved palatal anesthesia in 82.7% with articaine versus 1.3% with lidocaine (P<.001).
f.funding_coi: Financial support from Mashhad University of Medical Sciences (grant 961221)
Authors report no commercial, proprietary or financial interest

f.intervention: Modified impression post made on a PVS index of the provisional crown to transfer emergence profile
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 20 healthy patients (13 females, 7 males), mean age 27.7 years, with healthy gingiva and unrestored maxillary anterior teeth (240 sites)
f.intervention: Measurement on stone casts with digital calipers of gingival zenith position from the vertical bisected midline of each maxillary anterior tooth, and gingival zenith level of the lateral incisors relative to the line joining adjacent central and canine zeniths
outcomes: gingival zenith position (medial-lateral) per tooth group
gingival zenith level of lateral incisors (apical-coronal)
f.main_result: Central incisor zeniths lay a mean 1 mm distal to the midline, lateral incisors 0.4 mm, canines were centred (97.5%), and lateral incisor zeniths were about 1 mm coronal to the line joining adjacent central and canine zeniths.
materials_brands: Jeltrate irreversible hydrocolloid impression material (Dentsply Caulk)
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in companies whose materials are included

f.population: Lay public respondents to a web survey; 1934 from the United States and Canada analyzed (2185 valid responses from 45 countries)
f.intervention: Web page showing five pairs of digitally altered anterior-tooth images (flat incisal embrasures, midline diastema, whiter teeth, altered proportion, midline discrepancy) ranked by respondents
f.comparison: Within each pair, the altered image versus the unaltered one, rated on a five-point preference scale
outcomes: effect of age, gender, race and last dental visit on preference
f.main_result: Strongest preferences were against diastema and midline shift and weakest for whiteness and proportion; females had stronger preferences, as did those under 40 for whiteness and against diastema.
f.sample_size: 2185 valid respondents; 1934 from the US and Canada analyzed

f.population: Illustrative clinical case of a patient treated with ceramic veneers using the DSD protocol (no formal sample)
f.intervention: Digital Smile Design protocol: reference lines and shapes drawn over extra- and intraoral photographs in presentation software, transferred to cast, diagnostic wax-up, mock-up/provisional, then minimally invasive veneer preparation
f.main_result: The authors describe DSD as a multi-use tool improving the team's understanding of esthetic issues and patient acceptance; no quantitative results reported.

f.population: Dentists contacted by e-mail; 549 valid responses from 38 countries, 470 from the US or Canada
f.intervention: Web page with computer-manipulated images of the 6 maxillary anterior teeth at 5 tooth heights, each in 4 proportions (62% golden, 70%, 80%, normal), ranked best to worst
f.comparison: Four proportions compared within each tooth-height group (golden proportion vs 70% vs 80% vs normal)
outcomes: best and worst ranking of proportion per height group
association with gender, experience, specialty, patient load
f.main_result: Dentists preferred the 80% proportion for short and very short teeth and the golden proportion for very tall teeth; golden proportion was worst for normal or shorter teeth.

f.population: Orthodontic casts of 58 second-year dental students (University of Southern California)
f.intervention: Measurement of apparent tooth widths on video-captured cast images (58) and direct caliper measurement of casts (52) to test golden proportion ratios between maxillary and mandibular incisors and canines
f.main_result: Golden proportion (1.59-1.65:1) was found in the perceived maxillary central:lateral incisor ratio in only 10 of 58 images (17%) and in no lateral incisor:canine ratio.
materials_brands: Dental Dial Caliper (Masel Industries) with modified tips
f.limitations: Sample size was limited (author's statement)

f.population: Typical patients (adults and children) with infections commonly seen in general practice
f.intervention: Consensus first-choice and alternative antibiotic regimens, with doses and durations, per infection (dental section covers dental abscess and endocarditis prophylaxis)
f.main_result: Consensus guide recommending prescribing antibiotics only for significant or high-risk bacterial infections, using first-line narrow agents at recommended dose and duration.
f.limitations: Individual patient circumstances and local resistance patterns may alter treatment choices.

f.population: Oral cavity bacterial infections (dental caries, gingivitis, periodontitis, dental abscess) and their causative organisms; no study sample
f.main_result: Oral bacterial infections are caused by many species; diagnosis is usually clinical but microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility testing should guide antimicrobial choice to limit resistance.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare nothing to disclose

f.population: 263 patients (aged 10-79) treated at a cranio-maxillofacial department and outpatient clinic, 2013-2014; 485 cultured bacterial and fungal strains, mainly from submandibular and submental abscess pus
f.intervention: Microbial culture and antibiogram analysis with a cost-minimisation model combining antibiotic efficacy, price and hospital cost per patient-day
f.comparison: Sensitivity of Gram-positive vs Gram-negative bacteria and of antibiotics against each other (nine antimicrobial agents)
f.main_result: Most common pathogens were S. epidermidis (18%), Str. mitis/oralis (14%) and S. aureus (6.5%); gentamycin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and vancomycin were cheapest per effective therapy.

f.population: 54 patients with histologically and clinically proven chronic osteomyelitis of the mandible or maxilla from three maxillofacial departments in Israel (14 implant-induced)
f.intervention: Primary treatment of debridement and antibiotic therapy; failures treated with mandibulectomy or maxillectomy
f.comparison: Implant-induced osteomyelitis versus other etiologic groups (extraction, fracture, cyst, infected teeth)
f.main_result: 40 patients remitted with primary treatment and 14 failed; a previous dental implant was an independent predictor of failure (P = .0001).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 38 healthy individuals receiving platform-switched implants (37 completed)
f.intervention: Preoperative 2 g amoxicillin plus 7 days postoperative amoxicillin 500 mg tid
f.comparison: Same preoperative amoxicillin dose followed by an identical postoperative placebo
outcomes: peri-implant crestal bone change at 1 year
f.main_result: One-year crestal bone change was -0.44 ± 0.41 mm (antibiotic) vs -0.27 ± 0.56 mm (placebo), not significantly different; morbidity did not differ and survival was 100% in both groups.
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed TX or Astra EV implants (Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Supported by an Université de Montréal faculty research fund; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small sample precludes generalization and an accurate implant survival rate; chlorhexidine rinse use was not logged.

f.population: 236 medically and periodontally healthy patients receiving oral implants with simultaneous GBR at seven centres
f.intervention: Systemic amoxicillin: 2 g one hour before surgery, then 500 mg three times daily on days 1-3
f.comparison: Placebo
outcomes: PROMs (VAS pain, swelling, haematoma, bleeding, days 1-7 and 14)
f.main_result: No statistically significant difference between antibiotic and placebo groups for PROMs or post-surgical complications (p > .05); 4 implants lost (3 test, 1 control).
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation research grant; Geistlich, Medochemie and Straumann supplied materials/medication; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Larger sample sizes are still required to support the clinical outcomes.

f.population: Dental implant patients with a self-reported penicillin allergy
f.intervention: Peri-operative penicillin (amoxicillin)
f.comparison: Peri-operative clindamycin
f.main_result: Patients given clindamycin because of self-reported penicillin allergy had over three times the odds of implant failure (OR 3.30, 95% CI 2.58-4.22).
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Evidence is limited and based on retrospective observational studies.

f.population: 8 beagle dogs, 64 implants in mandibular premolar regions
f.intervention: Plateau root form (PRF, Bicon) titanium implants
f.comparison: Screw root form (SRF, Straumann) implants
f.main_result: BIC and BAFO tended to be greater for SRF but not significantly (P=0.07, P=0.06); both increased significantly with time and progressed in parallel.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus Narrow Neck SLA implants
f.limitations: BIC and BAFO reflect structural connection, not the functional properties of the bone-implant interface.

f.population: 108 patients with 228 implants (posterior maxilla restorations)
f.intervention: OsseoSpeed implants with internal conical connection and LILAC uni-abutments of different heights, giving different mismatching distances
f.comparison: 4.5 mm vs 5 mm diameter implants (different mismatching distances); short vs long abutments
outcomes: marginal bone loss at 6 and 18 months post-loading
f.main_result: Greater mismatching did not reduce MBL; MBL was greater with short abutments, grafted bone, heavier smoking and 5.0 mm implants.
f.funding_coi: Research groups grant (Junta de Andalucia); authors declare no financial interest in listed products
f.limitations: Results should be interpreted with caution and validated in wider randomized clinical trials.

f.population: 219 patients with 270 single-tooth Branemark implants (215 upper jaw)
f.intervention: Single-implant restorations on Branemark System implants
f.main_result: Cumulative success 93% for implants and 96.5% for restorations over 11 years; bone loss 0.71 mm in first 6 months then 0.036 mm/year.

f.population: Ten female Göttingen minipigs (nine analysed), healed mandibular ridges
f.intervention: Fully tapered BLX implants placed at inter-implant thread-peak distances of 1, 2, 3 mm and at 3 distances from outer buccal bone
f.comparison: Different thread-peak distances compared with each other
f.main_result: Inter-implant bone height was maintained even at 1 mm thread-peak distance; buccal bone resorption was significant when thread-peak to outer buccal bone distance was < 0.5 mm.
materials_brands: Straumann BLX Roxolid SLActive 4.5 x 8 mm
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Straumann Group; authors received no payment

f.population: Partially edentulous patients with bone-level implants, University of Michigan clinics
f.intervention: Groups by transmucosal abutment height (>2 mm vs <2 mm) and restorative emergence angle (<30 vs >=30 degrees)
f.comparison: Long/Narrow, Long/Wide, Short/Narrow and Short/Wide groups compared
f.main_result: Short abutment with wide emergence angle (SW) had 0.25-0.48 mm greater MBL than other groups and about 4 times the likelihood of peri-implantitis.
f.follow_up: at least one year after T0 (T0 at 12-18 months after crown placement)
f.funding_coi: No specific funding

f.population: 5 beagle dogs, 6 Branemark implants each in the mandible
f.intervention: Abutment connection after surgically thinning the ridge mucosa (test side)
f.comparison: Contralateral control side with standard abutment connection
f.main_result: Where ridge mucosa was thin (<=2 mm), wound healing consistently included bone resorption and an angular bone defect.

f.population: 5 minipigs, 4 implants each placed flapless in the mandible
f.intervention: Platform-switched implants (0.25 mm mismatch) placed flush, 1 mm below or 1 mm above the bone crest
f.comparison: Conventionally restored implant at bone level
f.main_result: Platform switching resulted in less crestal resorption (0.58 mm less); effect on biologic width limited to a shorter epithelial attachment when placed at crest level.

Narrative conclusion: CAD/CAM zirconia-based restorations give better marginal fit, less inflammation and better periodontal health and hygiene than conventional constructions, and supragingival margins are better than subgingival ones.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared

outcomes: evidence on gingival retraction techniques for implant versus tooth impressions
f.main_result: The authors found insufficient evidence on gingival displacement techniques for impression making in implant dentistry; retraction methods are designed for natural teeth and further research and product development are needed.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures reported
f.limitations: No rigorous selection protocol was applied; all references were accepted because the literature on implants was scarce.

f.population: Eight adult beagle dogs; implants placed in healed mandibular sites
f.intervention: Tissue-level implant with a convergent transmucosal neck (Prama-type design)
f.comparison: Conventional bone-level implant with cylindrical machined titanium abutment
