f.main_result: At 4 and 12 weeks there were no statistically significant differences between test and control implants in peri-implant hard and soft tissue height and thickness; test implants tended to have a more coronal free gingival margin and first bone contact.
f.sample_size: 16 test and 16 control implants in 8 dogs
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by a research contract with Sweden & Martina Dental Implants
f.limitations: Animal model with a reduced sample size, so the null hypothesis could not be rejected.

f.population: Nine dogs; mandibular premolar sockets
f.intervention: Immediate one-piece zirconia implant with xenograft (Bio-Oss Collagen) grafted in the buccal gap
f.comparison: Same implant without gap grafting (spontaneous healing)
f.main_result: Xenograft in the buccal gap gave a more coronal marginal mucosa and longer buccal barrier epithelium (shorter connective tissue contact) than control, with no significant difference in total supracrestal soft tissue height; less recession.
materials_brands: Straumann Pure Ceramic one-piece zirconia implant (narrow, 3.3 mm)
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grant 1215_2017

f.population: Partially or completely edentulous patients (and canine preclinical models)
f.intervention: Implants placed in healed ridges with thin or absent buccal bone wall
f.comparison: Thick or present buccal bone wall; augmented buccal wall
f.main_result: Sites with a thin buccal bone wall are more prone to major dimensional changes, vertical bone loss and mucosal recession, with biologic and esthetic complications; simultaneous augmentation of dehiscence-type defects favours stability.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no direct financial interests
f.limitations: Heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis; conclusions rest mainly on preclinical and nonrandomized studies.

f.population: Healthy patients receiving at least one dental implant
f.intervention: Direct measurement of soft tissue thickness at implant placement
f.comparison: Thin (<2 mm) versus thick (>=2 mm) peri-implant soft tissue
outcomes: radiographic marginal bone loss at 12 months or more
f.main_result: Implants with thick soft tissue had less marginal bone loss: WMD -0.80 mm (95% CI -1.18 to -0.42), P<0.0001.
f.sample_size: 8 articles in the review, 5 in the meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by a University of Michigan graduate research fund; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity among studies in all comparisons.

f.population: 42 patients (27 partially edentulous maxilla, 15 edentulous mandible)
f.intervention: Non-submerged one-piece implants placed with the rough-smooth border at varying positions relative to the alveolar crest
f.comparison: Rough-smooth border placed below versus at or near the crest
outcomes: radiographic bone remodeling from implant shoulder to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: Mean bone remodeling was 1.10 mm by 6 months and virtually stable afterwards; it was greater when the rough-smooth border was below the crest (1.72 mm) than at or near it (0.68 mm).
materials_brands: Straumann titanium plasma-sprayed hollow-cylinder and solid-screw implants

f.population: 39 patients with 80 implants restored with single crowns or FDPs
f.intervention: Implant-supported single crowns or FDPs re-examined for interproximal contact loss
f.comparison: Implant sites without ICL
outcomes: plaque control record, BOP, probing depth
f.main_result: Interproximal contact loss occurred in 50% of implants after at least 10 years, mesial contacts more than distal, and was linked to +0.46 mm probing depth.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the University of Zurich clinic

f.population: 51 patients with a single delayed posterior maxillary implant
f.intervention: Platform-switched implants (Shape1, I-RES)
f.comparison: Conventional non-platform-switched implants (Screw Vent Tapered, Zimmer)
outcomes: mesial and distal marginal bone loss at 12 months
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss fell with greater abutment height and was nil at about 2.5 mm (platform-switched) versus 3.0 mm (conventional); control loss was over twice that of the test group.

f.intervention: Esthetic biological contour (EBC) concept: E, B and C zones of the implant emergence profile
f.main_result: The EBC concept divides the emergence profile into esthetic (E), bounded (B) and crestal (C) zones, each with a specific design recommendation.

f.population: 64 patients with edentulous posterior mandible/maxilla sites receiving bone level implants placed 1.5 mm subcrestally
f.intervention: Immediate tissue level (ITL) abutment torqued to the implant at surgery (no abutment disconnection)
f.comparison: Regular healing abutment at implant level with repeated abutment disconnections
outcomes: crestal bone loss at 1 month after prosthesis (T2) and at 1 year (T3)
f.main_result: Early bone loss was 0.14 mm (ITL) vs 0.64 mm (control), a significant 0.5 mm difference; at 1 year the difference was no longer significant (p = .22).
materials_brands: CONNECT immediate tissue level abutment (MIS Implant Technologies)
f.funding_coi: Funded by a grant from MIS Implant Technologies; first author reports study grant and lecture honoraria from MIS
f.limitations: Standardized periapical radiographs were not obtained.

f.population: Published literature on twelve dental implant types (subperiosteal, blade-vent, Brånemark screw, etc.)
f.intervention: Proposed criteria of implant success applied to assess long-term efficacy of each implant type
outcomes: long-term implant success rates by implant type
f.main_result: Review proposes stricter success criteria than the 1979 NIH minimal criteria; the Brånemark osseointegrated screw met the yardstick while e.g. subperiosteal implants showed 54% success at 15 years.

f.population: 50 patients with 119 implants (internal conical connection) supporting screw-retained fixed partial dentures
f.intervention: Implant-level (IL) connection of the screw-retained FPD
f.comparison: Abutment-level (AL) connection with multi-unit abutments
f.main_result: MBL change did not differ between groups at 1, 2 or 3 years (3 years: 0.18 mm AL vs 0.15 mm IL).
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech Implant System, Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Dentsply Sirona Implants; first author receives a personal fee from Dentsply Sirona

f.population: Premolar extraction sites (P1, P2) in five beagle dogs
f.intervention: Flapless extraction with or without socket preservation (BioOss Collagen plus free soft-tissue graft) versus flap elevation
f.comparison: Extraction without treatment (Tx 1) and with flap elevation/repositioning (Tx 2)
outcomes: volumetric tissue change on scanned casts at 2 and 4 months
f.main_result: Flapless groups showed significantly lower resorption than flap groups, and socket-preservation sites did better than untreated sockets.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 54 included publications: 2 clinical papers, 8 human histology and 44 animal studies
f.intervention: Systematic review of biologic width structure and function around implants
f.main_result: Knowledge of biologic width around implants derives mainly from animal studies; controlled clinical human studies are insufficient.
f.limitations: Evidence is mainly animal-based with insufficient controlled human studies.

f.population: 103 partially edentulous patients, one internal hex implant each in posterior mandible, grouped by gingival thickness
f.intervention: Thickening of thin mucosa with allogenic membrane before two-stage implant placement (group B)
f.comparison: Thin tissues without thickening (A) and naturally thick tissues (C)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: At 1 year bone loss was 1.65/1.81 mm (thin), 0.31/0.34 mm (thin thickened) and 0.44/0.47 mm (thick) mesial/distal; thickening matched thick tissues.

f.population: 4 patients with thin mucosa (2 mm or less) receiving 12 two-piece implants
f.intervention: Platform-switching implants (Prevail, 3i Biomet)
f.comparison: Horizontally matching implant-abutment connection (Prodigy, BioHorizons)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: With thin mucosa, bone loss was about 1.7-1.8 mm for platform-switching implants versus 1.6-1.76 mm for controls, with no significant difference.
f.limitations: Pilot study with small sample, stated within the limitations of this pilot study.

f.population: 26 patients with 64 implants, placed in thin, medium or thick mucosa
f.intervention: Test implants placed about 2 mm supracrestally
f.comparison: Control implants placed at bone crest level
outcomes: crestal bone loss at 1 year by mucosal thickness group
f.main_result: Around supracrestal test implants bone loss was 1.35 mm in thin, 0.32 mm in medium and 0.12 mm in thick mucosa; control implants lost 1.55-1.8 mm regardless of thickness.

f.population: 97 patients with one bone-level implant each in posterior mandible, grouped by mucosal thickness
f.intervention: Thickening of thin mucosa with allogenic membrane during one-stage implant placement (T2)
f.comparison: Thin mucosa without thickening (T1) and naturally thick mucosa (C)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 2 months and 1 year
f.main_result: At 1 year bone loss was 1.22/1.14 mm (thin), 0.24/0.19 mm (thickened) and 0.22/0.20 mm (thick); thickened tissue matched thick tissue.

f.population: 19 partially edentulous patients with 46 implants (23 test, 23 control)
f.intervention: Test implants placed about 2 mm supracrestally, grouped by thin (A) or thick (B) mucosa
f.comparison: Control implants placed at bone level
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: Bone loss around test implants was 1.61/1.28 mm in thin mucosa versus 0.26/0.09 mm in thick mucosa (mesial/distal); controls lost about 1.8 mm.

f.population: 24 minipigs, 96 lateral augmentation sites on the mandible
f.intervention: Lateral GBR with DBBM:particulate autogenous bone ratios 50:50, 75:25, 100:0, or autogenous bone block covered with DBBM, under a collagen membrane
f.comparison: The different graft ratios and the autogenous bone block against each other, at 10, 20 and 30 weeks
f.main_result: After 30 weeks height reduction was about 1.7-1.8 mm (33-38%) for particulate grafts versus 0.2 mm (3.7%) for block graft; volume reduction did not differ at 30 weeks.
f.funding_coi: Grants from Danish Dentist Association, Region Northern Jutland and a foundation; Bio-Oss and Bio-Gide partly sponsored by Geistlich, pins by Dentsply Sirona

f.main_result: Periodontal regeneration evolved from barrier-membrane GTR to papilla-preservation and minimally invasive flaps with biologics, with combined intrabony and soft-tissue approaches.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interests

f.population: 12 systemically healthy patients with Miller class I and II gingival recessions
f.intervention: Porcine collagen matrix placed under a partial thickness flap
f.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Root coverage was 24.7 percent with connective graft and 16.6 percent with matrix; keratinized tissue gain was similar (4.33 vs 4.5 mm).
Four graft classes (autologous, allogeneic, xenogenic, alloplastic) all show bone regeneration; autogenous bone remains the gold standard.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

f.main_result: No current therapy regenerates the pulp-dentin complex in pulp necrosis; advanced scaffolds, antibiotic-eluting nanofibers and 3D-printed membranes are emerging strategies.
f.funding_coi: NIH/NIDCR grants

f.population: Patients treated with two-stage maxillary sinus augmentation via lateral approach (34 RCTs, 842 sinus augmentations)
f.intervention: Grafting biomaterials for sinus augmentation (xenografts, allografts, synthetic grafts, composites with autologous bone, PRP, BMC)
f.comparison: Autologous bone alone and other biomaterials, ranked by network meta-analysis
f.main_result: Bovine xenograft + bone marrow concentrate ranked highest for new bone (81%); autologous bone alone ranked twelfth (57%), so it was not confirmed as gold standard.
f.funding_coi: Grants (EFOP, GINOP); funders had no role; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 4 mongrel dogs; mandibular premolar extraction sites
f.intervention: Buccal pouch grafting with xenograft, FDBA, or FDBA + DFDBA
f.comparison: Untreated control pouch
f.main_result: Xenograft sites gained ridge width from T1 to T3 while control and FDBA sites lost width, and grafted sites kept soft tissue thickness.
f.funding_coi: University funds; no conflicts of interest

f.main_result: Bovine xenografts and synthetics dominate the cranio-maxillofacial graft market; autografts remain gold standard but no graft has all ideal properties.
f.funding_coi: EU Horizon2020 Eurostars project and Research Council of Norway

f.main_result: Calcium phosphate degradation in vivo occurs through phagocytic cell activity and acidic dissolution with osteoclast resorption, influenced by composition and ion substitution.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.main_result: No marketed bone substitute has all ideal properties; autografts and allografts have donor-site and immune/disease limitations, driving research into synthetic and tissue-engineered substitutes.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.intervention: Geistlich Mucograft collagen matrix for recession coverage

f.funding_coi: Alpha Omega Foundation of Canada, AAID Foundation and NSERC grants; no competing interests

f.comparison: AlloDerm RTM versus Puros Dermis, Mucograft and Perioderm by number of published articles

f.population: Tnfsf11fl/fl;Dmp1-Cre mice lacking osteocyte-specific RANKL and Dmp1-Cre control mice
f.intervention: Calvarial bone disks transplanted subcutaneously or subperiosteally
outcomes: graft resorption and new bone formation
residual graft area, volume and thickness (micro-CT)
f.main_result: Control subcutaneous grafts resorbed, whereas grafts lacking osteocyte RANKL showed neither resorption nor formation; residual graft area differed between sites only in controls (p<.01 vs p=.17).
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation and ITI Foundation grants; no conflicts of interest
NIDCR (NIH) and Medical Research Foundation of Oregon grants

f.population: Human studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants and in partially edentulous areas
f.intervention: Apically positioned flap/vestibuloplasty with FGG, SCTG or collagen matrix; SCTG for volume
f.comparison: APF/V alone or no treatment; non-grafted sites
outcomes: papilla fill and marginal mucosal level
f.main_result: APF/V plus FGG/SCTG was the best-documented method to increase keratinized mucosa; collagen matrix gave less gain but less morbidity and surgery time.

f.population: Human liposuction adipose tissue, human adipose-derived stem cells and subcutaneous injection in an in vivo model
f.intervention: Injectable acellular adipose matrix prepared by mechanical delipidation, Tris-HCl/SDS decellularization and homogenization
f.main_result: Mechanical disruption sped delipidation; the matrix showed no cytotoxicity, supported hADSC migration and proliferation, and degraded gradually in vivo with peripheral adipogenesis at 8 weeks.
f.funding_coi: Vietnam National University HCMC grant C2019-18-20; no competing interests

f.population: Six patients with 17 mandibular Class II buccal molar furcation invasions

f.intervention: Cementation using preheated restorative composite resin
f.comparison: Cementation using resin cement

f.main_result: Production-center machines offer a wider range of materials and restoration shapes than labside machines, which offer more than chairside; more complex solutions need more skilled users and cost more

f.comparison: Implants of FDPs adjacent to versus distant from the cantilever extension

f.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses (ICFDPs)
f.main_result: Estimated 5-year implant survival 98.9% and ICFDP survival 97.1%; biological complications 5.7% at implant level; veneer fracture was the commonest technical complication

f.population: Silver-palladium complete metal crowns on metal dies of a prepared dentoform premolar with three finish lines
f.intervention: Cementation with zinc phosphate or glass-ionomer at seating forces of 25, 100 and 300 N on chamfer, shoulder or beveled-shoulder margins

f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq grant; authors reported no conflicts of interest

f.main_result: Successful ceramic restorations depend on material selection, manufacturing technique and restoration design
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: Five patients aged 32-53 years with hyperplastic tissue response after connective tissue grafting

f.main_result: Follow-up of 1-5 years showed stable results with no relapse or recurrence of tissue overgrowth.

f.funding_coi: Financial support from the KOF/Calcin Foundation of the Danish Dental Association; no conflict of interest

f.funding_coi: Sponsored by Dentsply; no conflicts of interest reported

f.funding_coi: Korea Medical Device Development Fund grant (Korean government ministries)

Escherichia coli ATCC 35218 in BHI broth

f.intervention: Disinfection and sterilization of patient-care items by Spaulding risk category
Special infection-control precautions in dental care during the COVID-19 outbreak (screening, hand hygiene, PPE, pre-procedural rinse, rubber dam, air filtration, surface disinfection)

f.main_result: Thermal fogging combined with cleaning and surface disinfection is reported to outperform surface decontamination alone, per cited studies.

materials_brands: 1,100 W wet-dry-blow household vacuum cleaner modified as EOVA

f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest declared

outcomes: error rate in cleaning and disinfection

f.population: Reusable elastomeric half and full facepiece respirators (3M 6000, 6500, 7500 and FF-400 series) after potential coronavirus exposure
f.intervention: Cleaning with warm water and detergent, then disinfection (sodium hypochlorite 5,000 ppm or 70% isopropanol, or EPA-registered quat disinfectant)

f.population: Klebsiella pneumoniae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, influenza A (H1N1) and rotavirus in suspension tests
f.intervention: 7% PVP-I gargle/mouthwash diluted 1:30 (0.23% PVP-I), contact time from 15 s
f.comparison: Untreated control with distilled water in place of product
f.main_result: At 0.23% PVP-I all viral titres fell by 4.40 to 6.00 log10 TCID50/ml within 15 s, and bacteria by more than 5 log10.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Mundipharma Research; one author is an MRG employee

f.population: COVID-19 patients and the healthcare workers attending them (proposed protocol)
f.intervention: Protocolised intra-nasal and oral application of povidone-iodine
f.main_result: The authors recommend considering immediate PVP-I use in healthcare workers and patients as an adjunct to PPE, based on in vitro virucidal evidence.
f.limitations: The proposal extrapolates in vitro findings to the in vivo setting.

f.population: MSSA and MRSA suspensions dried on blood agar, filter paper or glass in a 33.1 m3 hospital side-room
f.intervention: Gaseous ozone from a domestic generator (Biosan 2000) for 4 and 7 h
f.comparison: Inoculated specimens in a neighbouring side-room without ozone
f.main_result: Counts fell near the generator in most cases but the effect across the room was limited, and MRSA was more resistant than MSSA.
f.sample_size: Model A 10 groups of colonies per condition; model B 5; model C 3
f.funding_coi: Equipment loaned by Enright Industries; no funding statement

f.population: Participants of the BNT162b2 phase 3 trial discussed (21,720 vaccine, 21,728 placebo)
f.intervention: BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine, two injections 21 days apart
f.comparison: Placebo
f.main_result: In the trial's primary analysis 8 Covid-19 cases occurred in the vaccine group versus 162 in the placebo group, an efficacy of 95%.
f.limitations: The number of severe cases is too small to draw conclusions about severity in vaccinated persons.

f.population: Persons 16 years of age or older, healthy or with stable chronic conditions
f.intervention: Two 30-μg doses of BNT162b2, 21 days apart
f.comparison: Saline placebo
f.main_result: BNT162b2 gave 95% efficacy against Covid-19 (8 cases versus 162 on placebo), with short-term mild-to-moderate reactions and a low serious adverse event rate.
f.funding_coi: Funded by BioNTech and Pfizer

f.population: Hospitalised COVID-19 patients (mild/moderate and severe), SARS-CoV-2-negative ALI/ARDS patients and healthy controls
f.intervention: Whole-blood single-cell immune profiling and serum functional assays
f.main_result: Mild COVID-19 patients show coordinated interferon-stimulated gene expression across cell types that is absent in severe disease, which instead shows very high antibody titres blocking these cells.
f.limitations: Patients were enrolled early in the pandemic, depended on self-reporting to hospital, and came from the greater Bay Area.

f.population: Periodontally healthy patients with thick gingival biotype and intact buccal bone wall, single failing tooth in aesthetic zone (15-25)
f.intervention: Single immediate implant with flapless surgery, DBBM socket grafting and immediate provisional crown
f.comparison: Outcomes at 5 years compared with 10 years
f.main_result: Mean outcomes were stable between 5 and 10 years, but six implants (33%) showed 1 mm or more mid-facial recession.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; Nobel Biocare Belgium supplied free materials; one author has collaboration agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann

f.population: 47 patients with a single implant in the anterior region
f.intervention: Implant provisional and crown with a convex emergence profile
f.comparison: Concave-profile provisional and crown, and a control with no provisional
f.main_result: Recession frequency was 64.3% (convex), 14.3% (concave) and 31.4% (control); a convex profile had an odds ratio of 12.6 for recession versus concave.
f.sample_size: 47 patients with 47 implants; 44 available at 12 months
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech, Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Funded by the University of Zurich clinic, SSRD and Dentsply Sirona Implants; no conflict declared

f.population: 25 single maxillary anterior implant sites (patients aged 23-38, thick biotype)
f.intervention: Two-stage adaptive pressure contouring with a screw-retained interim restoration
f.comparison: Gingiva of the adjacent natural tooth as colour reference
outcomes: gingival colour change (L*a*b*, delta E) over 15 minutes
f.main_result: Peri-implant mucosa blanching recovered within 10 minutes, with colour difference from the adjacent tooth within the acceptable 3.7 limit.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 169 patients with 349 implants treated at Seoul National University Dental Hospital 2002-2012
f.intervention: Radiographic assessment of prosthetic features (emergence angle, emergence profile, crown/implant ratio, splinted position) at 1 and 5 years after prosthesis insertion
f.comparison: Emergence angle <30 vs >=30 degrees; concave/straight/convex profile; single vs splinted positions
f.main_result: Peri-implantitis prevalence was higher with emergence angle >=30 degrees, convex profile and implants splinted to both neighbours in bone-level implants; crown/implant ratio had no effect.
f.funding_coi: Seoul National University Dental Hospital Research Fund; no conflict of interest declared

f.intervention: Abutment and crown contour modifications in critical and subcritical zones of implant restorations
f.main_result: Alteration of critical or subcritical contour can modify the peri-implant soft tissue profile; only subcritical contour changes enhance soft tissue without altering crown shape.
f.limitations: The authors state the findings are preliminary observations and the exact critical-contour dimension is yet to be determined.

f.population: Randomly selected Swedish patients provided with implant-supported restorative therapy in 2003 (2,765 patient files; 596 examined clinically)
f.intervention: Implant-supported restorative therapy provided in routine care by over 800 clinicians; early and late implant loss assessed
outcomes: patient and implant factors associated with loss
f.main_result: Early implant loss occurred in 4.4% of patients (1.4% of implants) and late loss in 4.2% of examined patients (2.0% of implants); 7.6% of examined patients lost at least 1 implant.
f.sample_size: 2,765 patients (11,311 implants) from files; 596 patients (2,367 implants) examined
f.funding_coi: Swedish Social Insurance Agency, Swedish Research Council, TUA research Gothenburg and Swedish Dental Society; some authors report fees from Dentsply Implants IH

f.population: 15 3D-printed mandibular models with missing first molar and single implant analog, cleaned by 30 volunteers (periodontists, hygienists, laypersons)
f.intervention: Cleaning of artificial biofilm from implant crowns with five interdental cleaning aids
f.comparison: Concave (15 degrees), straight (30 degrees) and convex (45 degrees) crown contours; different cleaning tools
f.main_result: Concave crowns had the greatest artificial biofilm removal; dental floss (43.0%) and superfloss (42.5%) were the most effective tools and none removed all biofilm.
f.funding_coi: Rackham Graduate Student Research Grant; no financial interests in the tested products
f.limitations: Only three crown contours were tested in vitro with artificial biofilm, so results cannot be generalized to real clinical scenarios.

f.population: Three clinical cases of patients with overcontoured implant crowns and peri-implantitis or high risk of it
f.intervention: Reduction and recontouring of overcontoured implant crowns, with digital design of abutments and crowns, for plaque-control access
f.main_result: Overcontoured implant crowns restrict hygiene access and favor biofilm accumulation, leading to peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis; recontouring resolved inflammation in the presented cases.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: The authors note there was no randomized clinical trial on restorative design and contour, and call for future studies.

f.population: Digest of a cross-sectional study: 83 patients with 168 implants (101 bone-level, 67 tissue-level)
f.intervention: Radiographic measurement of restoration emergence angle and profile in relation to peri-implantitis
f.comparison: Emergence angle >30 vs <=30 degrees; convex vs straight/concave profile; bone-level vs tissue-level implants
f.main_result: Peri-implantitis was significantly greater with emergence angle >30 degrees in bone-level implants, and a convex profile plus wide angle gave the highest rate (37.8%).
f.limitations: Few tissue-level patients (only two with peri-implantitis), implant status rather than bone loss as outcome, and facial/lingual contours not visible radiographically.

f.population: Implant-supported single crowns in clinical studies with mean follow-up of at least 5 years (46 studies)
f.intervention: Implant-supported single crowns
f.comparison: Conventional and cantilever FDPs (discussion comparison from prior reviews)
f.main_result: Implant survival was 97.2% at 5 years and 95.2% at 10 years; single-crown survival was 96.3% at 5 years and 89.4% at 10 years.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

f.intervention: Effect of implant depth, interproximal position, bodily position and axial inclination on emergence profile design
f.main_result: The abutment emergence profile design depends on 3D implant position and on hard and soft tissue conditions; adequate position and soft tissue volume increase esthetic success.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.intervention: Digital workflow (intraoral scan, CBCT, STL superimposition in Meshmixer) to design and 3D-print a single surgical guide for crown lengthening
f.comparison: Conventional two-guide or wax-up-based crown-lengthening guides (discussion only)
outcomes: predicted gingival margin and bone crest levels
f.main_result: A single digitally designed 3D-printed guide indicates both the marginal incision level and the alveolar bone crest reduction level for crown lengthening.
f.limitations: Additional time before surgery and greater cost than conventional methods.

f.population: One patient needing esthetic crown lengthening from maxillary right lateral to left central incisor
f.intervention: Digitally guided dual technique: printed gingivectomy guide and alveolectomy guide from registered intraoral scan and CBCT
f.main_result: The dual-guide technique is described as giving satisfactory esthetics and harmonious alveolar and gingival contours (no quantitative outcome).
f.funding_coi: Beijing Natural Science Foundation and Peking University grants
f.limitations: Technique needs extra pre-surgical time and cost; clinical studies are needed to validate predictability

f.population: Two esthetic cases needing crown lengthening
f.intervention: Standardized early restorative phase after crown lengthening: abutment preparation at 3 weeks and staged provisional modification
f.main_result: Early postsurgical temporization conditions soft tissues, especially papillae, and allows patient-specific timing of the definitive phase (descriptive, no numeric outcome).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Patient has short temporary crowns and larger interdental black holes for 3 weeks

f.intervention: Classification system (types I-III) for aesthetic crown lengthening treatment planning
f.main_result: Proposes a classification of aesthetic crown lengthening based on alveolar crest position relative to anticipated gingival margin, to streamline diagnosis and treatment sequence.
f.funding_coi: Author declares no financial interest
f.limitations: Long-term gingival margin stability and biotype effects need further study

f.population: 15 systemically healthy patients, 90 teeth (30 crown-lengthened, 60 adjacent), maxillary anterior
f.intervention: Aesthetic crown lengthening using Chu aesthetic gauges
f.comparison: Treated vs adjacent vs non-adjacent sites; baseline vs 3 vs 6 months
f.main_result: Biologic width at treated sites rose from 1.63 mm at baseline to 1.79 mm at 3 months and 1.99 mm at 6 months.
f.funding_coi: Gauges donated by Dr Stephen Chu; no funding statement
f.limitations: Small sample and short follow-up; larger, longer studies needed

f.population: 100 healthy patients, unrestored anterior teeth
f.intervention: Total dentogingival complex measured from free gingival margin to osseous crest by probing
f.main_result: Total dentogingival complex measured 3 mm on the facial aspect and 3 to 4.5 mm interproximally.

f.population: 30-year-old woman with inflamed gingiva and asymmetric margins on anterior maxillary teeth (nos. 11, 21, 22)
f.intervention: 3D-printed template-guided crown lengthening, then interim CAD/CAM crowns to induce papilla growth
f.main_result: Interim CAD/CAM crowns induced papilla growth of 0.5 to 1.5 mm, giving a symmetrical gingival contour.
f.funding_coi: Grant from China Medical University School of Stomatology; no disclosures

f.population: Clinical and radiographic studies and reviews on crown lengthening, plus one case followed 8 years
f.intervention: Periodontal crown-lengthening surgery
f.main_result: About 3 mm of supragingival soft tissue rebounds coronal to the alveolar crest, taking at least three months.

f.population: 22-year-old woman with altered passive eruption and gummy smile
f.intervention: Single 3D-printed surgical guide from CBCT and intraoral scan for gingivectomy and osteoectomy
f.main_result: A satisfactory outcome was obtained 6 months after surgery.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Further clinical studies needed for reliability and repeatability

f.population: 41-year-old woman with short clinical crowns and diastemas
f.intervention: Surgical crown lengthening (13-23) guided by silicone guide from wax-up, then veneers
f.main_result: Crown lengthening was a viable option for facilitating restorative therapy and improving esthetics; definitive prostheses delivered after 6-month healing.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interests declared

f.main_result: Sufficient bone removal, not flap manipulation, is essential for stable gingival margins after esthetic crown lengthening.
f.funding_coi: Author declares no conflict of interest

f.population: Patients with single or partial edentulism and alveolar bone atrophy
f.intervention: 6-mm ultra-short microrough implants without bone grafting
f.main_result: No significant relationship between crown-to-implant ratio and peri-implant bone loss; implant success 96.9%.
f.sample_size: 66 ultra-short implants in 47 patients followed up

f.population: 17-year-old female with excessive gingival display
f.intervention: Esthetic crown lengthening followed by modified lip repositioning surgery
f.limitations: Persistent mouth breathing and recurrent gingival inflammation remained unresolved.

f.main_result: Little evidence-based research; no definitive recommendations on crown-to-root ratio could be ascertained.

f.population: Extracted noncarious human third molars (dentin)
f.intervention: 10-MDP-containing self-etch adhesive applied on dentin, analysed by FIB-SEM, TEM and SPM
f.main_result: 10-MDP nano-layering forms a 3D network with higher elastic modulus than the surrounding adhesive resin.
f.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI funding; no conflicts declared

f.population: Immediate implants in extraction sockets in mandibles of dogs
f.intervention: Implants placed 0.8 mm deeper and more lingually
f.comparison: Implants positioned in the center of the alveolus
outcomes: position of alveolar crest relative to implant rough/smooth limit
f.main_result: At the buccal aspect the rough/smooth limit lay 2 mm from the crest in controls vs 0.6 mm in test sites (P<0.05).

f.population: Implants in edentulous mandible of mongrel dogs
f.intervention: Implants placed at, 1 mm or 2 mm below crestal bone, with conventional or immediate restoration
f.main_result: More apical placement moved first bone contact apically without affecting ridge loss or soft tissue margin; immediate restoration kept the margin more coronal.
f.funding_coi: Brazilian public research grants; implants supplied by Conexão; no conflicts reported
f.limitations: Longer healing periods needed to confirm significance.

f.population: Patients with diabetes receiving dental implants
f.main_result: 16 studies included; implant failure in diabetic patients ranged 0–14.3% and glycemic control was rarely interpretable.
f.limitations: Glycemic control reporting was insufficient in most studies.

f.main_result: Hyperglycaemia negatively influences bone formation and remodelling, reduces osseointegration and increases implant failure percentages in diabetic patients.

f.population: 10 non-diabetic individuals (12 implants) and 20 persons with type 2 diabetes (30 implants)
f.intervention: Placement of rough-surfaced (SLA) Straumann implants with resonance frequency analysis over 4 months
f.comparison: Non-diabetic individuals and diabetic groups stratified by HbA1c level
outcomes: time to healing (return to baseline stability)
f.main_result: Persons with HbA1c of 8.1% or higher had a greater maximum decrease in stability and about double the time to return to baseline stability.
f.funding_coi: NIH/NIDCR grant R01 DE017882, ITI Foundation, San Antonio Area Foundation; implants provided by Institut Straumann AG

outcomes: clinical diagnostic parameters (probing depth, bleeding on probing, suppuration)
f.main_result: Clinical parameters are highly specific but less sensitive for peri-implant conditions, and definitive diagnosis of peri-implantitis relies on progressive radiographic bone loss.
f.funding_coi: The authors declared no direct conflicts of interest.

f.population: 14 clinical human studies of diabetic and non-diabetic patients receiving dental implants
f.intervention: Dental implant placement in diabetic patients
f.comparison: Non-diabetic patients
f.main_result: Diabetes did not significantly affect implant failure (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.80-1.44, p=.65), but marginal bone loss was greater in diabetic patients (mean difference 0.20 mm, p=.001).
f.sample_size: 1,260 implants in diabetic patients and 11,476 in non-diabetic patients from 14 studies
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil); no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Results should be interpreted with caution because of uncontrolled confounding factors in the included studies.

f.main_result: Recent clinical studies and systematic reviews suggest implant survival is manageable even with poor glycemic control, while long-term vulnerabilities such as marginal bone loss and peri-implantitis risk remain in question.

f.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, well-controlled versus not well-controlled, in 7 studies
f.intervention: Dental implant placement in patients with diabetes not well controlled
f.comparison: Patients with well-controlled diabetes
f.main_result: Pooled analysis showed no direct association between glycemic level and implant failure (RR 0.620, 95% CI 0.225-1.705).
f.limitations: The authors noted limitations of the meta-analysis and called for well-designed future studies with adequate control of confounding factors.

f.population: Sixty-six patients with a single posterior edentulous site
f.intervention: Implant bed preparation with low-speed drilling (150 rpm) without irrigation
f.comparison: High-speed drilling (800 rpm) with irrigation
f.main_result: Postoperative pain and inflammation were significantly lower with low-speed drilling without irrigation, and comfort was higher; quality of life did not differ.
f.funding_coi: Not funded; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Sample size was calculated for marginal bone loss, not for the patient-centered secondary outcomes, so results are interpreted with caution.

f.population: Eight Yucatan minipigs, 32 implants placed
f.intervention: Tri-oval Nobel Biocare N1 TiUltra implants (3.5 x 11 mm) placed with a low-speed, no-irrigation site preparation protocol
f.comparison: Circular cross-section NobelActive TiUltra implants (3.5 x 10 mm) with back-tapered collar and conventional drilling
f.main_result: Histological BIC was higher for the tri-oval test implants than controls (74.1% vs. 60.9%, p < .001), with mildly higher platform-level inflammation.
f.follow_up: 13 weeks of healing after implant placement
f.funding_coi: Funded by Nobel Biocare AG; one author is a scientific advisor for Nobel Biocare
f.limitations: Limitations pertinent to preclinical settings and short-term evaluation.

outcomes: early implant failure in patients on antiresorptive drugs
f.main_result: Zirconia implants show a mean 5-year survival of 97.2% comparable to titanium; low-dose antiresorptive drugs did not increase early implant failure.
f.funding_coi: Authors reported conflicts of interest at the ITI Consensus Meeting.
f.limitations: Current evidence remains limited, especially for 2-piece zirconia implant designs.

f.funding_coi: Conferences fully funded by the EAO to avoid commercial influence

f.population: Preclinical in vivo (dog) studies and clinical studies of dental implants with or without peri-implantitis, via two systematic reviews and one critical review
f.intervention: Implant surface/material, implant and restorative design elements, and surgical peri-implantitis treatment types
f.comparison: Modified vs non-modified implant surfaces; reconstructive vs access flap treatment
f.main_result: Overcontouring (emergence angle >30 degrees with convex profile) and restricted hygiene access raise peri-implantitis risk; reconstructive therapy gave less mucosal recession than access flap (WMD -1.35 mm).
f.sample_size: Critical review of 31 studies; SR of 25 preclinical and 31 clinical publications (7,605 patients, 26,188 implants)
f.follow_up: 12 clinical studies had at least 10 years follow-up
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Implant surface technologies are tied to other brand-specific features, so surface effects per se cannot be isolated

f.population: Patients with dental implants undergoing soft tissue augmentation, via three systematic reviews and one critical review
f.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation procedures at dental implant sites
f.comparison: No soft tissue augmentation, hard tissue augmentation alone, or soft tissue substitutes vs autologous grafts
f.main_result: Soft tissue augmentation reduced mid-buccal recession (0.34 mm immediate, 0.17 mm delayed placement) with limited effect on marginal bone and on PROMs.
f.sample_size: Meta-analysis of 4 RCTs and 2 CCTs (215 patients, 215 implants) for immediate placement
f.funding_coi: Supported by the European Association for Osseointegration; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Included studies possibly underpowered and heterogeneous in implant timing and graft type

f.intervention: Abutment and provisional restoration emergence profile design to shape peri-implant soft tissue
f.main_result: A narrowed emergence profile lets soft tissue drape coronally and increases apparent soft-tissue volume, while a larger profile compresses tissue apically.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures
f.limitations: Clinicians cannot fully predict how peri-implant tissues will respond to treatment and modifications

f.population: Patients with dental implants (three included studies, 168-349 implants)
f.intervention: Dental implants with a large emergence angle and/or convex emergence profile
f.comparison: Implants with small EA and/or concave or straight profile
f.main_result: Both prevalence studies found significantly more peri-implantitis in bone-level implants with EA above 30 degrees (prevalence 16.7% and 24.8% at implant level); convex profile may also raise prevalence.
f.sample_size: 3 studies included from 1116 unique titles; 168-349 implants
f.funding_coi: No funding
f.limitations: Only three eligible studies; associations should be considered with caution and causality remains unclear

f.intervention: Preparation, prevention and management of medical emergencies, including an emergency drug kit
f.main_result: Medical emergencies occur with similar frequency in Japan and North America (syncope most common); dentists need ABC/CPR competence and six essential emergency drugs.

f.population: Mandibular molars with class II furcation defects treated with guided tissue regeneration
f.intervention: Guided tissue regeneration at class II furcation defects, with grading of cervical enamel projection at surgery
f.comparison: Sites with grade 0 (no) cervical enamel projection vs grades I to III
outcomes: prevalence and grade of cervical enamel projection
f.main_result: Cervical enamel projection was present in 82.1% of mandibular molars with class II furcation defects (grade II most common, 34.8%); sites with CEP had higher baseline probing depth but greater attachment gains after GTR.
f.sample_size: 37 mandibular molars (grade 0: 8, grade I: 9, grade II: 12, grade III: 8 listed in table)

f.population: 57-year-old woman with chronic periodontitis
f.intervention: Non-surgical therapy then apically positioned flap surgery; CEPs left in place
f.main_result: CEPs were found on the palatal roots of both maxillary second molars, an undocumented location, at the sites of greatest attachment loss; pockets reduced to maintainable depth (4 mm or less).
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Extracted mandibular first and second molars with Grade III cervical enamel projections
f.intervention: Stereomicroscopy, light microscopy and SEM of the CEP-cementum interface
outcomes: pouch-like opening between enamel and cementum
f.main_result: 16 of 35 teeth (45.7%) had CEPs covered by cementum, and 15 of those 16 (93.8%) had a narrow pouch-like opening between cementum and enamel.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Clinical significance of the pouches is yet to be determined

f.population: Endodontically treated teeth restored with endocrowns (3 clinical and 7 in vitro studies)
f.intervention: Endocrown restorations
f.comparison: Conventional crowns
f.main_result: Estimated 5-year survival 91.4% for endocrowns vs 98.3% for conventional crowns and success 77.7% vs 94%, with no significant difference (P>.05).
f.sample_size: 10 studies (3 clinical, 7 in vitro) from 2584 records; 3 clinical studies in the meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: No specific grant funding
f.limitations: Few clinical studies and no randomized trials; long-term well-designed clinical studies are needed

f.population: 20 healthy mandibular molars, endodontically treated
f.intervention: Endocrown (IPS e.max Press) anchored in the pulp chamber
f.comparison: Conventional indirect crown with filling core and glass fiber post
f.main_result: Endocrowns had higher median fracture strength (674.75 N) than post-retained conventional crowns (469.90 N), p=0.002
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated

f.population: 45 extracted molars, decoronated and endodontically treated, without ferrule
f.intervention: Resin nanoceramic (Lava Ultimate) CAD/CAM crowns with 4-mm buildup, 2-mm buildup or no buildup (endocrown), self-adhesive cement
f.comparison: 4-mm and 2-mm composite buildups versus endocrown without buildup
f.main_result: Fatigue survival was 53%, 87% and 87% (4-mm, 2-mm, no buildup), not significantly different; post-fatigue load-to-failure 2969, 2794 and 2606 N also did not differ
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq and CAPES grants; 3M ESPE provided materials; no conflict declared

f.population: 90 extracted human premolars, root canal treated
f.intervention: Premolar endocrowns in lithium disilicate, polymer infiltrated ceramic or high translucency zirconia, with 2 mm or 4.5 mm occlusal reduction or 4.5 mm plus 2 mm radicular extension
f.comparison: Comparison across the three materials and three preparation designs
f.main_result: Lithium disilicate endocrowns had the highest fracture resistance (62.55, 45.80 and 74.27 MPa) versus PIC (about 22-26 MPa) and HTZ (23-37 MPa); radicular extension improved LD and HTZ
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 40 extracted human molars, intact, no caries
f.intervention: Posterior partial coverage restorations in lithium disilicate (IPS e.max) at 1 or 2 mm thickness, luted with Variolink II
f.comparison: Leucite-reinforced ceramic (IPS Empress) at 1 or 2 mm thickness
f.main_result: 2-mm lithium disilicate (2505 N) was more fracture resistant than 1-mm (1569 N) and 2-mm (1716 N) leucite-reinforced ceramic; thickness had no significant effect
f.funding_coi: Ivoclar Vivadent donated ceramic materials; no conflict declared

f.main_result: Remaining tooth structure plays an important role in ETT survival, while the literature is contradictory on post type and root fractures and on avoiding a post
f.funding_coi: No commercial or associative interest declared

f.population: Bonded bar specimens of zirconia, glass-infiltrated graded zirconia and feldspathic ceramic
f.intervention: Glass infiltration of the zirconia cementation surface (graded zirconia), bonded with Panavia F 2.0 after sandblasting or HF etching
f.comparison: Conventional zirconia and feldspathic ceramic
f.main_result: Baseline and long-term GC of graded zirconia was 2-3 and 8 times that of zirconia and similar to feldspathic ceramic
f.follow_up: 7 days hydration baseline; long-term after 20,000 thermal cycles and 2-month aging
f.funding_coi: NIDCR/NIH and Israeli Science Foundation grants

f.population: Three 3-D finite element models of a maxillary central incisor
f.intervention: Leucite and lithium disilicate ceramic endocrowns (100 N load at 130 degrees)
f.comparison: Metal post and core with ceramic crown
outcomes: modified von Mises stresses in dentin, ceramic, cement and post
contact stresses at the adhesive interface
f.main_result: Post-and-core had the lowest stresses; leucite endocrown 47.5 MPa mvM, close to its tensile strength; lithium disilicate endocrown 61.8 MPa, over 4 times below its tensile strength

f.population: 50 sound human maxillary first molars
f.intervention: Endodontically treated molars restored with lithium disilicate full crown, endocrown, onlay or inlay
f.comparison: Intact teeth (control)
f.main_result: Mean failure loads: intact 985 N, full crown 1076 N, endocrown 989 N, onlay 908 N, inlay 638 N

f.population: 36 recently extracted mandibular third molars
f.intervention: Lithium disilicate (IPS e.max CAD) endocrowns with 1 mm or 2 mm preparation ferrule
f.comparison: Endocrown without ferrule
f.main_result: Failure load was 638.5 N without ferrule vs 1101.0 N (1 mm) and 956.3 N (2 mm); failure stress did not differ; catastrophic failures were frequent in all groups
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 30 extracted human maxillary molars, endodontically treated
f.intervention: CAD/CAM endocrowns with 2-mm pulp chamber extension in resin nanoceramic (Lava Ultimate)
f.comparison: Feldspathic (CEREC Blocks) and lithium disilicate (e.max) endocrowns
f.main_result: Lava Ultimate endocrowns had higher fracture resistance (1583 N vs 1341 and 1369 N) and more favorable failures, but more dye penetration (2.80 vs 1.11 and 1.91 mm)
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated

f.intervention: Preparation forms and clinical procedure for CAD/CAM ceramic inlays and partial crowns using standardized preparation instruments
f.main_result: Adhesively bonded ceramic restorations need different preparations from metal ones: rounded internal angles and no bevels.

f.population: Extracted mandibular third molars
f.intervention: Lithium disilicate CAD/CAM endocrowns with pulp chamber extension depths of 2, 3 and 4 mm
f.comparison: Endocrowns with different pulp chamber extension depths (2 vs 3 vs 4 mm)
f.main_result: The 2- and 4-mm chamber extension groups had the highest fracture resistance stress; 3- and 4-mm groups showed nearly universal catastrophic tooth fracture, and 8 of 12 in the 2-mm group had nonrestorable fractures.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no proprietary, financial or other interest
f.limitations: Fixed crown height and a single force application height may change fracture load results.

f.population: Patients over 18 years treated with onlays in the posterior region, follow-up of one year or more
f.intervention: Onlay restorations (ceramic, hybrid, composite) in the posterior region
f.comparison: Different onlay restoration materials
f.main_result: Estimated onlay survival was 94.2%; composite onlays had lower survival, and survival decreased with follow-up time.
f.sample_size: 29 studies in qualitative and 27 in quantitative analysis
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 3D finite element models of an endodontically treated maxillary premolar (plus restored teeth for fatigue testing)
f.intervention: CEREC ceramic endocrown
f.comparison: Classical crown with glass fiber post and composite core
f.main_result: Endocrown dentin and cement stresses were lower than for the classical crown; overall failure probabilities were similar, and fatigue testing gave higher fracture resistance for the endocrown (1,446 vs 1,163).

f.population: Endodontically treated premolar with MOD preparation (3D FE models and CEREC-restored teeth)
f.intervention: CEREC ceramic endocrown
f.comparison: CEREC ceramic inlay and conventional crown
f.main_result: Weibull failure probability for normal biting was 95% (inlay), 2% (endocrown) and 2% (conventional crown); endocrown and crown were similar in first AE load.

f.population: 3D finite element models of an endodontically treated premolar with shallow or deep cracks
f.intervention: CAD/CAM ceramic endocrown
f.comparison: CAD/CAM ceramic onlay and conventional crown
outcomes: stress in enamel, dentin and cement
f.main_result: Failure probability in a shallow-cracked premolar was 27% (onlay), 2% (endocrown), 1% (crown); in a deep-cracked premolar 70%, 10% and 2%.
f.funding_coi: Authors deny any conflicts of interest

f.population: Decoronated endodontically treated molars without ferrule
f.intervention: Direct buildup with dual-cure composite Multicore HB, restored with bonded Empress CAD glass ceramic crowns
f.comparison: Multicore Flow buildup with a glass-fiber-reinforced composite post
f.main_result: No significant difference between MHB (859.4 N) and MFP (796.13 N) in fracture load, cycles or survival; post insertion did not enhance performance.
f.funding_coi: Ivoclar Vivadent provided materials; authors declare no interest

f.population: Single-rooted premolars, endodontically treated, no ferrule
f.intervention: CAD/CAM endocrowns (2.5-mm or 5-mm deep) in composite or lithium disilicate
f.comparison: 5-mm deep post&crown; composite vs lithium disilicate
f.main_result: All specimens survived 1,200,000 chewing cycles; only for the 2.5-mm endocrown did composite give higher load-to-failure than lithium disilicate, and higher loads came with more root fractures.
f.funding_coi: CAPES scholarship; GC and Ivoclar Vivadent donated materials

f.population: Extracted maxillary central incisors, endodontically treated, 2 mm ferrule
f.intervention: Glass fiber posts of 5 mm or 10 mm, or no post (endocrown), with composite or ceramic CEREC crowns
f.comparison: Short vs long post vs endocrown; composite vs ceramic crowns
f.main_result: Post presence, post length and crown material did not significantly affect fracture resistance (P = 0.778); endocrowns and short posts gave more repairable fractures than long posts.
f.funding_coi: Declared no conflict of interest

f.population: 48 devitalized human upper first premolars cut at the CEJ
f.intervention: CAD-CAM lithium disilicate endocrowns with a 2 mm or 4 mm endo-core
f.comparison: Flat overlays without endo-core (negative control) and crowns with post and core (positive control)
outcomes: marginal integrity (closed margins) before and after thermo-mechanical loading
f.main_result: Survival after stepwise fatigue loading did not differ significantly between groups (4/8 overlays, 5/12 endocrowns with 2 mm core, 6/12 with 4 mm core, 3/12 post-and-core crowns survived 105000 cycles); four overlays debonded early.
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Swiss Dental Association (SSO); materials supplied by Ivoclar-Vivadent; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Authors frame conclusions as limited to this in-vitro study and call for further studies.

f.population: 42 sound human mandibular molars, endodontically treated and cut 2 mm above the CEJ
f.intervention: Endocrowns made of conventional composite, bulk fill composite, composite modeled with adhesive (SBMP or SBU), or IPS e.max
f.comparison: IPS e.max lithium disilicate endocrowns (positive control) and unprepared sound teeth (negative control)
f.main_result: Load-to-fracture (1979.2 N e.max to 2681.4 N bulk fill) and work-of-fracture did not differ among materials, but e.max endocrowns had about 71% irreparable fractures versus about 14% for composite with SBMP.
f.funding_coi: Financed in part by CAPES (Brazil); authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 8 studies: 3 clinical trials and 5 in vitro studies of endocrowns
f.intervention: Endocrown restorations
f.comparison: Conventional treatments (intraradicular posts, direct composite resin, inlay/onlay)
f.main_result: Clinical success of endocrowns was 94 to 100%; pooled fracture strength was higher than conventional treatments overall (p = 0.03) but not in posterior teeth alone (p = 0.07).
f.sample_size: 8 studies; 102 teeth in the in vitro studies
f.follow_up: Clinical trials: up to 6, 15 or 36 months
f.limitations: Caution is needed interpreting in vitro results; clinical trials scored poorly on bias items.

f.intervention: Endocrown restorations for endodontically treated teeth with extensive coronal loss
f.comparison: Conventional post-core and fixed partial dentures
f.main_result: Endocrowns are presented as an alternative to post-core restorations with better esthetics and mechanical performance, lower cost and shorter clinical time.
f.funding_coi: No funding and no conflict of interest declared

f.population: One adult male patient with worn teeth and amalgam restorations with recurrent caries, seeking a smile makeover
f.intervention: Lithium disilicate vonlays (onlay with extended buccal veneer surface) on posterior teeth, with anterior porcelain veneers
f.main_result: Authors report, from experience, under 1% annual failure for bicuspid vonlays with enough enamel and no documented failures for monolithic lithium disilicate molar vonlays.

f.population: 3D finite element model of a maxillary central incisor
f.intervention: Endocrowns of composite, sintered alumina or feldspathic ceramic
f.comparison: Sound tooth and glass fiber post restorations with feldspathic or alumina crown
f.main_result: High modulus materials such as alumina altered the natural biomechanical behavior with high interface stress, while composite endocrowns gave low stress concentration.
f.limitations: Conclusions apply within a linear static analysis using an arbitrary 10 N load.

f.population: 320 automated osteotomies in standardised bone specimens
f.intervention: Ceramic (zirconia-based) implant drills of four diameters, with and without external saline irrigation, at 10 and 16 mm depth
f.comparison: Stainless steel implant drills
outcomes: temperature change at 1 and 2 mm from the osteotomy
f.main_result: Steel drills produced significantly lower temperatures than ceramic drills; with irrigation all steel drills stayed below 47 C while small-diameter ceramic drills reached or exceeded it at 16 mm depth.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' institutions and ITI Research Grant 772_2011

f.population: 25 patients with single-tooth edentulism receiving 30 implants
f.intervention: Low-speed (50 rpm) drilling without irrigation
f.comparison: Conventional high-speed (800 rpm) drilling with saline irrigation
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone loss at 12 months
f.main_result: Mean bone loss was 0.83 mm with irrigation versus 0.62 mm without (p>0.05), and success was 93.3% versus 100%.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no competing interests

f.intervention: Cosmetic dentistry guided by smile design principles
Use of the golden ratio (phi) as a measure of facial proportion and symmetry
f.main_result: The authors conclude that the golden ratio can characterize symmetrical forms and propose its use in facial aesthetics.
f.funding_coi: No financial disclosures or conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Phi ratio has difficulty explaining facial harmony in the moving face and inter-racial mixtures.

f.population: One patient with an excessively worn dentition (case report)
f.intervention: Rehabilitation of the worn dentition using a digital workflow combined with conventional procedures
f.main_result: The digital workflow aims at faster, more predictable treatment, but a combination of digital and conventional procedures is still needed for complex cases.
f.limitations: Digital technology alone is not sufficient; digital and conventional procedures must be combined in complex cases.

f.population: Maxillary anterior teeth with tooth size and proportion discrepancies (clinical examples)
f.intervention: Aesthetic measurement gauges (T-Bar and In-Line Proportion Gauge tips, preset 78% width/length ratio) used to diagnose and correct tooth size discrepancies
outcomes: clinical crown length after crown lengthening
f.main_result: The gauges give objective width/length targets for maxillary anterior teeth (lateral 6.5/8.5, canine 7.5/9.5, central 8.5/11 mm) at a preset 78% ratio.
f.funding_coi: Author is the inventor of Chu's Aesthetic Gauges and a consultant to Hu-Friedy

f.population: Patients accepted for treatment in an Advanced Education in General Dentistry program
f.intervention: Seven-point dental esthetic checklist (midline, vertical axis, horizontal, central incisors, incisal edge line, smile line, profile and phonetics) for diagnostic work-up
f.main_result: A seven-point checklist prompts residents to assess lip, cheek, tongue, smile and facial features and so aim treatment at dentofacial harmony.
f.limitations: The checklist is not a complete list of all possible categories and nuances of an esthetic assessment.

f.population: Healthy Caucasian adults aged 19-29 with natural anterior dentition
f.intervention: Standardized photographic analysis of smile parameters (midlines, lip position and curvature, incisal curve vs lower lip, teeth displayed, tooth form, tooth and lip arc slope)
outcomes: tooth arc and lip arc slope
f.main_result: Average smile: coinciding midlines (85%), average smile line (52%), straight upper lip curvature, no lower-lip contact (75%), teeth to second premolar (45%), oval tooth most common (63%); tooth arc slope 9 degrees, lip arc 13 degrees.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Additional research is needed to verify the findings in other populations and with advanced methods.

f.population: 146 extracted human maxillary anterior teeth from white subjects, worn and unworn
f.intervention: Measurement of crown width (W), length (L) and width/length ratio (R) on standardized digital images
f.comparison: Worn versus unworn teeth within each tooth group
f.main_result: Incisal wear did not change crown width but shortened crowns; width/length ratio was highest in worn central incisors (87%) and lowest in unworn canines and lateral incisors (73%), unworn central incisors 78%.
f.sample_size: 146 teeth (44 central incisors, 41 lateral incisors, 38 canines, 23 first premolars)

f.intervention: Tooth-colored restorations: posterior composite resin, ceramic inlays/onlays, CEREC, porcelain laminate veneers, all-ceramic crowns and fixed partial dentures
f.main_result: Prognosis of esthetic restorations depends mainly on choice of material, precise technique and patient selection.
f.sample_size: Medline search 1986-2006 plus manual search of textbooks
f.limitations: For zirconia, 5- to 10-year clinical studies on success rate and mode of failure are lacking.

f.population: Patients with implant-supported restorations in the esthetic zone (maxillary and mandibular anterior teeth and premolars) in 58 included studies
f.intervention: Prosthodontic parameters: 3D implant position, provisional restorations and their timing, platform size and form, abutment and definitive restoration material, retention mode
outcomes: esthetic outcome indices (PES/WES, papilla score, midfacial mucosal level)
f.main_result: Facial malpositioning of implants consistently increased mucosal recession; no significant esthetic difference between all-ceramic and metal-ceramic prostheses, and no firm conclusion for cement vs screw retention.
f.sample_size: 58 studies (15 RCTs, 6 cohort studies, 37 case series)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: The literature is small and generally of low quality, and most studies concern single-tooth replacement.

f.population: Partially dentate adults needing fixed implant-supported prostheses
f.intervention: Definitive fixed implant-supported prosthesis without a prior interim restoration
f.comparison: Interim fixed implant-supported prosthesis before the definitive prosthesis
f.main_result: Only two RCTs qualified; evidence is insufficient to support or refute providing an interim restoration, though interim restorations may improve esthetics and omitting them may reduce chair time.
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of study methodologies and outcome measures prevented meta-analysis.

f.population: Patients with single-tooth implant rehabilitation in the esthetic area
f.intervention: Objective esthetic indices and patient-reported outcome measures for assessing single-implant outcomes
outcomes: agreement between professional and patient esthetic ratings
f.main_result: No consensus exists on a universal esthetic index for implant-supported crowns, and patients rate cosmetic outcomes more favorably than professionals do.
f.limitations: It is not yet possible to provide evidence-based conclusions on success assessment in implant dentistry.

f.main_result: Very few studies of plastic surgery around teeth and implants consider patient needs (true end points), and no validated questionnaire exists to quantify patient esthetic satisfaction.

f.population: Natural dentitions of populations in 6 studies: 395 men and 446 women
f.intervention: Evaluation of the golden proportion in maxillary anterior tooth width ratios
f.comparison: Tooth width ratios of male versus female participants
f.main_result: The golden proportion was not prevalent; lateral-to-central incisor ratio did not differ by sex (P=.22, I2=89%), canine-to-lateral ratio was greater in men (P<.001).
f.funding_coi: No specific funding received
f.limitations: High heterogeneity among studies reduced precision of results

f.intervention: Historical overview of the evolution of aesthetic dentistry over the past 100 years
f.main_result: Aesthetic dentistry has progressed tremendously over 100 years, especially through digital tools and workflows for 3D interdisciplinary smile design.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts declared

f.population: 376 dental students with natural dentition (Arab subjects)
f.intervention: Measuring maxillary anterior tooth widths on standardized frontal smile images and testing the golden proportion, RED proportion and golden percentage
outcomes: golden proportion between successive tooth widths
f.main_result: Golden proportion between right central and lateral incisors in 31.3% of men and 27.1% of women; golden and RED proportions unsuitable, golden percentage usable if adjusted (central 23%, lateral 15%, canine 12%).
f.funding_coi: Supported financially by the Deanship of Scientific Research, University of Jordan

f.intervention: Discussion of implant placement alternatives in the esthetic area: timing, 3D position, multiple missing teeth, infected sites, abutment and crown morphology
f.main_result: Immediate placement can succeed esthetically but is technique sensitive; aiming the implant axis at the incisal edge with a shoulderless abutment allows a natural cervical contour.

f.intervention: Interdisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management of anterior dental esthetics, planning starting from esthetics
f.main_result: Treatment planning should start with esthetics, then function, structure and biology, using restorative, orthodontic and periodontal disciplines as needed.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients with single-unit implants in the esthetic zone (RCTs, minimum 10 patients, 1-year follow-up)
f.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and/or immediate loading protocols
f.comparison: Conventional (delayed) placement and loading protocols
f.main_result: Immediate and early placement gave stable esthetic outcomes at 1, 2 and 10 years; loading protocols did not influence esthetic outcomes short and medium term.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated
f.limitations: Small number of included RCTs and limited extracted data

f.population: Patients 18 or older with single-tooth implants in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation with autologous, allogeneic, xenogeneic or synthetic grafting material
f.comparison: No soft tissue augmentation or a different graft material
f.main_result: Grafting gave 0.34 mm less recession and 0.66 mm thicker mid-buccal mucosa after immediate placement, and 0.17 mm less recession after delayed placement, versus no graft at 1 year.
f.follow_up: At least 1 year after implant placement
f.funding_coi: No financial support, no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Large heterogeneity in study designs and few eligible studies per topic

f.intervention: Macroesthetic smile design criteria based on the facial midline and tooth reveal
f.main_result: Macroesthetic criteria are organized by facial midline and tooth reveal, and serve as guidelines only.

f.population: Patients requiring anterior esthetic rehabilitations
f.intervention: Mathematical tooth proportions: golden proportion, golden percentage and RED proportion
f.comparison: Not using such formulas
f.main_result: No formula gave consistent esthetic results; golden proportion occurs between central and lateral incisor in some cases but rarely lateral-canine; golden percentage is a starting point if adjusted.

f.population: 45 patients with maxillary anterior single-tooth implants
f.intervention: Early implant placement with GBR, provisional then PFM crown; esthetic outcome by PES/WES
f.main_result: Mean total PES/WES was 14.7 (range 11 to 18) with all 45 implants meeting osseointegration success criteria
materials_brands: Straumann Dental Implant System (sandblasted acid-etched titanium implants)
f.funding_coi: Departmental funds of the Universities of Bern and Geneva; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Retrospective design; authors state prospective trials are needed to validate the index

f.intervention: Review of principles governing smile design
f.main_result: Smile design should be esthetically appealing, functionally sound, conservative and multidisciplinary

f.intervention: Prosthetically driven design measures (white crown morphology, pink ceramics) to compensate peri-implant soft tissue deficiencies in the esthetic zone
f.main_result: Minor-to-moderate soft tissue deficiencies can be compensated by morphological crown design alone; major deficiencies may need pink ceramics

f.intervention: Literature review of esthetic guidelines, patient preference studies and anatomic norms for complete dentures
f.main_result: Little useful evidence-based information exists for restoring dentate appearance in edentulous patients; 3 esthetic concepts identified

f.intervention: Review of literature on facial bone, implant diameter, implant-tooth distance, abutment design and provisionalization for esthetics
f.main_result: Generous facial bone, implants under 4 mm, platform-switched abutments, 2-4 mm implant-to-tooth distance, avoiding adjacent implants and early provisionalization favor esthetics

f.intervention: Prosthetically induced soft tissue topography via custom provisional crown and abutment

f.population: 10 patients with 43 interdental papilla sites in the maxillary anterior region
f.intervention: Injectable hyaluronic acid gel applied up to five times at 3-week intervals
outcomes: black triangle area, height and width
f.main_result: 29 of 43 sites had complete papilla reconstruction and 14 improved by 39 to 96%
materials_brands: Teosyal Puresense Global Action hyaluronic acid gel
f.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
f.limitations: Results beyond 6 months are not known

f.intervention: Step-by-step Photoshop technique for smile analysis and digital smile design
f.main_result: Digital smile design can be completed in about three to four minutes and aids communication between dentist, ceramist and patient

f.intervention: Review of scientific and artistic principles of smile design
f.main_result: A comprehensive approach analyzing face, lips, gingiva and teeth is needed for a natural smile that also enhances oral health

f.population: Published clinical and preclinical studies on hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies at implant sites
f.intervention: Narrative review of factors and conditions associated with hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies at implants
outcomes: etiological factors of hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies
f.main_result: Deficiencies at implant sites result from many factors (post-extraction resorption, trauma, periodontitis, peri-implantitis, overload, thin tissues, lack of keratinized mucosa, malpositioning, tooth migration, systemic disease), and combined factors can worsen severity.
f.funding_coi: Hämmerle and Tarnow report research support and consulting/lecture fees from implant and biomaterial companies (Straumann, Geistlich and others).
f.limitations: No formal quality assessment or statistical analysis was done, the search was limited to English, and evidence varies from strong to scant across factors.

f.population: One 44-year-old woman seeking an esthetic consultation
f.intervention: Facial flow (FF) concept: organic orofacial analysis of the vertical component (facial midline, dental midline, tooth axis)
outcomes: harmony of dental midline and tooth axis with facial structures
f.main_result: The facial flow concept offers a more organic, perception-based alternative to straight-line, symmetry-driven smile design, using green and red zones to guide decisions.
f.limitations: Authors state research is needed to define the relationship between facial flow and the lips, and the horizontal component needs further research.

f.intervention: Application of principles of visual perception (composition, unity, proportion, shade) to denture esthetics
f.main_result: Understanding perceptual principles can free dentists from confusion in dental esthetics and let them approach denture construction with confidence.

f.population: Teeth receiving ceramic veneers, e.g. conoid teeth, diastemas, worn teeth
f.intervention: Mock-up driven technique: step-by-step conservative preparation for ceramic veneers guided by the desired final contour
f.comparison: Classic preparation technique (reduction driven by the existing tooth surface) and silicone index technique
f.main_result: The mock-up driven technique considers the final veneer contour and gives considerably less invasive preparations (cited: 80.5% of preparations confined to enamel).
f.sample_size: One illustrated case with eight maxillary anterior veneers

f.population: Two esthetic-zone cases with bone-level implants: one single implant and one two adjacent implants
f.intervention: Dynamic compression technique: soft tissue conditioning with an implant-supported provisional (initial pressure, then release by undercontouring)
f.main_result: The dynamic compression technique (initial provisional pressure, then undercontouring) is presented as a method to shape peri-implant soft tissue; stable soft tissues at 1 year in both cases; needs further validation.
f.sample_size: 2 cases (1 single implant, 1 two adjacent implants)
f.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Authors state clinical studies and in vivo histologic analyses are needed to confirm validity and long-term soft-tissue stability.

f.intervention: Aesthetic crown lengthening guided by measurement gauges (Chu's Aesthetic Gauges) that link ideal tooth proportion to the amount of osseous resection
f.main_result: Using tooth proportion and measured osseous resection with the gauges was described as beneficial for aesthetic crown lengthening in a presented case.
f.follow_up: Recalled at 4 months; restorations cemented at 6 months post-surgery
f.funding_coi: Dr. Chu is creator of Chu's Aesthetic Gauges and consultant for Hu-Friedy

f.population: Five male beagle dogs, microgrooved implants placed in the mandible
f.intervention: Microgrooved-collar one-piece implants of titanium, Y-TZP and Ce-TZP/Al2O3
f.comparison: The three implant materials (Ti, Y-TZP, Ce-TZP/Al2O3) compared with each other
outcomes: epithelial, connective and soft tissue length
f.main_result: All implants osseointegrated, with no significant differences in any histomorphometric parameter among Ti, Y-TZP and Ce-TZP/Al2O3 microgrooved implants.
f.sample_size: 18 implants (6 per material) in 5 dogs; 16 samples measured
materials_brands: Ti: ASTM F67 Grade4 (Allegheny Technologies Japan)
f.funding_coi: Supported by Nanto, which also processed the implants
f.limitations: Soft tissue frequently detached from the implant surface on sections; fractured Y-TZP implants reduced that group to four samples.

f.intervention: Suturing materials and techniques for primary wound closure and flap stabilization in periodontal and implant surgery
f.main_result: Stable flap adaptation with appropriate suturing is a key prerequisite for optimal surgical outcomes; as few sutures as needed, left 7-10 days.

f.population: Patients with dental implants (clinical studies)
f.intervention: Reduced keratinized tissue width (KT < 2 mm) as exposure
f.comparison: KT width >= 2 mm
outcomes: prevalence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
f.main_result: Implants with KT < 2 mm had significantly worse BOP, plaque indices, marginal bone loss and mucosal recession than KT >= 2 mm, and higher peri-implantitis prevalence (10.5-44% vs 5.1-8%).
f.sample_size: 22 articles describing 21 studies (15 cross-sectional, 5 longitudinal comparative, 1 case series)
f.funding_coi: Self-funded by the authors' departments; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Over half of the studies (13) did not report periodontal health, and mixed KT cut-offs (2 and 0 mm) were pooled, adding heterogeneity.

f.population: Dental implants and patients in published studies on implant loss
f.intervention: Narrative review of the etiology, occurrence and consequences of early and late implant loss
f.main_result: Early implant loss occurs in about 1.5% of implants (1 in 67) and about 4% of patients; late loss in about 3% of implants over 10 years and about 4% of patients; smoking is a risk indicator for early loss and peri-implantitis the main cause of late loss.
f.follow_up: Late loss assessed over observation periods of 10 years
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Authors note few evaluations of the consequences of implant loss and patient-reported outcomes.

f.population: Commercially available implants (Astra Tech EV) with multispecies biofilm mounted in 3D-printed intra-bony defect models
f.intervention: Air-polishing or rotating titanium brush, each combined with saline, alkaline electrolyzed water or N-acetyl-L-cysteine
f.comparison: Wiping with gauze soaked in saline, AEW or NAC; untreated contaminated implants as negative control
f.main_result: Air-polishing and rotating titanium brush removed more biofilm and reduced surface carbon more than gauze wiping; chemical adjuncts gave no benefit over saline and no method removed biofilm completely.
f.sample_size: 123 implants (33 analysed by SEM, n=3 per group)
materials_brands: Astra Tech Implant EV OsseoSpeed (Dentsply Sirona)
Airflow Prophylaxis Master with erythritol powder (EMS)
f.funding_coi: TUA research funding and Patentmedelsfonden; authors declare no conflicts, though some report honoraria/grants from implant companies
f.limitations: One implant brand, artificial short-term biofilm without calcified deposits, bacterial viability not assessed, differences from clinical anatomy.

f.population: Patients who received Bicon implants at one implant centre, 1992-2000
f.intervention: Bicon dental implant placement (exposure analysis of demographic, medical, implant, anatomic, prosthetic and reconstructive risk factors)
f.main_result: Overall complication frequency was 13.9% (10.2% inflammatory, 2.7% prosthetic, 1.0% operative); smoking, 1-stage implants and reconstructive procedures increased complication risk.
f.sample_size: 677 patients (677 implants analysed, 1 per patient; 2,349 placed)
f.funding_coi: Institutional research funds, OMS Foundation award and NIH/NIDCR awards
