f.population: 1,140 consecutively treated patients who received dental implants from one surgeon, 1982-2003
f.intervention: Dental implant placement; exposure analysis of patient factors (age, gender, smoking, medical conditions, implant location)
f.comparison: Patients without the risk factor (e.g. age under 40, healthy patients)
f.main_result: Implant failure was 8.16% in the maxilla and 4.93% in the mandible; age 60-79 (RR 2.24), smoking (1.56), diabetes (2.75), head and neck radiation (2.73) and postmenopausal estrogen therapy (2.55) raised failure risk.

f.population: Published literature on biologic complications and failing oral implants (to December 1998)
f.intervention: Literature review of diagnosis and treatment of biologic complications and failing implants
f.main_result: Infection, impaired healing and overload are the major etiologic factors; few clinical and animal studies validate the treatments, which remain largely empirical.
f.funding_coi: Public research funds; no support from any oral implant company
f.limitations: Treatment of failing implants lacks systematic scientific validation and rests on empirical experience and in vitro extrapolation.

f.population: Consecutively treated patients at one specialist clinic (Brånemark Clinic), 1986-2012
f.intervention: Implant placement with turned (Brånemark) and moderately rough (TiUnite, Osseospeed) surfaces
f.comparison: Turned versus moderately rough surface, upper versus lower jaw, first year versus later
outcomes: annual incidence of first implant failure
failure by jaw and surface type
f.main_result: 857 patients (10.0%) had at least one failure; first failures were more frequent in upper jaws, mostly within the first year (69%), and with turned versus moderately rough surfaces.
f.funding_coi: Grants from Nobel Biocare and Swedish foundations

f.population: Patients who received implants at Yonsei University Dental Hospital, 1991-2009
f.intervention: Implants from Nobel Biocare, Straumann and Biolok; analysis of risk factors for early and late failure
f.main_result: 150 of 2,796 implants failed (86 early, 64 late); early failures were mainly due to inflammation (47%) and late failures to overloading (53%), with machined surface, reconstructive procedures and two-stage surgery associated with higher failure.
f.follow_up: Between Feb 1991 and May 2009 (19-year study period)
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare, Straumann and Biolok implants
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Controlled clinical human studies of endosseous root-form titanium implants reporting failure (311 publications)
f.intervention: Review of factors associated with dental implant failure (surgical, patient, implant and prosthetic factors)
outcomes: implant failure (complete loss of the implant)
f.main_result: Failure rate was correlated with low insertion torque under early/immediate loading, inexperienced surgeons, maxilla, posterior region, heavy smoking, bone type III-IV, small bone volume, short implants, and overdentures, among others.

f.population: Seven healthy patients, each with at least 2 periodontally hopeless teeth scheduled for extraction
f.intervention: Extraction sockets grafted with DFDBA or autologous bone, re-entered 3-13 months later for biopsy and implant placement
f.comparison: Autologous bone graft in the paired socket
outcomes: presence of vital versus dead graft particles
f.main_result: DFDBA sockets showed dead graft particles with no bone formation on them, whereas autologous sockets showed vascular channels with woven and lamellar bone.
f.sample_size: 7 patients, 7 paired sites; biopsies from 6 evaluated
materials_brands: Freeze-dried cortical allograft (DFDBA), LifeNet Transplant Services, 250-500 micron

f.population: Forty patients needing extraction of a single-rooted non-molar tooth and planning an implant
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA)
f.comparison: Mineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (FDBA) from the same donor
f.main_result: DFDBA gave 38.42% vital bone versus 24.63% for FDBA and fewer residual particles (8.88% vs 25.42%), with no difference in ridge dimension changes.
f.sample_size: 40 patients (20 per group); 32 received implants with biopsy
f.follow_up: 19 weeks (18 to 20 weeks) to biopsy and implant placement
materials_brands: FDBA and DFDBA from a single donor, LifeNet Health
f.funding_coi: LifeNet Health supplied graft materials; authors report no conflicts of interest

f.population: Subjects with sites completely lacking attached gingiva associated with gingival recession, treated in one private practice
f.intervention: Free gingival graft, placed at the presurgical margin level (MFGG) or submarginally (SMFGG)
f.comparison: MFGG versus SMFGG (no untreated control)
f.main_result: From baseline to 1 year the margin shifted coronally 0.8 mm and KT increased 4.2 mm; over 10 to 25 years the margin shifted a further 0.6 mm coronally, KT decreased 0.7 mm and PD stayed stable.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 55 subjects with 73 sites lacking attached gingiva associated with recessions
f.intervention: submarginal or marginal free gingival grafts
f.comparison: 73 untreated contralateral homologous sites
f.main_result: Treated sites showed coronal displacement of the margin with reduced recession (SMFGG 1.5 mm, MFGG 1.3 mm) and stable gained KT, while untreated sites showed apical displacement and increased recession over 10 to 27 years.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 47 patients with thin biotype, 64 sites lacking attached gingiva with recession
f.intervention: marginal or submarginal free gingival grafts
f.comparison: 64 untreated contralateral homologous sites
f.main_result: At 18 to 35 years 83% of treated sites had recession reduction and 48% of untreated sites had increased recession; treated sites ended 1.7 mm more coronal with 3.3 mm wider KT.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Population selected for motivation and compliance, and only unrestored natural teeth, so external validity is limited

f.population: 44-year-old systemically healthy woman with missing mandibular incisors, severe resorption and no keratinized tissue
f.intervention: free gingival graft before implant placement, then two one-piece implants
f.main_result: The graft increased keratinized tissue and vestibule depth at the implant sites, with healthy keratinized tissue maintained around both implants.
f.limitations: Patient moved away and did not return for final restorations

f.population: Biopsies from 10 patients previously grafted for severe mucogingival defects
f.intervention: strip autograft combined with xenogeneic collagen matrix
f.comparison: 3 reference palatal strip autograft samples
f.main_result: Strip autograft/XCM biopsies were histologically indistinguishable from palatal autograft references in morphology, keratin and collagen expression, indicating normal keratinized gingiva.
f.follow_up: Biopsies taken 6 months to 1.5 years postoperatively
f.funding_coi: Lead author received honoraria from Geistlich Pharma; other authors none

f.intervention: apically positioned flap, free gingival graft and subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: These procedures augment attached gingiva effectively and predictably, the gain can be maintained long term, and they can halt recession progression.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Two patients with severe mandibular ridge resorption, lack of keratinized tissue and shallow vestibule
f.intervention: free gingival graft with modified button-suture lingual sulcoplasty
f.main_result: Case 1 gained 5 mm lingual and 4 mm buccal vestibular depth at 10 months; case 2 reached 6 mm lingual sulcus and 7 mm buccal depth at 6 months with stable keratinized tissue.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus tissue-level implants (SP, RN, 10 mm x 4.1 mm)
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Very small sample size limits interpretation

f.intervention: vascularized flaps (gingivectomy, sliding pedicle, rotated papilla, internal pedicle) at nonsubmerged implants
f.main_result: Four vascularized flap techniques are described with illustrated cases showing preserved or extended peri-implant keratinized mucosa at 3 months.

f.intervention: free gingival graft and subepithelial connective tissue graft at nonsubmerged implants
f.main_result: Both illustrated cases healed uneventfully, and the connective tissue graft case showed excellent peri-implant soft tissue health after 8 weeks.
f.sample_size: 2 illustrated cases (1 free gingival graft, 1 connective tissue graft)

f.population: 8 edentulous patients (mean age 65) with <2 mm keratinized tissue around implant overdentures
f.intervention: apically positioned flap, pedicle graft, connective tissue graft or free gingival graft
f.comparison: Techniques compared with each other, no untreated control
f.main_result: Second-stage apically repositioned flap gave a mean 3.1 mm keratinized tissue gain and pedicle flap 2.8 mm; an APF before implant placement gave 5 mm in case 1.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 5 implant candidates (3 women, 2 men, mean age 47) with major loss of attached gingiva
f.intervention: free gingival graft immobilized with a newly designed acrylic stent
f.main_result: After 1 year the remaining graft averaged 37% of its initial size, with a proper increase in attached gingiva width.

f.population: 20 patients with at least one site without keratinized tissue and loss of vestibular depth after advanced ridge augmentation
f.intervention: Combination graft: apically placed autogenous strip gingival graft plus xenogeneic collagen matrix (Mucograft)
f.main_result: Mean keratinized tissue width at 12 months was 6.33 mm (SD 2.16), with 43% graft contraction.
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by Geistlich Pharma; authors reported no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: No control group, so no firm conclusions could be drawn.

f.population: One 60-year-old edentulous woman with four mandibular interforaminal implants and no keratinized mucosa
f.intervention: Free gingival graft from the palate on the buccal side of the interforaminal area after placing a mandibular fixed implant-supported prosthesis
f.main_result: A 3 mm increase in keratinized mucosa height at 6 months, with good peri-implant health and easier hygiene.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported
f.limitations: The technique involves two surgical sites, causing morbidity in both, and some graft shrinkage is expected.

f.population: 20 partially edentulous patients needing horizontal or vertical bone augmentation in the maxilla
f.intervention: Suspended external-internal (SEI) suture after periosteal release, with flap tension measured by dynamometer
f.comparison: Flap tension before the SEI suture (after periosteal release only), same patients
f.main_result: Mean flap tension fell from 32.9 g to 4.1 g (87.6% reduction) after the SEI suture, and all 20 patients healed uneventfully.
f.sample_size: 20 patients (15 GBR sites, 5 autogenous bone block sites)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: Three patients with Miller class II-IV gingival recessions and small vestibule depth in the frontal mandibular region
f.intervention: Strip free gingival graft with longitudinal division of the donor palatal tissue
f.main_result: Strip free gingival graft gave a mean 4.33 mm gain of attached gingiva, with initial healing complete in two weeks.
f.limitations: The authors only note that results are within the limitations of the three presented cases.

f.population: 10 patients aged 25-30 years with 12 mandibular Miller class I and II recession sites and thin gingival biotype
f.intervention: Single-step free gingival graft with root biomodification (citric acid)
f.main_result: Mean recession depth fell from 3.66 to 0.91 mm (82% root coverage) at 9 months, with attached gingiva rising from 0.33 to 2.92 mm.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: Literature on autologous platelet concentrates in oral and maxillofacial pathologies (in vitro and in vivo studies)
f.intervention: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP), platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) and fibrin adhesives
f.main_result: Evidence on the efficacy of platelet concentrates in the oral and maxillofacial region is controversial and limited.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Medical University Sofia (Grant 42/2015); no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Quality of platelet concentrates varies with donor state and protocols are inconsistent, making outcomes hard to compare.

f.population: Mouse ST2 bone stromal cell line cultured on fibrin sealant
f.intervention: TISSEEL fibrin sealant loaded with rhBMP9 (100 ng/ml)
f.comparison: Tissue culture plastic and TISSEEL alone
f.main_result: TISSEEL retained about 65% of rhBMP9 with slow release over 10 days; TISSEEL plus rhBMP9 raised ALP activity threefold and osteoblast markers versus TISSEEL alone.
f.sample_size: Triplicate wells, three independent experiments per condition
f.funding_coi: Departmental support (Inselspital, Bern); no conflict of interest
f.limitations: In vitro only; animal studies are still needed.

f.population: Blood-derived biomaterials (fibrin sealant, platelet gel, platelet fibrin glue) across surgical fields
f.intervention: Fibrin sealant, platelet gel and platelet fibrin glue: production, properties and clinical uses
f.comparison: Synthetic glues and other biomaterials (qualitative)
f.main_result: Fibrin sealant gives sealing and haemostasis, while platelet gel and platelet fibrin glue release growth factors that support tissue regeneration; all are biocompatible and biodegradable within days to weeks.
f.funding_coi: Two authors are employed by HPPS, a company providing R&D services for this project; others declare none

f.population: 6 mongrel dogs, 18 titanium implants in tibia with a 2.0 mm peri-implant gap
f.intervention: Gap filled with autogenous particulate bone mixed with platelet-enriched fibrin glue
f.comparison: Autogenous particulate bone with PRP, and empty gaps (control)
f.main_result: At 6 weeks bone-implant contact was 59.7% with fibrin glue, 29.2% with PRP and 10.2% in controls (P<.05).
f.funding_coi: Korean Science & Engineering Foundation grant R13-2003-13

f.intervention: Fibrin glue as a tissue adhesive for wound closure in periodontal and oral surgery
f.comparison: Conventional sutures
f.main_result: Fibrin glue is presented as having great potential for periodontal and oral surgery and as a possible alternative to sutures; further clinical trials are needed.
f.limitations: Fibrin sealant cannot be used in people hypersensitive to bovine protein or for massive arterial or venous bleeding.

f.population: 13 patients with partial edentulism, keratinized mucosa under 2 mm or inadequate soft tissue volume, receiving 21 implants
f.intervention: Connective tissue graft at second-stage surgery around implants with BOPT abutments and immediate provisionalization (test group)
f.comparison: Delayed provisionalization (control group)
f.main_result: Both approaches were valid for limited horizontal defects; control soft tissue gain 1.17 mm vs test 0.82 mm, recession change about 0 mm in both groups; sample too small to say which is better.
f.limitations: Preliminary results from a small sample, so it is impossible to assess which option is best.

f.intervention: Geistlich Fibro-Gide collagen matrix for soft-tissue augmentation
f.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Manufacturer claims comparable soft-tissue volume change to connective tissue grafts.

f.population: Patients receiving soft tissue augmentation during implantation or around existing implants
f.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation with a substitute material (xenogeneic collagen matrix or acellular dermal matrix)
f.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Seven RCTs: both CTG and substitutes increased mucosal thickness; five showed no significant difference and two favored CTG.
f.limitations: Methodological quality of included studies was low and heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis.

f.population: Patients with single or multiple Miller I/II gingival recessions treated with coronally advanced flap
f.intervention: Coronally advanced flap plus de-epithelialized gingival graft
f.comparison: Coronally advanced flap plus subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Mean root coverage at 1 year was 89.3% with SCTG and 94.0% with DGG; DGG was modestly better on secondary outcomes (within 1 mm).
f.follow_up: At least 1 year (up to 5 years in two studies)
f.limitations: Limited evidence is available comparing the two techniques.

f.population: 50 Wistar rats with four subcutaneous dorsal pouches each (ectopic model)
f.intervention: Cross-linked (CCM) and non-cross-linked (NCCM) collagen matrices, with or without rhPDGF-BB
f.comparison: Matrices soaked in saline
f.main_result: rhPDGF-BB had no significant effect (all P > 0.05); NCCM stayed 440-570 um thick to 8 weeks then vanished by 16 weeks, while CCM peaked near 2690 um at 2 weeks, lost about 40% by 8 weeks and persisted to 24 weeks.

f.population: 76 patients (mean age 36) with 235 teeth, 136 anterior and 99 posterior, needing full crowns
f.intervention: Monolithic lithium disilicate full crowns bonded to feather-edge preparations
f.main_result: Only 1 of 235 monolithic crowns fractured (a molar after 3 years, in severe parafunction); no biological or technical complications otherwise.
f.follow_up: Recall every 6 months; range given in Table 1 (not in text)
f.limitations: Authors state prospective clinical studies are needed to validate the approach.

f.population: 398 patients with 1,132 zirconia-based single crowns on natural teeth
f.intervention: Porcelain-veneered zirconia single crowns with chamfer or knife-edge preparations
f.comparison: Patients with parafunction versus without
outcomes: USPHS/FDI esthetic, functional and biologic criteria
f.main_result: Cumulative survival 98.1% and success 94.3% over up to 5 years; parafunction raised technical complications (OR 2.60).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Retrospective design with lower level of evidence than RCTs.

f.population: 20 pressed lithium disilicate molar crowns bonded to epoxy resin abutments
f.intervention: Knife-edge finish line abutments
f.comparison: Large chamfer finish line abutments
f.main_result: Finish line did not significantly change fracture strength (KE 1655 N vs LC 1618 N, p = 0.7898).
f.funding_coi: Authors deny conflicts of interest

f.population: 53 patients with 265 veneers, mostly maxillary anterior teeth
f.intervention: Lithium disilicate veneers with a vertical (feather-edge) finish line
f.main_result: Survival 99.63% over a mean 54.4 months; one adhesive failure after trauma; nearly all veneers rated Alfa.
f.funding_coi: Manufacturer gave the authors a positive opinion on the finish line; no funding statement
f.limitations: Authors state further long-term clinical studies are needed.

f.population: 52 patients with posterior mandibular partial edentulism and bone height under 7 mm above the canal
f.intervention: Coronal advancement of the lingual flap by detaching the mylohyoid muscle insertion during vertical GBR
outcomes: maintenance of primary closure for 6 months
f.main_result: Primary closure was maintained in all 69 sites for 6 months; 4 sites (5.8%) failed from infection, 3 of them in smokers.

f.population: 173 GBR-treated sites in 169 patients
f.intervention: A new flap design used with previously described flap designs to maintain primary closure after GBR
outcomes: maintenance of passive primary soft tissue closure for 6 months
f.main_result: 171 of 173 GBR sites maintained primary closure at 6 months (98.8%).

f.population: 47-year-old healthy non-smoking man missing an upper first molar
f.intervention: Buccal peri-implant soft tissue augmentation with a volume-stable porcine collagen matrix and a modified flap
outcomes: marginal bone and soft tissue stability
f.main_result: Single case: the technique gave satisfying functional and esthetic results with marginal bone and soft tissue stability.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Single case

f.population: 60-year-old woman, partially edentulous 24 to 27, with severe maxillary ridge atrophy
f.intervention: Maxillary bone reconstruction with cortical autogenous bone plates harvested from the external oblique ridge with a computer-designed surgical guide
f.main_result: At re-entry and at 6 and 12 months the reconstruction showed volume stability without complications.

f.population: 60 patients scheduled for single implant installation
f.intervention: Measurement of wound closing force with an electronic tension device before suturing
f.main_result: 72% of sites had 0.01-0.1 N tension with 10% dehiscences; higher tension increased dehiscences significantly.

f.population: 38 patients with immediately placed post-extraction implants
f.intervention: Palatal advanced flap, a pedicle flap rotated coronally for primary coverage
f.main_result: Complete primary coverage in all cases, maintained for 6-8 months, with no implant lost over 1-5 years.

f.population: Consecutive cases of vertical GBR in the posterior mandible
f.intervention: Brushing technique to enhance coronal advancement of the buccal flap after periosteal releasing incision
f.main_result: Primary closure over d-PTFE membranes was maintained in 97% of cases.
materials_brands: Cytoplast Ti-250 XL titanium-reinforced d-PTFE membrane
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 5 patients with bilateral atrophic alveolar ridges
f.main_result: Both materials gave equivalent bone gains; horizontal gain 5.8 mm autogenous vs 6.1 mm allogeneic.
f.funding_coi: No funding; first author receives honoraria from Botiss and Straumann
f.limitations: Needs replication in larger studies including a control group without relining

f.intervention: Classification of healing (Class I-IV) and surgical (A-C) complications of GBR with nonresorbable membranes
f.main_result: A classification of GBR complications with nonresorbable membranes is proposed to aid identification and treatment.

f.population: 16 patients with 23 vertical/horizontal ridge defect sites (Seibert Class III)
f.intervention: Double-flap incision (DFI) for flap advancement in GBR
f.comparison: Conventional periosteal releasing incision (PRI)
f.main_result: DFI gave 9.64 mm flap advancement vs 7.13 mm for PRI (P<.001), with lower pain and swelling scores.

f.population: One 61-year-old man with severe vertical and horizontal ridge deformity in the posterior mandible (bilateral)
f.intervention: Double flap incision (separate mucosal and periosteal layers) for tension-free closure over GBR with titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane and allograft
f.main_result: No dehiscence or membrane exposure; 3-5 mm vertical gain and increased horizontal thickness, then two implants per side placed with good primary stability
f.follow_up: 6-8 months of healing before implants; 1 year after loading

f.intervention: Techniques for minor, moderate and major buccal and palatal flap advancement (periosteal scoring, vertical releasing incisions, deeper submucosal release) to achieve tension-free primary closure
f.main_result: Tension-free primary closure is attainable; the technique chosen depends on how far the flap must be advanced, and the simplest adequate technique should be used.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

f.population: 30 patients scheduled for implant surgery with bone augmentation (Seibert Class I deficiency)
f.intervention: Stepwise buccal flap extension: first and second vertical incisions then a periosteal-releasing incision in a trapezoidal flap
f.comparison: Flap length at baseline and after each successive incision; compared by gender, site and operator experience
outcomes: flap extension length (mm, dynamometer at 5 g tension)
f.main_result: First VI +1.1 mm, second VI +1.9 mm, PRI +5.5 mm (171.3% of original length, P<0.001); no differences by gender, site or operator experience

f.intervention: Stepwise periosteal releasing incision (and muscle release) for flap advancement over augmented sites
outcomes: tension-free flap coverage of augmented site
f.main_result: A PRI cut 1-3 mm deep apical to the mucogingival junction, checked for 3-5 mm buccal margin overlap, gives tension-free closure; illustrated clinically without complications at 3 months.

f.population: One patient with a 7 mm vertical deficit in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Proportionally vestibularly shifted (PVS) crestal incision to lengthen the palatal flap at least 4 mm above the graft level, with autogenous block vertical augmentation
f.main_result: With the shifted incision the palatal flap sat about 4 mm coronal to the graft, allowing mattress plus simple sutures for a seal; healing was uneventful for 4 months before implant placement.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 102 participants with a missing mandibular first molar (single-tooth gap), healed site
f.intervention: Flapless (tissue punch) single implant placement with immediate functional loading
f.comparison: Flapped placement (mid-crestal incision with releasing incisions), also immediately loaded
f.main_result: Implant failure was similar; crestal bone loss was higher in flapped than flapless implants at 12 months (1.04 vs 0.90 mm)
f.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

f.population: Systemically healthy patients needing implant placement (14 RCTs)
f.intervention: Flapless implant placement
f.comparison: Flap implant placement
f.main_result: Flapless showed better papilla preservation (PPI WMD 0.32), less 1-day pain and less peri-implant PD; SR, BOP, KM width and CBL were comparable.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Sichuan Science and Technology Department key research program; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: More high-quality, aesthetics-related RCTs are needed

f.population: Patients rehabilitated with dental implants in 23 clinical studies (randomized or not)
f.intervention: Flapless implant surgery
f.comparison: Open flap implant surgery
f.main_result: Flapless surgery had higher implant failure (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.07-2.86, P=0.03), but sensitivity analysis by risk of bias differed; no significant effect on infection or marginal bone loss.
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil); no competing interests
f.limitations: Sixteen studies at high risk of bias; results must be interpreted carefully

f.population: 40 patients, one posterior single interdental implant each, with healthy adjacent teeth
f.intervention: Intrasulcular incision (including adjacent-tooth sulci, no release incisions) for single implant placement
f.comparison: Trapezoidal incision with two release incisions sparing the interproximal tissue
f.main_result: No significant differences between incision types in probing depth, recession or papilla; across the whole sample recession, scar and papilla index changed significantly by 1 year postloading.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 80 patients, 195 implants analysed (no augmentation procedures needed)
f.intervention: Flapless implant insertion (small crestal incision, transmucosal healing)
f.comparison: Implant insertion after full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap
outcomes: peri-implant crestal bone level change at 12 months (radiographic)
f.main_result: Mean bone loss 0.55 mm with flap vs a 0.09 mm gain flapless at 1 year (P<.001)
materials_brands: Dentsply titanium drill sleeves / surgical guide
f.funding_coi: No external support; author later received contributions from Dentsply Implants

f.population: Adult human subjects needing one or more dental implants
f.intervention: Flapless computer-aided fully guided (static or dynamic) implant placement
f.comparison: Flapped conventional implant placement (free-handed or partially guided)
f.main_result: Flapless static fully guided placement improved accuracy versus the planned position and was linked to shorter surgery and less morbidity (very low/low certainty), with about 24 minutes shorter surgery.
f.follow_up: Mostly up to 12 weeks; one trial longer
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Only five RCTs, frequent non-low risk of bias, short follow-up and no long-term clinical outcomes.

f.population: Single dental implants placed immediately in the anterior esthetic region
f.intervention: Immediate interim restoration
f.comparison: No interim restoration / delayed interim restoration
f.main_result: No significant difference in mid-facial mucosal level (MD 0.01 mm), mesial papilla (MD 0.12) or marginal bone loss (MD 0.01) with immediate interim restoration at 12 months; esthetic scores and PROMs improved.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Additional well-designed trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

f.population: Healthy candidates for immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla (39 teeth)
f.intervention: CBCT measurement of labial and palatal bone thickness
f.comparison: Direct caliper measurement after extraction (gold standard)
f.main_result: CBCT overestimated labial bone thickness (0.76 vs 0.50 mm direct); correlation 0.795, ICC 0.840, better when bone exceeded 1 mm.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Immediate implants placed in compromised extraction sockets (buccal plate defect, periapical pathology, periodontal lesion)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in compromised sockets
f.comparison: Noncompromised sockets
f.main_result: Compromised sockets showed no significant difference in implant survival (RR 0.992) or 12-month marginal bone level (MD 0.033) versus noncompromised sockets.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant received
f.limitations: Randomized trials with large samples are still needed for a definite conclusion.

f.population: Patients with maxillary extraction sites (teeth 15-25) scheduled for immediate implants
f.intervention: Intra-operative caliper measurement of buccal and palatal socket wall width, 1 mm apical to the crest
f.comparison: Buccal versus palatal walls, anterior versus premolar sites
outcomes: proportion of walls 2 mm or wider
f.main_result: Mean buccal wall was 1 mm and palatal 1.2 mm; 87% of anterior buccal walls were 1 mm or thinner and only 3% were 2 mm wide.
materials_brands: Astra Tech OsseoSpeed and MicroThread implants

f.population: Two patients with hopeless maxillary anterior teeth (socket class I and II with Miller class I recession)
f.intervention: Marginal Migration Concept protocol: immediate implant, tulip-shaped temporary abutment, membrane and bone replacement graft, immediate provisionalization
f.main_result: The protocol gave esthetically sound results in type I and II sockets with Miller class I recession; tested in over 25 cases with up to 3 years follow-up.
f.funding_coi: No external funding
f.limitations: Prospective randomized controlled trials are needed to evaluate efficacy and validity.

f.population: Five beagle dogs, mandibular fourth premolar distal sockets (10 sites)
f.intervention: Grafting the buccal-approximal void around immediate implants with Bio-Oss Collagen
f.comparison: Contralateral sites without grafting
outcomes: buccal bone crest position and thickness
f.main_result: Grafted sites had a thicker buccal crest at or near the SLA border and better marginal bone-to-implant contact than ungrafted controls after 6 months.

f.population: 33 patients needing anterior maxillary extraction with complete or partial buccal bone plate deficiency
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with porcine xenograft, PRF and exposed collagen membrane, then delayed implant placement
f.main_result: Keratinized mucosa gained 2.3 mm at 5 months (3.2 mm at 1 year), bone level improved by about 0.7-0.8 mm, and no implant failed in 1 year.
f.limitations: Preliminary findings that need confirmation by longer follow-up.

f.population: Single dental implants placed in the anterior maxilla (premolar to premolar)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement and loading protocols and augmentation materials
f.comparison: Early/delayed placement; delayed loading; other augmentation materials
f.main_result: Buccal bone thickness did not differ significantly between immediate, early and delayed placement or between immediate and delayed loading.

f.population: 25 subjects with a maxillary anterior tooth to be extracted and replaced by an implant
f.intervention: New extraction socket classification based on soft and hard tissue parameters
f.main_result: The classification had 96% interobserver agreement (weighted kappa 0.94); 80% of sockets were adequate on soft tissue parameters.

f.population: 100 patients (40 men, 60 women; mean age 53.1 years) with CBCT scans, all maxillary anterior teeth present
f.intervention: Classification of sagittal root position of maxillary anterior teeth relative to the osseous housing (Class I-IV) on CBCT
outcomes: frequency of each sagittal root position class
f.main_result: Of 600 maxillary anterior teeth, 81.1% were Class I, 6.5% Class II, 0.7% Class III and 11.7% Class IV.

f.population: 45 patients (mean age 48 years) receiving single-tooth implants in anterior or premolar regions of maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Early placement of single-tooth implants (about 10 days after extraction), full-thickness flap
f.comparison: Delayed placement 3 months after extraction in 22 patients
f.main_result: After 5 years early and delayed placement were comparable: 3 early/delayed failures before loading, annual bone loss under 0.2 mm, no significant soft tissue differences, high satisfaction.
f.funding_coi: Supported by Biomet 3i
f.limitations: Reproducibility of papilla scores was low, so soft tissue appearance results must be interpreted with caution

f.population: 101 randomly selected patient CBCT scans, 202 healthy maxillary central incisors
f.intervention: CBCT measurement of facial alveolar bone width 1-10 mm apical to the crest
outcomes: prevalence of bone of 2 mm or more
f.main_result: Facial bone of 2 mm or more was found in no more than 3% of teeth at 1-5 mm from the crest; mean thickness was 1.05 mm.
f.funding_coi: University of Southern California periodontology program research funds

f.intervention: Placement of implants in extraction sockets, with a new four-type classification of placement timing (types 1-4)
f.comparison: Immediate (type 1) versus early/delayed (types 2-4) placement
f.main_result: Survival of immediately placed (type 1) implants was reported similar to that of implants in healed ridges (type 4); short-term survival of types 2 and 3 also appears similar.
f.limitations: The adopted classification has not yet been validated, and comparative data are scarce.

f.population: 5 male adult cynomolgus monkeys; buccal aspect of the mandibular angle bilaterally
f.intervention: Titanium mesh over perforated cortical bone covered with an ePTFE membrane (test side)
f.comparison: Titanium mesh without membrane, periosteum-lined flap covering the mesh (control side)
outcomes: percentage of new bone under the mesh
mineralized tissue vs marrow spaces in new and old bone
f.main_result: New bone filled 77.2% of the space on test sides versus 68.6% on control sides (P=0.018); mineralized tissue content did not differ between groups.
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by W.L. Gore & Associates

f.population: 14 adults (2 males, 12 females, mean age 57.1 years) needing immediate implants in the anterior maxilla (incl. premolars) with buccal bone dehiscence of at least 5 mm
f.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement with collagen-enriched bovine xenograft blocks filling the buccal dehiscence and gap, no membrane
f.comparison: Contralateral natural tooth
f.main_result: Buccal wall height at 6-12 months did not differ from the contralateral tooth and exceeded baseline (P<0.01); treated sites had thicker buccal walls and wider ridges than contralateral teeth.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 73 clinical human studies (randomized or not) comparing implants in fresh sockets with healed sites
f.intervention: Dental implants inserted in fresh extraction sockets
f.comparison: Dental implants inserted in healed sites
f.main_result: Implants in fresh sockets had a higher failure rate (RR 1.58, 95% CI 1.27-1.95, P<0.0001); 4.00% vs 3.09%.
f.sample_size: 73 publications: 8,241 implants in sockets and 19,410 in healed sites
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil)
f.limitations: Results should be interpreted with caution due to uncontrolled confounding factors in the included, mostly non-randomized studies

f.population: Adults aged 18 years or older receiving implants, from 10 eligible studies (6 RCTs, 4 non-randomised comparative studies)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh sockets at the time of extraction
f.comparison: Delayed implant placement in healed sites at least two months after extraction
f.main_result: No significant difference in implant survival between immediate and delayed placement (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.96-1.02, p=0.45); 97.4% vs 97.5%.
f.follow_up: Varied by study, from 1 year up to about 10 years
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Some included studies had one-year follow-up and small samples

f.population: 50 patients (22 males, 28 females, age 21-50) with one Miller Class I/II recession each
f.intervention: Coronally advanced flap with de-epithelialized gingival graft (test group)
f.comparison: Coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft harvested by trap-door approach (control)
f.main_result: No differences in post-operative pain or root coverage between CAF+CTG and CAF+DGG (root coverage 96.2% vs 92.3%); the CTG group had lower stress and better chewing, DGG gave greater thickness gain.
f.funding_coi: Self-supported by the authors; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: The lack of difference may reflect considerable within-group variability; larger studies are needed

f.population: Photoelastic model of a partially edentulous left mandible with 3 screw-type implants (3.75 x 10 mm)
f.intervention: Splinted restorations: five cemented 3-unit fixed partial dentures
f.comparison: Non-splinted individual crowns with five levels of interproximal contact tightness (open to heavy)
outcomes: stress distribution under non-loaded and loaded (6.8 kg) conditions
f.main_result: Splinted restorations shared occlusal loads and distributed stress more evenly than non-splinted ones, and heavier interproximal contacts in non-splinted crowns increased tensile stresses between implants.
f.sample_size: 1 model; 5 FPDs and one set of 3 single crowns

f.population: 42 patients with 51 maxillary central incisor sites treated with immediate implant placement and buccal gap grafting
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with the buccal gap grafted with deproteinized bovine bone mineral, grouped by gap width at surgery
f.comparison: Wide gap (>2 mm) versus narrow gap (<=2 mm)
outcomes: buccal and palatal bone wall thickness on CBCT
percentage of implant height covered by bone
position of buccal and palatal bone crests
f.main_result: Buccal bone was thicker with wide gaps (1.9 ± 0.9 mm) than narrow gaps (0.5 ± 0.6 mm), and gap width was the only predictor of buccal wall thickness.
f.sample_size: 51 implants in 42 patients (34 wide gap, 17 narrow gap)
f.follow_up: At least 1 year in function (mean 5 ± 4 years)
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; two authors give lectures sponsored by Geistlich Pharma
f.limitations: Retrospective design, one experienced periodontist, wide follow-up range (1-15 years) with changing techniques, and CBCT implant artifacts.

f.population: Adults with socket defects in the esthetic zone receiving immediate implants (23 studies)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement into defective sockets (with or without flap)
f.main_result: Pooled implant survival was 98.1%, MBL 0.72 mm at 12 months, gingival recession 0.25 mm and PES 12.34 at 12 months.
f.follow_up: At least 12 months with definitive prosthesis
f.funding_coi: Natural Science Foundation of Liaoning Province grant; no other conflicts declared

f.population: Systemically healthy patients with at least one abutment connected to an implant
f.intervention: Any change in abutment material, design or surface manipulation
f.comparison: Any other abutment material, design or surface manipulation
f.main_result: Zirconia abutments showed a smaller BOP increase than titanium (WMD -26.96%, p = .003); other abutment characteristics had no significant effect, except decontamination method on bone loss.
f.follow_up: At least 6 months after implant loading
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Small number of included studies in some comparisons and short follow-up

f.population: 23 consecutive patients (mean age 39.5) with a failing maxillary anterior tooth and a facial bony defect over 3 mm
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization and guided bone regeneration, sites classified by defect shape (V, U, UU)
f.comparison: V-shaped versus U- and UU-shaped facial defects
f.main_result: Implant success was 100% (23/23); facial recession >1.5 mm occurred in 8.3% of V-, 42.8% of U- and 100% of UU-shaped defects.
f.sample_size: 23 implants in 23 patients (12 V, 7 U, 4 UU defects)
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Select / NobelPerfect (TiUnite) implants
f.limitations: Small sample of 23 patients prevented assessment of less dominant factors.

f.population: 20 consecutive patients needing a single anterior maxillary implant (incisor or canine region)
f.intervention: Screw-retained implant-supported provisional crown with soft tissue conditioning (dynamic compression technique) for 6 months before the definitive all-ceramic crown
f.comparison: Definitive crown inserted directly after reopening, without a provisional phase
outcomes: modified pink esthetic score and white esthetic score
f.main_result: Combined modPES and WES were 16.7 with provisional conditioning versus 10.5 without (p = .00044); bone loss was similar (about 0.09 vs 0.08 mm).
f.sample_size: 20 single implants in 20 patients (10 per group)
f.funding_coi: Research grant, study material and financial support from Institut Straumann AG

f.population: Single-tooth implants placed after extraction of maxillary anterior and premolar teeth
f.intervention: Immediate (type 1) and early (types 2/3) implant placement, with or without simultaneous bone augmentation
f.comparison: Immediate versus early implant placement
outcomes: pink esthetic score and other esthetic indices
facial bone wall detectability on CBCT
f.main_result: Immediate placement showed more variable outcomes and recession >1 mm at midfacial mucosa in a median 26% of sites (range 9-41%), versus none in early placement.
f.sample_size: 50 studies (6 RCTs, 6 cohort, 5 cross-sectional, 33 case series)
f.follow_up: 1 to 3 years after placement for trend analysis
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity in study design; no meta-analysis of controlled studies; mostly case series

f.population: Systemically healthy patients with dental implants
f.intervention: Soft tissue grafting to increase keratinized tissue width or mucosal thickness around implants
f.comparison: Implant sites without grafting (or other grafting materials)
f.main_result: Grafting to widen keratinized tissue improved gingival and plaque indices, and connective tissue grafts for thickness gave less marginal bone loss (WMD 0.110 mm); limited evidence supports soft tissue augmentation for peri-implant health.
f.sample_size: 10 studies in the underlying review (6 mucosal thickness, 4 keratinized tissue)
f.funding_coi: Grant of the Osteology Foundation; no conflicts declared, three authors are Foundation board members
f.limitations: Peri-implant disease incidence based on clear case definitions was not sufficiently reported in the studies

f.population: Patients with horizontal alveolar ridge deficiencies
f.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation procedures (simultaneous or staged) before or with implant placement
f.comparison: Different bone regenerative interventions compared with each other
f.main_result: Lateral bone augmentation was associated with stable peri-implant tissues (minimal, non-significant changes in BOP, PD and marginal bone levels) over 1-10 years, without significant differences between interventions.
f.sample_size: 8 studies (12 publications) in the underlying review
f.funding_coi: Grant of the Osteology Foundation; no conflicts declared, three authors are Foundation board members
f.limitations: Case definitions of peri-implant health versus disease were used inconsistently across studies

f.population: Patients receiving flapless maxillary anterior immediate implant placement and provisionalization with scarf-connective tissue graft, min 1-year follow-up
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with simultaneous scarf-connective tissue graft
f.main_result: All 22 implants osseointegrated, mean midfacial gingival level change 0.19 mm was non-significant and midfacial gingival thickness rose from 1.1 mm to 2.5 mm.
f.funding_coi: Authors declared no financial interests in products mentioned

f.population: 40 pig-jaw bone blocks with titanium or zirconia implants and abutments at variable buccal bone thickness
f.intervention: CBCT imaging with two units, two voxel sizes and two reconstruction thicknesses, with 1-3 implants and Ti/Zr combinations
f.comparison: TiTi vs TiZr vs ZrZr implant-abutment; Scanora vs Cranex; 0.2 vs 0.13 mm voxel
outcomes: detectability (conspicuity) of buccal bone condition by three examiners
f.main_result: Zirconia implant-abutment and three implants most impaired buccal bone detection; thinner bone and lower resolution also raised risk, thicker reconstruction helped.
f.sample_size: 40 bone blocks, 80 buccal bone registrations, three examiners
materials_brands: Thommen Medical internal hexagon Ti and Zr implants and abutments

f.population: Forty patients with a failing tooth in the aesthetic zone
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate provisionalization
f.comparison: Immediate placement with delayed provisionalization
f.main_result: Immediate provisionalization was non-inferior for marginal bone level at 1 year (about 0.7 mm loss in both groups).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; unrestricted grant and implant materials from Nobel Biocare Services AG

f.population: 16 beagle dogs, mandibular premolar sockets
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in the distal socket after premolar extraction
f.comparison: Mesial socket left to heal spontaneously
f.main_result: Implant sites showed greater B’L’ distance than controls at 2 and 8 weeks and a 62% reduction in crest width in the test group.
f.follow_up: Five healing periods, up to 8 weeks (2 to 8 weeks reported)
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; partially supported by Biomet 3i research grant

f.population: Subjects with chronic periapical infection of a tooth scheduled for extraction and immediate implant, with intact cervical facial and lingual plates
f.intervention: Extraction, flapless immediate implant placement and provisionalization with perioperative amoxicillin (or clindamycin)
f.comparison: Placebo (sucrose capsule) instead of antibiotic
f.main_result: One implant failed in each group; overall survival 84.7% (87.5% placebo, 80% antibiotic), suggesting antibiotics gave no added benefit.
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by ACP Educational Fund, AAID research grant and unrestricted fund from Zimmer Dental, which supplied implants and abutments
f.limitations: Small sample; authors call for further large-scale trials

f.population: Single missing teeth in the anterior maxilla (aesthetic zone)
f.intervention: Type 1A protocol: immediate implant placement with immediate loading/restoration
f.main_result: Type 1A protocol in the anterior maxilla under favorable conditions is predictable with high survival rates, though complications can occur.
f.sample_size: Underlying review: 43 prospective and 25 retrospective studies, 2531 implants
f.follow_up: Minimum 12 months in included studies (mean 2.6 years)
f.funding_coi: All participants declared no conflicts
f.limitations: Statements rest on studies with highly selective populations

f.population: 18 healthy subjects with 21 extraction sockets (incisors, canines, premolars)
f.intervention: Immediate implant installation in extraction sockets without membrane or filler, flaps repositioned with healing cap exposed
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone wall width
f.main_result: Over 4 months buccal bone width resorbed about 56% and lingual/palatal 30%, while marginal gaps largely resolved by bone fill.
materials_brands: Straumann ITI solid screw implant with SLA surface, 4.1 mm diameter

f.population: One patient with a nonrestorable maxillary left canine
f.intervention: Immediate implant at the palatal aspect of the socket with straight-profile healing abutment, healing by secondary intention, no flap closure, graft or membrane
outcomes: histologic bone-to-implant contact at the buccal wall interface
f.main_result: Biopsy at 10 months showed intimate bone contact to the first thread despite a 4.2 mm gap, with biologic width re-established coronally.
f.follow_up: Loaded at 5 months, biopsied at 10 months

f.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization of maxillary anterior single implants

f.population: 40 patients with hopeless teeth needing extraction and immediate implants (42 sites, maxilla and mandible, anterior and lateral)
f.intervention: Atraumatic extraction, immediate tissue-level implant, socket filled with PRGF and/or deproteinized bovine bone, covered by collagen membrane or cyanoacrylate and left exposed (open healing)
f.main_result: Open healing gave uneventful healing with 100% survival and 95.2% success at 4 years, with no differences in crestal bone stability between augmentation materials.
materials_brands: TRI Octa tissue-level implant (TRI Dental Implants)

f.population: Eight beagle dogs, 32 implants in fresh extraction sockets of mandibular premolars
f.intervention: Immediate placement of four commercial implant systems (3i Osseotite Certain, Astra MicroThread OsseoSpeed, Thommen SPI Element, Straumann ITI standard) into fresh extraction sockets
f.comparison: The four implant systems compared with each other
f.main_result: At 6 weeks the biological width comprised 2-2.7 mm junctional epithelium and 1-1.8 mm connective tissue, with no significant differences among the four systems.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared

f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh extraction sockets (type-1 protocol)
f.main_result: Survival, osseointegration and interdental bone levels are not negatively affected by immediate placement, but buccal bone resorption is variable and esthetic/soft-tissue data are limited.
f.limitations: Scarce data on biological complications because of the lack of long-term studies.

f.population: 5 patients scheduled for extraction of remaining teeth (severe chronic periodontitis); 10 immediate implants, 7 retrieved for histology
f.intervention: SLA titanium implants placed into extraction sockets and completely covered with a connective tissue (resorbable collagen) membrane with primary closure
f.comparison: Horizontal defect dimension 0.0-1.5 mm as controls versus 1.5-4.0 mm and >4.0 mm
outcomes: vertical distance to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: Osseointegration occurred across all HDDs; bone-to-implant contact was 69.29% (0-1.5 mm), 39.37% (1.5-4.0 mm) and 64.72% (>4.0 mm).
f.funding_coi: Funds from the first and second authors and in part an ITI Foundation grant
f.limitations: It remains undetermined which of membrane type, membrane placement or implant surface was responsible; further study needed.

f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in the aesthetic zone
f.main_result: Guiding and maintaining extra bone and soft tissue volume around implants is key to long-term esthetics, to compensate for the lack of a periodontal ligament.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Clinical studies (trials, cohorts, case-control, case reports of at least 10 cases) on immediate and delayed implants after extraction
f.intervention: Immediate and delayed (early) implant placement following tooth extraction
f.comparison: Immediate versus delayed placement, and implants in healed ridges
f.main_result: Short-term survival and clinical outcomes of immediate and delayed implants were similar and comparable to implants in healed ridges.
f.follow_up: At least 12 months for survival/success studies
f.limitations: Most studies were short-term and not randomized with respect to timing of placement and augmentation methods.

f.population: 32 patients with hopeless maxillary premolars (25 analysed) in three private clinics
f.intervention: Immediate definitive platform-switched abutment never disconnected (one abutment-one time)
f.comparison: Provisional abutment later replaced by definitive abutment
f.main_result: 100% success in both groups at 3 years; marginal bone loss 0.34 mm (definitive abutment) versus 0.55 mm (provisional abutment), significantly lower with the definitive abutment.
f.sample_size: 25 patients analysed (10 PA, 15 DA) after 7 exclusions
f.funding_coi: No financial interest in the products listed

f.population: 124 subjects needing single anterior or premolar tooth extraction, seven private practices
f.intervention: Immediate placement of tapered Thommen SPI Contact implants at extraction, with Bio-Oss and Bio-Gide when needed
f.comparison: Delayed placement after 12 weeks of socket healing
f.main_result: Immediate placement needed more augmentation (72% vs 43.9%), had more wound failure (26.1% vs 5.3%), deeper probing depth and inadequate pink esthetic score in 42% vs 19% of cases.
f.funding_coi: ERGOPerio; partly an unrestricted grant from Thommen Medical AG; materials from Geistlich
f.limitations: Longer follow-up is needed to assess differences in complication rates.

f.population: 81 patients in three private practices (27 single, 27 partial, 27 full-arch)
f.intervention: Immediate (within 48 h) and early (6 weeks) loading of implant prostheses
f.comparison: Conventional (delayed) loading at 3 months
f.main_result: No implant or prosthesis failed and no complications occurred in any group up to 4 months post-loading.
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by MegaGen, which did not interfere with conduct or publication
f.limitations: Limited sample size, too low to detect a significant difference; protocol deviations.

f.population: 210 patients needing a single implant-supported crown to replace a tooth to be extracted
f.intervention: Immediate and immediate-delayed (6 weeks) post-extractive single implants
f.comparison: Delayed implants after 4 months of healing
f.main_result: Implant failures were 6%, 6.2% and 1.6% (not significant); marginal bone loss was 0.25, 0.29 and 0.31 mm; esthetic scores were higher with immediate and immediate-delayed placement.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare implants (manufacturer of the implants evaluated)
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by Nobel Biocare Services, manufacturer of the implants
f.limitations: Limited sample size despite being the largest RCT on implant timing.

f.population: Mandibular premolar extraction sockets of four fresh-frozen human cadavers
f.intervention: Immediate placement of ITI TE and solid screw implants (4.1 and 4.8 mm) into fresh extraction sockets
f.comparison: TE implant versus 4.1 mm and 4.8 mm solid screw implants
f.main_result: The TE implant had higher ISQ than the 4.1 mm implant (P<0.01) and values comparable to the 4.8 mm implant.
f.sample_size: Four cadavers (number of implants not stated in extracted text)
f.limitations: The clinical value of radiographic analysis is a matter of debate.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients treated with implant-supported fixed prostheses
f.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement combined with immediate, early or conventional loading
f.comparison: Late placement and conventional loading
f.main_result: Weighted cumulative survival was 98.4% (Type 1A), 98.2% (1B) and 96.0% (1C) for immediate placement, with the loading protocol influencing outcome of immediate placement
f.funding_coi: Supported by Harvard department and ITI Foundation; authors declare no conflict of interests
f.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity in study design prevented meta-analysis of controlled studies

f.population: 20 patients needing immediate implants in fresh extraction sockets (second premolar to second premolar)
f.intervention: Internal grafting only of the peri-implant gap when implant-to-buccal-plate distance (I-BP) was below 4 mm (group A)
f.comparison: Internal plus external grafting (IEG) in group B
outcomes: buccal and palatal contour change by superimposed optical scans
f.main_result: After 1 year of loading, buccal volume decreased slightly in group A and increased in group B (P=0.02), with higher IAS in group B
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Studies with a larger sample size are needed to confirm the outcome

f.population: Patients with compromised teeth to be extracted who required dental implants, with or without bone augmentation
f.intervention: Immediate (same-day) and immediate-delayed (within 8 weeks) implants in fresh extraction sockets
f.comparison: Delayed implants placed at least 2 months after extraction
f.sample_size: 7 randomised trials included of 14 potentially eligible
f.follow_up: at least 1 year under functional loading

f.main_result: An ideal implant position in all 3 dimensions is required, defining comfort and danger zones in the anterior maxilla

f.population: Humans with periodontal intra-bony defects (comparative trials, at least eight defects, follow-up of 6 months or more)
f.intervention: rhPDGF-BB or rhFGF-2 applied to intra-bony defects
f.comparison: Carrier alone
f.main_result: PDGF gave significantly more linear defect fill (0.95 mm) and CAL gain (0.34 mm) than carriers alone, and FGF-2 more percentage defect fill (21.22%)
f.funding_coi: Two authors are research investigators for a trial supported by Sunstar Corp.; no external funding
f.limitations: Only one included study was at low risk of bias

f.population: 20 patients with a terminal maxillary dentition (fully edentulous maxilla)
f.intervention: Immediate placement of six implants per maxilla with immediate loading by a fibre-reinforced temporary fixed prosthesis
f.comparison: Implants in fresh extraction sockets versus healed edentulous sites
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone level was -0.35 mm 18 months after loading, with no significant effect of extraction-socket versus healed placement; survival 100%
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: Patients treated with single implants in different locations
f.intervention: Immediate or early placement and loading protocols (Types 1A to 4B)
f.comparison: Conventional placement and loading protocol
f.main_result: The anterior maxilla was the most reported site (35 studies, 1,391 implants, weighted survival 97.5% to 99.6%), with Types 1C and 4A validated there
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Meta-analysis was not possible because few controlled studies had the same comparison

f.population: 591 maxillary anterior teeth on CBCT scans from 150 patients
f.intervention: Classification of tooth position and inclination in the alveolus (classes I to V) with facial and palatal bone wall measurement
outcomes: facial and palatal bone wall thickness
f.main_result: Thin facial bone predominated at the crest (83%) and mid-root (92%), and class II (retroclined) was the most common position (76.5%)

f.population: Patients with a single failing tooth or single tooth gap in the anterior maxilla (IIT cohort 16 treated, CIT cohort 23 treated)
f.intervention: Immediately restored single implant (Astra Tech OsseoSpeed) placed in an extraction socket (IIT)
f.comparison: Immediately restored single implant placed in a healed ridge (CIT)
outcomes: buccal bone and soft tissue thickness on CBCT
f.main_result: After at least 8 years a buccal bone wall under 2 mm was found at all implant sites and under 1 mm at 42%, while vertical soft tissue levels and PES stayed stable.
f.sample_size: 11 IIT and 18 CIT patients evaluated of 16 and 23 initially treated
materials_brands: Astra Tech Implant System OsseoSpeed (Dentsply Sirona Implants)
f.funding_coi: Departmental funds and Dentsply Sirona Implants; Prof. De Bruyn has a research collaboration agreement with Dentsply Sirona, Prof. Cosyn with Nobel Biocare
f.limitations: Limited sample size and subjective PES scoring may have hidden differences; CBCT rarely taken before placement.

f.population: 60 healthy adults (26 thin biotype, 34 thick/average) with maxillary anterior teeth (360 teeth)
f.intervention: Clinical classification of periodontal biotype correlated with CBCT labial plate thickness, crest position and other clinical measures
f.comparison: Thin versus thick/average periodontal biotype
outcomes: labial plate thickness at 4, 6, 8, 10 mm from CEJ
f.main_result: A thin biotype had thinner labial plate (P<.001, roughly half the thickness, 0.3 to 0.5 mm less), narrower keratinized tissue and greater CEJ-to-crest distance, with probe visible in 84% of thin-biotype teeth vs 7%.
f.limitations: Only 6.1% of teeth had recession so recession results need caution; tooth malposition may influence measurements.

f.population: Ten freshly frozen unembalmed human head and neck cadaver specimens (edentulous maxillae and fresh maxillary extraction sockets)
f.intervention: Implant placement after bone condensation with an electrical mallet, late (edentulous) or immediate (fresh socket)
f.comparison: Contralateral sites without condensation, placed per manufacturer drilling protocol
f.main_result: Torque and ISQ correlated in edentulous jaws in both untreated (r=0.63) and condensed bone (r=0.82), but in extraction sockets only in untreated bone (r=0.78), not condensed (r=0.15).
f.sample_size: 10 specimens; 26 implants in edentulous jaws and 29 in extraction sockets
f.funding_coi: No funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Low sample size, implants removed before measuring postoperative BV/TV, and high donor age.

f.population: Five beagle dogs, mandibular third and fourth premolar extraction sockets
f.intervention: Implant (Straumann SLA) placed in fresh extraction sockets of distal roots
f.comparison: Contralateral extraction sockets left for spontaneous healing
outcomes: bone crest level relative to SLA margin
vertical distance between buccal and lingual bone walls
f.main_result: At 3 months the buccal bone crest was 2.6 mm apical of the SLA level at implants; at edentulous sites buccal and lingual walls differed vertically by 2.2 mm, so implant placement did not prevent socket-wall remodelling.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Implant, SLA surface, 4.1 mm diameter, 6-8 mm long

f.population: 39 patients needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla after inevitable tooth extraction
f.intervention: Flapless tooth extraction with collagen sponge in the socket, with two consecutive CBCTs (baseline and 8 weeks) analysed in 3D
outcomes: vertical and horizontal facial bone loss
facial bone wall thickness at baseline
f.main_result: Central sites showed median vertical bone loss of 5.2 mm; thin-wall phenotypes (<=1 mm) lost a median 7.5 mm versus 1.1 mm for thick-wall phenotypes.
f.sample_size: 39 patients (29 central incisors, 8 lateral incisors, 2 canines)
f.funding_coi: Supported by the ITI Foundation; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Only anterior maxillary sites and an eight-week healing period, so results apply only to esthetic-zone extraction sites.

f.population: Six male Beagle dogs; maxillary first premolar fresh sockets with surgically created buccal bone defects (4x4x5 mm)
f.intervention: Sockets filled with tunnel structured beta-TCP blocks
f.comparison: Extraction alone, no graft (contralateral control sites)
outcomes: alveolar ridge width at coronal, middle, apical levels
woven bone, connective tissue, bone marrow percentages
f.main_result: Ridge width at coronal and middle levels was greater at test sites (3.2 and 3.6 mm) than controls (1.2 and 2.0 mm), with more woven bone (62.4% vs 26.8%).
f.sample_size: 6 Beagle dogs, bilateral defects (test vs control)
materials_brands: Tunnel structured beta-tricalcium phosphate (beta-TCP) blocks, about 70% porosity
f.funding_coi: Supported by Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (KAKENHI 23792465); no conflicts of interest

f.population: Five beagle dogs, third mandibular premolar sockets
f.intervention: Bio-Oss Collagen (90% deproteinized bovine bone, 10% porcine collagen) placed in the fresh extraction socket
f.comparison: Contralateral ungrafted socket (blood clot)
outcomes: tissue composition (woven bone, lamellar bone, marrow, graft particles)
f.main_result: After 6 months the alveolar process dimension and ridge profile were better preserved at Bio-Oss Collagen sites (marginal reduction three times smaller than ungrafted), but the graft did not enhance new bone formation.

f.population: Forty patients with 71 Miller class I and II gingival recessions
f.intervention: Modified microsurgical tunnel technique (MMTT) with connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Coronally advanced flap (CAF) with connective tissue graft
f.main_result: At 12 months root coverage was 98.3% for CAF and 97.2% for MMTT with no significant difference; both gave high aesthetic scores (RES about 9.2).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; no funding other than the department's own

f.population: Patients needing single tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla (15-25 FDI)
f.intervention: Type 1A protocol: immediate implant placement with immediate loading, grouped by site selection criteria
f.comparison: Immediate placement and loading without one or more site-specific selection criteria
f.main_result: Weighted mean survival of Type 1A single implants in the maxillary esthetic zone was 97.7%; pre-2012 studies had lower survival (-1.9 PP), as did facial gaps and endodontic infection groups.
f.sample_size: 68 articles included from 3118 identified (mean 37.2 implants per study)
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Heterogeneity in study duration, no multivariate analysis possible, English-only search, and inclusion of lower-quality case series with inherent risk of bias.

f.population: 90 consecutive patients (50 female, 40 male, 18-69 years) scheduled for periodontal or peri-implant plastic surgery requiring palatal mucosal graft harvesting
f.intervention: Free palatal mucosal graft harvesting with patient-reported pain (VAS) recorded postoperatively
f.main_result: Pain peaked on day 1 and declined; thicker grafts increased pain while thicker palatal mucosa reduced it, and wound surface area had no effect
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; supported by the Clinical Research Foundation (CRF), Brienz, Switzerland

f.population: 20 participants with a single edentulous gap in the anterior maxilla receiving an implant-supported crown (commented trial)
f.intervention: Screw-retained implant-supported provisional crown conditioning soft tissue for 6 months before the definitive crown
f.comparison: Definitive crown placed immediately without provisional phase
f.main_result: At 3 years the provisional-crown group had a mean total pink esthetic score 2.6 points higher; only mesial and distal papilla differed significantly; white esthetic score did not differ
materials_brands: Bone Level Implant, RC, SLActive, Straumann
f.funding_coi: Commentary author reported no disclosures
f.limitations: Small number of participants, which may explain missing significance or suggest chance findings

f.population: Three consecutive cases of single failing anterior maxillary teeth (e.g. vertical root fracture of a central incisor)
f.intervention: Socket seal surgery with a free gingival graft combined with immediate, early or delayed implant placement
f.main_result: Healing occurred without complication and soft tissue stability was confirmed at 2 years in case 1
f.limitations: Technique is skill sensitive and increases treatment time and number of procedures

f.population: Maxillary front teeth situated close to the buccal plate in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Socket transformation: buccal concavity grafting with elective root canal and apicectomy, then extraction and immediate implant months later
f.main_result: Socket transformation is proposed as feasible for suitable cases but may not always solve long-term esthetic problems in Type B3 cases
f.limitations: Further clinical studies are needed to evaluate long-term bony and soft tissue stability

f.population: One patient with a horizontally fractured maxillary central incisor (tooth No. 9)
f.intervention: Atraumatic flapless extraction, immediate implant with bone graft in the buccal gap and screw-retained provisional as prosthetic socket seal
f.main_result: At 6 months bone levels around the platform-switched implant were good and there was little to no contour difference versus the untreated contralateral tooth

f.population: Adult patients in need of a single implant
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement (IIP)
f.comparison: Delayed single implant placement (>=3 months post-extraction)
f.main_result: Implant survival was lower for IIP (94.9%) than DIP (98.9%), RR 0.96; probing depth and pink esthetic score were similar
f.sample_size: 3 RCTs and 5 non-randomized studies, 473 single implants (IIP 233, DIP 240)
f.limitations: One RCT had unclear risk of bias and all other studies high risk of bias

f.population: 420 maxillary anterior teeth in 70 participants with CBCT scans
f.intervention: CBCT classification of sagittal root position (classes I-IV) and measurement of bone housing
f.main_result: Class distribution was 65.2%, 9.3%, 0.7% and 24.8% for classes I-IV; bone housing measurements differed between classes except alveolar ridge height
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by CAPES, Brazil (Finance Code 001)

f.intervention: Immediate placement of implants into fresh extraction sockets (literature through December 1996)
f.comparison: Delayed implantation after socket healing
f.main_result: Implants in fresh sockets showed survival of 93.9% to 100%; no consensus on gap filling, membranes not better and exposure may cause complications

f.population: 22 fresh cadaver heads, maxillary anterior teeth (#6-#11)
f.intervention: Clinical caliper and CBCT measurement of labial/palatal gingival and bone thickness
f.comparison: Clinical measurements versus CBCT measurements
f.main_result: CBCT and clinical thickness did not differ except palatal soft tissue; labial gingival thickness was moderately associated with bone thickness (R = 0.429)

f.population: Systemically healthy patients requiring a single immediate post-extraction implant in the maxillary esthetic zone
f.intervention: Surgical modifications during IIP: connective tissue grafts, bone grafts, flapless surgery, palatal implant positioning
f.comparison: IIP without the individual surgical modifications
outcomes: horizontal and vertical soft and hard tissue changes
f.main_result: Connective tissue grafts improved facial gingival level (MD -0.51 mm) and bone grafts reduced horizontal buccal bone resorption (MD -0.59 mm); flapless and palatal positioning gave no significant gains
f.limitations: Additional longitudinal studies are required

f.population: Patients needing tooth extraction and implant replacement (evidence mostly from single-tooth extraction)
f.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation/bone grafting, immediate, early and delayed implant placement, and bone augmentation at implant placement
f.comparison: Unassisted socket healing (for ridge preservation); different implant placement timings against each other
f.main_result: The group formulated 23 consensus statements and 12 clinical recommendations; ridge preservation via socket grafting may prevent 1.5-2.4 mm horizontal and 1-2.5 mm vertical mid-buccal resorption versus extraction alone
f.sample_size: 25 articles from 22 RCTs in the ridge preservation review
f.funding_coi: Participants declared research funding/consultancy from several implant and biomaterial companies (e.g. Straumann, Geistlich)
f.limitations: None of the RCTs in the ridge preservation review had low risk of bias

f.population: 20 patients (8 men, 12 women) with one missing tooth distal to the canine and a shallow buccal bone dehiscence
f.intervention: Transmucosal implant placement with submarginal connective tissue graft covering the dehiscence
f.main_result: Buccal soft tissue thickness and vertical soft tissue level improved significantly at 6 months, 1 and 3 years, with no recession, no significant marginal bone loss and no mucositis or peri-implantitis
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Case series design; RCTs comparing bone augmentation with submarginal CTG are needed

f.population: Postextraction sites in the esthetic zone requiring implant therapy
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate prosthetics, alveolar ridge preservation, early or delayed placement with bone augmentation, socket shield
f.main_result: For an intact alveolus, immediate placement with immediate prosthetics is the reference choice if primary stability and the buccal bone plate are present; a compromised alveolus favors staged placement with augmentation
f.funding_coi: Funded by the non-profit Fondazione Giuseppe Cardaropoli; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Expert-opinion based; socket shield technique lacks well-designed prospective controlled studies

f.population: Patients needing extraction of maxillary anterior teeth with immediate implant placement (three clinical examples)
f.intervention: Eight-step protocol: provisional on tooth to be extracted, atraumatic extraction, guided placement, >35 Ncm stability, 3D bone packing, custom abutment, provisional reline, tuberosity CTG
f.main_result: Case examples with up to 13 years follow-up showed stable buccal bone where bone graft was packed into the gap, and resorption where no graft was used

f.population: Patients with early implant placement and contour augmentation in the esthetic zone (case series of 20 implants)
f.intervention: Early implant placement with contour augmentation using autogenous bone chips, DBBM particles and a collagen membrane
outcomes: facial bone wall thickness on CBCT
f.main_result: At 6 years all 20 implants had a visible facial bone wall with mean thickness about 1.9 mm; one implant (5%) was at risk with a thin wall and slight recession

f.population: Single implant sites with horizontal ridge defects treated with GBR
f.intervention: Periosteal vertical mattress suture with resorbable sutures to fix the collagen membrane and stabilize particulate graft
f.comparison: Fixation with pins or osteosynthesis screws (discussed, not tested)
f.main_result: Authors report a low rate of dehiscence and good bone regeneration in their clinical experience with the technique
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Limited by tensile strength and resorption time of the suture; not enough stability for multiple missing teeth

f.intervention: Transfer soft tissue contours of an interim implant restoration to the definitive cast using gingival contour elastomer material
materials_brands: Zimmer Dental healing abutment and impression post
ResinRock Type IV dental stone (Whip Mix)

f.population: 12 single implant sites in the maxillary esthetic zone of 10 participants
f.intervention: Intraoral scans at 0 seconds to 20 minutes after removal of the interim restoration
f.comparison: Scan with the interim restoration in place (baseline)
f.main_result: After removal, papilla height fell up to 0.27 mm at 20 minutes and emergence profile discrepancy was significant immediately and increased over time
f.funding_coi: Foundation of State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases, Sichuan University

f.population: Humans undergoing tooth extraction (20 included studies)
f.intervention: Tooth extraction with undisturbed healing
outcomes: horizontal and vertical hard tissue change
f.main_result: At 6 months horizontal hard tissue reduction (3.79 mm) exceeded vertical reduction (1.24 mm buccal); re-entry studies showed horizontal bone loss of 29-63% and vertical 11-22%
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: Five Beagle dogs, four immediate implants each in the lower jaw
f.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement
f.comparison: Flap surgery (control side)
f.main_result: Bone-implant contact was similar (64.8% vs 65.1%); buccal mucosa-to-bone distance was 3.02 mm flapless vs 3.69 mm flap (significant), buccal bone crest 0.82 vs 1.33 mm apical to SLA level (not significant)
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Straumann Iberian; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Animal model with implants well within the socket

f.population: 46 patients (31 women, 15 men) referred for extraction of a maxillary or mandibular premolar or molar before single-tooth implant treatment
f.intervention: Single-tooth extraction of a premolar or molar, then 12 months of healing without prostheses (in 44 of 46) with clinical and radiographic evaluation
outcomes: alveolar ridge width and height on study casts
adjacent tooth pocket depth and attachment level
f.main_result: Ridge width fell about 50% (12.0 to 5.9 mm), two thirds of it in the first 3 months; height changes were under 1 mm.
f.limitations: Subtraction radiography was limited: 11 patients excluded because of reference-point or alignment problems, and radiographic magnification means measurements are approximate.

f.population: Eight adult beagle dogs; third and fourth mandibular premolar sockets
f.intervention: Immediate placement of one of four implant systems (3i Osseotite, Astra OsseoSpeed, Thommen SPI Element, Straumann ITI) in the distal socket of extracted premolars
f.comparison: Adjacent mesial sockets left to heal spontaneously
outcomes: relative vertical buccal bone loss versus lingual crest
absolute buccal bone loss at implant sites
woven bone area in healing sockets
f.main_result: Relative buccal bone resorption was similar at implant and control sites; absolute buccal bone loss at implant sites was 2.32 mm (SD 0.36).
f.sample_size: 8 dogs; 32 implant sites and 32 edentulous sites
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; supported by a research grant from Thommen Medical
f.limitations: The limitations of the histological evaluation method preclude a definite conclusion.

f.population: Five 1-year-old beagle dogs; third and fourth mandibular premolar fresh extraction sockets
f.intervention: Small-diameter (3.25 mm) implants placed in fresh extraction sockets of hemisected premolars with the neck at the buccal bone crest, submerged healing
outcomes: distance from implant shoulder to buccal and lingual bone crest
