f.main_result: Mean vertical buccal bone resorption was 0.5 mm; buccal crest 0.8 mm and lingual -0.3 mm from the implant shoulder at 12 weeks, and buccolingual crest width fell from 4.5 to 3.5 mm.
f.follow_up: 15 days to 3 months (assessments at 2, 4 and 12 weeks)

f.population: 17 molars extracted because of advanced periodontitis in patients planned for implant-retained replacement
f.intervention: Minimally invasive flapless molar extraction with natural healing, CBCT at baseline and 6 months
outcomes: horizontal ridge width change at -1, -3, -5 mm
vertical ridge height change at nine points
f.main_result: After 6 months the central buccal crest width fell 0.59 mm (maxilla) and 0.72 mm (mandible) at -1 mm, with no significant volumetric bone loss in either jaw.
f.funding_coi: Capital Medical Development and Research Fund and Capital foundation for Clinical Characteristics and Application Research; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Small sample size with limited statistical power, no correction for multiple tests in this pilot study.

f.main_result: Thin facial bone walls (1 mm or less) lose a median 7.5 mm (62%) of facial bone height by 8 weeks versus 1.1 mm (9%) for thick walls.

f.population: 45 adult patients needing an immediate implant to replace a maxillary premolar with sufficient buccal bone
f.intervention: Immediate implant with open flap and bone grafting (flap-graft)
f.comparison: Open flap without grafting (flap-nograft) and flapless without grafting (noflap-nograft)
outcomes: CBCT buccal bone dimensions at apical, medial and bevel levels
f.main_result: Treatment technique had no relevant effect on bone outcomes; the three techniques nearly filled the marginal gap (residual vertical gap 0.27 mm, horizontal 0.5 mm) and noflap-nograft was less painful.
f.sample_size: 45 patients, one implant each (15 per arm), one lost to follow-up
f.funding_coi: Implants supplied by Bone System; other costs self-funded; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: CBCT cannot confirm osseointegration quality or soft tissue changes, applies only to maxillary premolar sites with an intact facial wall, and follow-up was only 6 months.

f.population: Twelve mongrel dogs, mandibular 3rd and 4th premolar extraction sites
f.intervention: Hemi-sectioning of 3rd and 4th mandibular premolars and removal of the distal roots, sites covered with mobilized gingiva, histology at 1, 2, 4 and 8 weeks
outcomes: height of buccal and lingual bone walls
width of bone walls at 1, 3 and 5 mm below the crest
f.main_result: Marked dimensional alterations occurred in the first 8 weeks, with bone wall height reduced more on the buccal than the lingual side in two overlapping resorption phases.
Four systematic reviews showed mean ridge reduction of 3.8 mm in width and 1.24 mm in height within 6 months; immediate implants give high survival but a high recession risk in esthetic sites.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 20 consecutively enrolled patients with a single-tooth gap in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Flapless extraction, 4-8 weeks soft-tissue healing, early placement of a bone-level SLActive implant with simultaneous contour augmentation (autogenous chips, DBBM, collagen membrane)
outcomes: clinical parameters (plaque, bleeding, probing depth, keratinized mucosa)
facial bone wall thickness on CBCT
f.main_result: At 6 years all 20 implants were integrated with mean DIB 0.44 mm, and all had a detectable facial bone wall (mean thickness 1.06 to 1.93 mm).
f.funding_coi: Departmental funds of Bern and Geneva universities and a research grant from Institut Straumann AG; one author is consultant to the cited companies

f.population: Six beagle dogs; mandibular third premolar and first molar fresh extraction sockets
f.intervention: Immediate placement of Straumann standard implants (4.1 mm wide, 6 or 8 mm long) in fresh extraction sockets of distal roots, semi-submerged healing
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone wall width at 1, 2 and 3 mm
marginal level of bone crest and bone-to-implant contact relative to the implant surface
f.main_result: Implant placement failed to preserve ridge dimensions: both buccal and lingual walls were resorbed, with more bone loss at molar than premolar sites and some marginal loss of osseointegration buccally.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Implant, SLA surface, 4.1 mm

f.population: 20 Labrador dogs with mandibular premolars extracted and 3 months healed
f.intervention: Four c.p. titanium ITI implants per animal placed non-submerged with mucosa sutured to the implant, biopsies from day 0 to 12 weeks of healing
outcomes: histological composition of the peri-implant soft tissue over time
epithelial proliferation and barrier epithelium maturation
f.main_result: A mature barrier epithelium occurred after 6-8 weeks and collagen fibers were organized after 4-6 weeks; the soft-tissue barrier developed its final characteristics within 6 weeks.
f.follow_up: Healing periods from day 0 (2 h) to 12 weeks
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (Straumann), 4.1 mm solid screw implants
f.funding_coi: Supported by an ITI Foundation research program grant

f.population: Adult human subjects (>18 years) undergoing single tooth extraction, excluding mandibular incisors and third molars (28 included studies)
f.intervention: Standard-of-care tooth extraction with unassisted socket healing
outcomes: horizontal and vertical (mid-facial, mid-lingual) ridge reduction
f.main_result: Pooled clinical horizontal ridge reduction in non-molar sites was 2.73 mm, with greater reduction in molar sites (3.61 mm radiographic horizontal).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts; supported by University of Iowa Periodontics Graduate Student Research Fund

f.population: Patients needing a single anterior maxillary tooth extraction (canine to canine) with thin or thick facial bone wall; 33 analysed
f.intervention: Flapless extraction with collagen sponge in the socket, healing monitored over 8 weeks by sequential digitized impressions and CBCT superimposition
f.comparison: Thin (<1 mm) versus thick facial bone wall phenotype
outcomes: facial soft tissue thickness at extraction and 8 weeks
vertical and horizontal soft tissue and bone loss
f.main_result: In thin bone phenotypes facial soft tissue thickness rose from 0.7 to 5.3 mm over 8 weeks, so vertical soft tissue loss was only 1.6 mm versus 7.5 mm of vertical bone loss; thick phenotypes were unchanged.
f.funding_coi: Supported by the ITI Foundation; no conflicts declared

f.population: 35 patients with a single maxillary molar extraction
f.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation after maxillary molar extraction
f.comparison: Spontaneous healing
outcomes: crestal, buccal and palatal gingival thickness at 6 months
f.main_result: Crestal gingiva was thinner in ARP (2.17 mm) than spontaneous healing (3.33 mm), and buccal/palatal gingiva at implant shoulder were also thinner with ARP (p<0.05); MGJ change was similar.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Osteology Foundation (grant 16-048); no conflicts of interest

f.population: CBCT scans of patients referred for implant therapy in the anterior maxilla (125 scans, 498 teeth from first premolar to first premolar)
f.intervention: Measurement of facial bone wall thickness on sagittal CBCT slices at crest level (MP1) and mid-root (MP2)
outcomes: facial bone wall thickness at MP1 and MP2
frequency of missing, thin (<1 mm) and thick (>=1 mm) walls
effect of age, sex and tooth position
f.main_result: The facial bone wall was missing in 25.7% of teeth at MP1 and thin (<1 mm) in 62.9%, with only 11.4% >=1 mm; thickness decreased from premolars to incisors.
materials_brands: Morita 3D Accuitomo XYZ Slice View Tomograph

f.population: Human subjects undergoing tooth extraction (12 included publications, 7 to 46 subjects each)
f.intervention: Tooth extraction with post-extraction healing
outcomes: mid-buccal, mid-crestal and mid-lingual height change
f.main_result: Alveolar ridge width reduced by 3.87 mm, with mean clinical mid-buccal height loss of 1.67 mm; loss in width exceeded loss in height.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; self-funded

f.population: Nine periodontal patients with pockets to or beyond the mucogingival junction (7 surgically re-evaluated, 21 teeth per flap type)
f.intervention: Apically repositioned partial thickness flap
f.comparison: Apically repositioned full thickness flap on the opposite side of the arch
outcomes: crestal radicular alveolar bone height loss
f.main_result: Mean crestal bone loss was 0.62 mm after full thickness and 0.98 mm after partial thickness flaps, both significant, with greater loss after partial thickness (p<.01).
f.sample_size: 9 patients (7 surgically re-evaluated), 21 teeth per flap type

f.population: One 32-year-old healthy non-smoking male with a lost upper-right central incisor and horizontal and vertical soft tissue deficiency
f.intervention: NobelReplace CC PMC 3.5 x 13 mm implant with Slim Healing Abutment and palatal connective tissue graft placed simultaneously, then NobelProcera ASC abutment with zirconia crown
f.main_result: After three months of healing the soft tissue had grown vertically and horizontally and the contour developed correctly; final restoration placed at six months.
materials_brands: Slim Healing Abutment CC NP 7 mm
NobelProcera ASC Abutment with zirconia crown
f.funding_coi: Manufacturer-published case (Nobel Biocare products)

f.population: Patients with a tooth extracted in the esthetic zone who received immediate implant placement
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with simultaneous or delayed connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement without connective tissue graft
f.main_result: In four RCTs the mean buccal gingiva level difference between immediate implants with and without CTG was 0.09 mm (95% CI -0.54 to 0.72), i.e. CTG maintained but did not increase the gingival level.
f.sample_size: 5 RCTs, 245 patients (4 RCTs in quantitative analysis)
f.follow_up: At least 6 months (included studies mostly 12 months)
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Low level of evidence and study limitations acknowledged

f.population: 24 consecutive patients receiving implants in the maxillary anterior area at the time of tooth extraction
f.intervention: Immediate implant with subepithelial connective tissue graft using the tunnel technique (last 12 patients)
f.comparison: Immediate implant without flap and without graft (first 12 patients)
outcomes: labial tissue volume/ridge width change at 6 months
f.main_result: Nongrafted group lost 1.063 mm of labial tissue dimension whereas the grafted group gained 0.34 mm after 6 months.

f.population: 20 patients (ages 27-87) with a single failing maxillary tooth in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Single immediate implant placement and provisionalization with subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Facial gingival level change at 1 year was significantly greater without graft (-0.70 mm) than with graft (-0.25 mm); marginal bone change did not differ significantly and all implants survived.
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by Straumann USA; authors declare no financial interests in the products
f.limitations: Short-term (1-year) follow-up with a small sample; longer-term studies are needed.

f.population: Adults with single immediate implant placement (within 24 h post-extraction); 8 studies, 409 implants
f.intervention: Submucosal buccal connective tissue graft with immediate implant placement
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement without CTG
f.main_result: Meta-analysis showed 0.41 mm less vertical mid-facial soft tissue change with CTG than without (95% CI 0.21-0.61), and 12 times lower risk of >=1 mm asymmetry.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; senior author has a collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare and Straumann
f.limitations: Only 1 RCT showed low risk of bias; results inconclusive for horizontal soft tissue change and papilla height.

f.population: Patient with an abscessed right central incisor and absent buccal bone wall (clinical report)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with a triple graft (cancellous and cortical bone plus connective tissue) from the maxillary tuberosity to reconstruct the buccal wall and repair recession
outcomes: buccal bone wall stability on CBCT
f.main_result: Technique reconstructs the buccal bone wall and gingival recession with a triple tuberosity graft in a single procedure; no quantitative outcome reported.
f.limitations: Difficult donor-site access in small mouth opening; limited tuberosity tissue for large or multiple-tooth defects; insufficient residual bone may prevent primary stability.

f.population: 60 patients with a failing maxillary tooth (first bicuspid to first bicuspid) in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with a tuberosity connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without soft tissue graft
f.main_result: CTG did not reduce mucosal volume loss (-0.68 vs -0.49 mm, p=.189) but gave a more coronal mid-facial mucosa level (+0.20 vs -0.48 mm, p=.014).
f.sample_size: 60 patients (30 test, 30 control); 25 per group analysed
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Nobel Biocare Services AG; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Post-extraction facial bone wall thickness was not included as a risk factor; CBCT data needed.

f.population: Two cases of single hopeless anterior tooth / fractured teeth 11 and 21 in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Vertical or horizontal double-parallel mattress suture to fix a subepithelial connective tissue graft in a tunnel during immediate implant placement and provisionalization
f.main_result: The two cases gave similar esthetic outcomes with vertical and horizontal sutures; the technique achieved stable passive graft fixation (preliminary, no quantitative data).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Additional randomized controlled studies are required; turning the graft over during suturing may confuse the surgeon.

f.population: 60 patients with a single failing maxillary anterior tooth (incisor, canine, first premolar)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with a tuberosity connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without graft
f.main_result: At 5 years mid-buccal mucosa level change was 0.6 mm recession in controls versus 0.1 mm in grafted sites (p=.008); bone, esthetics and satisfaction did not differ clinically.
f.sample_size: 60 patients (30 per group); 27 per group analysed at 5 years
f.follow_up: 5 years (60 months after final crown placement)
f.funding_coi: 1-year study supported by Nobel Biocare Services AG grant; no funding for 5-year evaluation; authors declare no conflicts
f.limitations: Risk factors for soft-tissue loss and ideal timing of soft-tissue augmentation remain unclear from this study.

f.population: 30 adults needing extraction of one anterior tooth (premolar to premolar)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement plus sub-epithelial connective tissue graft, without bone graft in the gap
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement alone
outcomes: vertical and horizontal buccal bone resorption
f.main_result: CTG did not affect vertical buccal bone resorption but reduced horizontal ridge change coronally and maintained tissue contour (change 0.32-0.04 mm vs 1.94-1.08 mm in controls) via greater soft tissue thickness.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by a grant from BioSAF IN Srl; no conflicts reported

f.main_result: Narrative overview: tunneling flap elevation without papilla detachment or vertical releasing incisions is proposed to improve blood supply, wound healing and esthetics across root coverage and implant soft-tissue augmentation.
f.limitations: Long-term data are lacking and controlled clinical trials are needed.

f.population: 250 subjects aged 17-66 with all maxillary front teeth present
f.intervention: CBCT measurement of facial bone wall thickness and CEJ-to-bone-crest distance at 1, 3 and 5 mm apical to the crest
outcomes: distance from CEJ to facial bone crest
f.main_result: The CEJ-bone crest distance was 1.6-3 mm; the facial bone wall was thin, with about 85% of sites under 1 mm and 40-60% under 0.5 mm.

f.population: 43 implant patients; maxillary first premolars and anterior teeth (1,036 measurable sites)
f.intervention: CBCT measurement of CEJ-to-buccal-crest distance and buccal bone thickness at crest, midroot and apex
outcomes: distance from CEJ to buccal bone crest
buccal bone thickness at crest, midroot, apex
f.main_result: Median CEJ-to-crest distance was 2.79 mm; buccal bone 1 mm below the crest was 1.13 mm at premolars and 0.83 mm at anterior teeth, with few anterior teeth exceeding 1 mm.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: Patients needing single-tooth extraction and implant replacement, upper or lower jaw
f.intervention: Single implant placed early (about 10 days) or delayed (about 3 months) after extraction
f.comparison: Late (conventional, about 17 months) placement
f.main_result: No significant differences among groups in implant survival or marginal bone level at 10 years (1.15, 1.53 and 1.42 mm for early, delayed, late).
f.limitations: Dropout of 11.7% by 10 years and radiographs missing for some late-group patients at T1.

f.population: Patients with a single missing tooth in the anterior area (2nd premolar to 2nd premolar)
f.intervention: Early implant placement 4-16 weeks after extraction (Type 2 and Type 3)
f.comparison: Late implant placement at least 16 weeks after extraction (Type 4)
f.main_result: Type 3 implants showed survival comparable to Type 4 (95% vs. 100%); both early protocols had high survival, few complications and high aesthetic scores.
f.sample_size: 19 articles from 6 studies, 140 patients and 140 implants
f.follow_up: minimum 1 year after implant placement (inclusion criterion)
f.funding_coi: Funded by the authors and their institutions; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Limited number of cases, heterogeneity and high risk of bias reduce generalizability.

f.population: Single tooth extraction sites in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Immediate, early and late implant placement after extraction, reviewed historically with clinical recommendations
f.main_result: Immediate placement is advised only with ideal anatomy (intact thick facial wall, thick biotype); otherwise early placement with soft tissue healing and contour augmentation (type 2, used in over 80% of the authors' cases).

f.population: Patients needing a single premolar or molar extraction and implant
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh extraction socket, flapless, with socket-gap grafting
f.comparison: Implant placed 12 weeks after extraction in healed site with flap
f.main_result: Implant success 100% in both groups; ISQ at insertion and loading did not differ; CBL at 12 months was 0.68 mm (immediate) vs 0.40 mm (delayed), P = .02.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Small sample size; longer follow-up needed.

f.population: Patients needing extraction and immediate implant at a non-molar site
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with grafting of the buccal gap with anorganic bovine bone, flapless approach (test group)
f.comparison: Same procedure with a mucoperiosteal flap (control group)
outcomes: influence of initial buccal plate width
f.main_result: About 0.5 mm mean loss in height and width at 6 months, with no significant difference between flap and flapless.

f.population: Patients needing extraction of premolar or molar teeth and later implant
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with porcine bone and collagen membrane using a flapless procedure with secondary soft tissue closure (test)
f.comparison: Same ridge preservation with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap and primary soft tissue closure (control)
f.main_result: No histological or histomorphometric difference between flap and flapless: new bone 22.5% vs 22.5%, marrow spaces 59.3% vs 59.4%, residual graft 18.6% vs 18.2%.
f.follow_up: 3 months to bone biopsy at implant placement

f.population: Six Labrador dogs, implants in distal alveoli of second mandibular premolars
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless, test site)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap (control site)
outcomes: remaining gap between implant and socket wall
f.main_result: Buccal crest resorption was 1.7 mm (flap) and 1.5 mm (flapless), with no significant differences between approaches.

f.population: Patients with a non-restorable single tooth in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement with provisionalization
f.comparison: Flap-involving immediate implant placement with provisionalization
f.main_result: Flap elevation caused more mesial and distal gingival margin recession at 3 months (p=0.02 and p=0.01), with no other significant differences up to 12 months.
f.funding_coi: Implants and abutments supplied free by Biomet 3i; conflict of interest: none

f.population: Adults needing a single maxillary anterior or premolar tooth extraction with intact buccal plate
f.intervention: Immediate implant with minimal split-thickness envelope flap (MSTEF), with GBR and connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant with conventional flap (control)
f.main_result: No significant differences between flap and MSTEF: PES 10.54 vs 10.80, WES 6.97 vs 6.95, survival and success 100%; esthetic failures were common in both groups.

f.population: Adult patients with a single immediate implant in incisor, cuspid or premolar position
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with flap elevation
outcomes: papillary and midfacial soft tissue change
f.main_result: Flapless surgery gave 0.48 mm less horizontal buccal bone change (95% CI 0.13-0.84, p = .007) with no difference in implant survival (RR 1.00).
f.sample_size: 5 RCTs, 140 patients with 140 implants (68 flapless, 72 flap)
f.limitations: Scarce data prevented meta-analysis of secondary outcomes; three RCTs at high risk of bias.

f.population: 59 titanium implants in edentulous mandibular areas of 5 foxhounds
f.intervention: Six implant types (A-F): 1-piece or 2-piece, non-submerged or submerged, with the rough/smooth border or the implant-abutment microgap at, above or below the bone crest
f.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the six implant types (non-submerged vs submerged, 1-piece vs 2-piece)
outcomes: distance from rough/smooth border and microgap to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: In 1-piece implants the first bone-to-implant contact lay within about 0.2 mm of the rough/smooth border; in 2-piece implants the microgap position determined crestal bone loss, greatest (2.25 mm) when it lay 1 mm below the crest (type F).
f.follow_up: 6 months (abutment connection of submerged implants at 3 months)
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants, machined coronal part and SLA apical part
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation; Straumann manufactured the implants

f.population: 59 titanium implants placed at different levels to the alveolar crest in 5 foxhounds
f.intervention: Six types of unloaded titanium implants (1-part or 2-part, nonsubmerged or submerged, microgap and rough/smooth interface at different levels) followed with standardized radiographs
f.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the implant types
outcomes: distance from implant/abutment top to most coronal bone-to-implant contact (DIB)
f.main_result: In 2-part implants the most coronal bone-to-implant contact lay about 2 mm below the microgap whether non-submerged or submerged; in 1-part implants it followed the rough/smooth interface; changes occurred within the first month.
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants with SLA surface
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation

f.population: Patients with at least two adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla (4 studies, 114 patients)
f.intervention: Multiple adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla
f.comparison: Radiographic horizontal distance between the outer surfaces of the two adjacent implants
f.main_result: No precise threshold for the optimal horizontal distance between adjacent implants could be defined; incomplete inter-implant mucosa fill tended to occur at distances under 3 mm in 3 of 4 studies (one significant, p = .008).
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant supported the consensus meeting
f.limitations: Few studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria and heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis

f.population: 30 partially edentulous patients receiving two adjacent implant-supported crowns (60 implants)
f.intervention: Two adjacent implants placed at a horizontal interimplant distance of about 2 mm, 3 mm or over 4 mm, restored with single crowns after 3 months
f.comparison: 2-mm vs 3-mm vs over 4-mm interimplant distance groups
outcomes: probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque
f.main_result: No statistically significant differences in marginal and midproximal bone crest loss between the 2-mm, 3-mm and over 4-mm groups at any time point (marginal bone loss at 24 months 0.27, 0.23 and 0.44 mm).

f.population: 41 pairs of platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart in 37 patients
f.intervention: Platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart, evaluated radiographically
outcomes: height of the interimplant bone peak relative to the line connecting implant-abutment interfaces
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone resorption was 0.62 mm and horizontal 0.60 mm; the interimplant bone peak stayed on average 0.24 mm above the line connecting the two implant-abutment interfaces (preserved in 64% of pairs).

f.intervention: Four-dimensional (timing) concept and classification of extraction sites for immediate implant placement in the esthetic region
f.main_result: Timing of extraction and implant placement is added as a fourth dimension to 3D implant positioning, with a four-class site classification guiding when immediate placement is indicated.

f.population: 93 adults needing a maxillary tooth (15-25) replaced by an immediate implant
f.intervention: Immediate placement of OsseoSpeed implants in fresh extraction sockets, without additional grafting
f.comparison: Cylindrical (3.5/4.0 mm) vs conical/cylindrical (4.5/5.0 mm) implant configuration
f.main_result: After 3 years the mean gingival zenith change was 0.23 mm (not significant) and 79% mesial and 72% distal papillae were more than half-filled or complete, independent of implant configuration, tooth category, smoking and buccal wall thickness.

f.population: 40 subjects with a hopeless maxillary anterior or premolar tooth
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate provisionalization (non-occluding temporary crown)
f.comparison: Immediate placement with a healing abutment (no immediate provisionalization)
f.main_result: At 12 months mucosal level, papilla height and marginal bone changes did not differ significantly between groups; implant survival was 90% (test) vs 100% (control); immediate provisionalization did not improve the esthetic outcome.
f.follow_up: 12 months after permanent restoration (placed at 4 months)
f.funding_coi: University of Michigan Graduate Student Research Grant and a Neobiotech gift (implants provided); one author received speaking honoraria from Neobiotech
f.limitations: Two test implants failed early, possibly leaving the marginal bone analysis underpowered

f.population: 40 patients with a failing tooth in the maxillary anterior region
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement (NobelActive) with immediate provisionalization (group A)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with delayed provisionalization (group B)
f.main_result: After 5 years mean marginal bone level change was about 0.71 mm (group A) vs 0.49-0.54 mm (group B), not significantly different; implant and restoration survival was 100%.
f.sample_size: 40 patients (20 per group); 35 analysed at 5 years
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Nobel Biocare Services AG; implant materials provided
f.limitations: Fewer patients analysed at 5 years (35 of 40) reduced power; university setting with selected patients

f.population: 70 patients with a failed maxillary anterior tooth
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (screw-retained provisional crown)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement without provisionalization (healing abutment)
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss did not differ significantly between groups and survival was 100%; Group A had significantly higher ISQ at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months.

f.population: 21 patients receiving single-tooth implant replacement in maxillary sites distal to the canine (27 implants, 23 biopsies)
f.intervention: Experimental abutment connected at implant placement, with soft tissue biopsies after 2, 4, 8 or 12 weeks of healing for histological and ESEM analysis
f.comparison: Different healing times (2, 4, 8, 12 weeks)
f.main_result: At 8 weeks the soft tissue was about 3.6 mm (barrier epithelium 1.9 mm, connective tissue 1.7 mm), similar at 12 weeks; differences across healing times were not significant.

f.population: Animal and human studies of implants placed immediately into infected extraction sites (periapical or periodontal infection)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement into infected sites after debridement, usually with antibiotics and GBR
f.comparison: Pristine or non-infected sites
f.main_result: Implants can be placed into infected sites with survival similar to non-infected sites, though animal data suggest bone-to-implant contact may be impaired.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Evidence limited to few studies and patients; infection classification vague.

f.population: Patients treated with implant-supported full-arch fixed prostheses at one specialist clinic (1980-2018)
f.intervention: Implant-supported full-arch fixed dental prostheses
f.main_result: Cumulative prosthesis survival was 93.3% at 10 years and 87.1% at 20 years; bruxism raised risk of failure (HR 3.276) and technical complications.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Folktandvården Skåne AB; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Retrospective design with incomplete records; non-standardized treatment and bruxism diagnosis by self-report.

f.intervention: ACP classification system (Class I-IV) for diagnosis of the completely dentate patient
f.main_result: The ACP defines four classes of completely dentate patients, from uncomplicated (Class I) to most complex (Class IV), using diagnostic criteria for tooth condition and occlusal scheme.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the American College of Prosthodontists

f.population: Patients with at least one edentulous jaw, tooth loss mainly due to periodontitis
f.intervention: Fixed or removable full-arch implant-supported prostheses
f.comparison: Fixed versus removable full-arch designs
f.main_result: Cumulative implant loss at 5 years was 1.85% for fixed versus 4.45% for removable prostheses; 1-year loss was similar (0.64% vs 0.71%).
f.follow_up: At least 12 months; analysis up to 5 years
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Limited low-quality data; no assessment beyond 5 years.

f.population: Adults with an edentulous mandible undergoing implant treatment
f.intervention: Three implants supporting a fixed mandibular prosthesis
f.comparison: Mandibular fixed complete prosthesis with more than three implants
f.main_result: Mean cumulative implant survival was 96.2% over 3.35 years, with mean marginal bone loss of 1.25 mm and high patient satisfaction.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
f.limitations: Longer-term comparative data lacking.

f.population: Patients with complete edentulism treated with full arch immediate implants
f.intervention: Full-arch immediate implant placement and loading with PRF and i-PRF (Simonpieri technique)
f.main_result: Author reports over 98% success in full-arch immediate loading with PRF over 14 years.

f.population: Critical-sized dehiscence defects in mandibular canines of dogs
f.intervention: β-TCP alloplast with modified perforated collagen membrane
f.comparison: β-TCP alloplast with occlusive collagen membrane
f.main_result: Both groups regenerated periodontal tissues, but the perforated membrane gave higher bone surface area (70.9% vs 44.5% at 1 month; 82.5% vs 73.2% at 2 months).
materials_brands: BioTECK equine type I collagen membrane
f.limitations: Small sample; further larger studies needed.

f.population: Mouse ST2 bone marrow stromal cells (osteoblast lineage) in culture
f.intervention: DBBM particles pre-coated with bone-conditioned medium (BCM)
f.comparison: DBBM particles alone
f.main_result: BCM coating increased cell adhesion 2-fold, raised COL1A2, ALP and OCN mRNA, and gave 3-fold more alizarin red staining.
f.funding_coi: DBBM supplied by Geistlich AG; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: In vitro only; animal study needed.

f.population: Patients receiving posterior implants with small non-contained buccal bone dehiscences (≤5 mm)
f.intervention: Spontaneous healing of the dehiscence
f.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (DBBM + collagen membrane)
f.main_result: Survival was 100% in both groups at 7.5 years; remaining buccal dehiscence was larger with spontaneous healing (2.51 mm) than GBR (1.66 mm, p=0.02), with no difference in marginal bone levels.
f.sample_size: 22 patients with 28 implants; 20 patients with 26 implants recalled
materials_brands: Deproteinized bovine bone mineral with collagen membrane (GBR group)
f.funding_coi: Implant material from Oral Reconstruction Foundation grant; three authors report grants and fees from Geistlich Pharma outside the work
f.limitations: No power calculation possible due to lack of data

f.population: Experimental (mostly animal) studies of bone regeneration with cortical perforations in the recipient area
f.intervention: Cortical perforations combined with GBR, autologous bone blocks or periosteal distraction
f.main_result: Evidence that cortical perforations increase bone formation in GBR and with bone blocks is limited; number and size of perforations did not appear to matter.
f.funding_coi: No funding source declared
f.limitations: Moderate to high risk of bias; studies not comparable.

f.population: Murine bone marrow cell cultures exposed to conditioned medium from porcine fresh cortical bone and demineralized bone matrix
f.intervention: Conditioned medium from fresh bone (BCM, also heated to 85°C) and from demineralized bone matrix (DCM) added to RANKL and M-CSF induced osteoclastogenesis
f.comparison: Cultures with RANKL and M-CSF alone, and unheated BCM
outcomes: osteoclast marker and fusion gene expression
f.main_result: Unheated BCM did not change osteoclastogenesis, heated BCM approximately doubled TRAP-positive multinucleated cells, and DCM significantly stimulated osteoclastogenesis irrespective of heating.
f.sample_size: Experiments repeated at least four times in duplicate
materials_brands: Porcine cortical bone chips (BCM) and demineralized bone matrix (DCM)
f.limitations: Most but not all preparations of heated BCM supported osteoclastogenesis, and the resorption assay was not quantified because of large variation.

f.population: Patients with a single tooth gap in the anterior maxilla and a horizontal alveolar defect, bucco-palatal bone at least 6 mm
f.intervention: Single implant with CTG in a buccal envelope to re-establish buccal convexity (test)
f.comparison: Single implant with GBR using DBBM (Bio-Oss) and a collagen membrane (control)
f.main_result: PES did not differ (10.11 GBR vs 10.48 CTG, p=0.577) but MSI was lower with CTG (1.10 vs 2.53, p=0.017); GBR had more oedema, hematoma and painkillers (7.10 vs 4.86).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; implants and prosthetic components supplied free by Nobel Biocare; Prof. Cosyn has agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann.

f.population: Patients with severe vertical alveolar atrophy and missing teeth needing vertical bone augmentation for implants
f.intervention: Self-inflating hydrogel tissue expander (TissueMax) placed subperiosteally for ~4 weeks, then tunneling vertical bone graft without full flap reflection
f.comparison: Conventional vertical GBR with full flap and periosteal releasing incisions
outcomes: radiographic vertical bone gain and retention
f.main_result: Vertical bone gain was higher with the expander (5.12 vs 4.22 mm, P<0.05) and 6-month vertical bone reduction was smaller (30.7% vs 55.0%); mean soft tissue gain was 6.88 mm vertically.
f.follow_up: 6-month retention after grafting, then mean 10.2 months of prosthetic loading
materials_brands: Cytoplast RTM collagen membrane (Osteogenics) and OssMem (Osstem)
Cytoplast Ti-250XL d-PTFE titanium reinforced membrane
Straumann bone level SLActive and Osstem TS III SA implants
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; supported by a Korea Health Technology R&D Project grant (Ministry of Health & Welfare); some authors affiliated with Osstem Bio R&D Center.
f.limitations: Studies comparing the two techniques without tissue expanders are needed to elucidate the net effect of tissue expansion.

f.population: In vitro: bone chips from fresh pig mandibles and human mesenchymal cells (oral fibroblasts)
f.intervention: Preparation of bone-conditioned medium from native, pasteurized, autoclaved or demineralized pig bone and a bioassay on TGF-b regulated gene expression
f.comparison: Un-stimulated controls and medium from autoclaved (121 °C) bone
outcomes: expression of ADM, PTX3, IL11, IL33, NOX4 and PRG4 in oral fibroblasts
f.main_result: BCM from fresh, pasteurized or demineralized bone changed target gene expression (ADM and PTX3 down to 0.4-fold, IL11, IL33, NOX4, PRG4 up to 200-fold), whereas medium from autoclaved bone did not.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose; one author received a scholarship from the Foundation of Dental Research and Education, Basel.
f.limitations: BCM cannot be fully standardized because of variations between donors and harvesting techniques.

f.population: Four young adult mongrel dogs, membranes placed subperiosteally in the maxilla
f.intervention: Subperiosteal placement of three membranes: bovine collagen (GenDerm), collagen (Genoss, Dentium) and porcine dermis (Kytinon M.O.R.)
f.comparison: The three membranes compared with each other, and with normal gingival tissue samples
f.main_result: Absorption was <35% at 15 days for all membranes; at 90 days GenDerm bovine collagen was completely absorbed, Dentium collagen >65% and porcine dermis only 35-65%.
f.funding_coi: Self-supported; authors declare no conflicts of interest.

f.population: 40 clinical studies of lateral ridge augmentation (simultaneous, staged or ridge expansion) pooling 1,242 patients and 1,881 implants
f.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation (GBR with particulate grafts and membranes, or autogenous bone blocks) staged or simultaneous with implant placement
f.comparison: Comparisons between grafting materials and membrane types (RCTs/CCTs); otherwise baseline vs final
f.main_result: Simultaneous approach gave a significant defect height reduction (WMD -4.28 mm) and staged approach a bone width gain (WMD 3.90 mm); implant survival and success were high (>95%).
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest declared.
f.limitations: Case series did not meet the quality categories and well-designed long-term RCTs are lacking.

f.main_result: Buccal bone augmentation of more than 2 mm beyond the implant platform and vertical augmentation to a line joining adjacent interproximal bone peaks are needed for stable esthetic soft tissue around multiple implants; strategic pontics help preserve papilla height.
f.follow_up: 2-year periapical radiograph of the illustrated case
f.limitations: Very few long-term studies exist on compromised cases with multiple implants.

f.main_result: Osteoinduction, osteoconduction and osseointegration are interrelated but distinct; osteoinduction produces most new bone in healing, while osseointegration is stable direct bone anchorage of an implant maintained over time.

Collagen membranes show advantageous biological and clinical features versus non-resorbable and other resorbable membranes but need graft support and fixation, and cross-linked types have higher exposure rates.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared.

f.population: Patients with horizontal alveolar ridge deficiencies receiving implants after/with lateral bone augmentation
f.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation procedures (GBR, bone blocks), simultaneous or staged
f.comparison: Other lateral augmentation procedures or no treatment
f.main_result: Lateral ridge augmentation maintains peri-implant health; BOP changes minimal and no significant differences among modalities; peri-implantitis incidence 16-26% at 6-8 years.
f.funding_coi: Consensus meeting supported by Osteology Foundation grant; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Few studies in meta-analyses, not powered for peri-implant health outcomes, limited to English controlled studies.

f.population: Adult hound dogs (4 animals, 31 experimental sites)
f.intervention: Tibial corticocancellous bone graft to the lateral mandible protected by macroporous or microporous titanium mesh or resorbable mesh
f.comparison: Grafts without mesh (controls); cortical perforations vs none
f.main_result: New bone area was highest with the macroporous titanium mesh (66.26 mm2) versus microporous (52.82), resorbable (46.76) and no mesh (29.80).
materials_brands: Stryker-Leibinger macroporous and microporous titanium meshes

f.population: 15 patients with aggressive periodontitis, two intrabony defects each
f.intervention: GTR with xenogenic graft plus modified perforated collagen membrane
f.comparison: Xenogenic graft plus standard collagen membrane
f.main_result: PPD, CAL, DD and ACP improved in both groups without between-group differences; MPM sites gained additional LDF 0.4 mm and %DF 6.4% from 6 to 12 months.

f.population: Atrophic alveolar ridges in maxilla and mandible (case presentation)
f.intervention: In situ shell technique: autogenous bone plate, allograft plus injectable PRF, bioresorbable membrane
outcomes: osseous regeneration sufficient for implant placement
f.main_result: Sufficient osseous regeneration was achieved to place dental implants in an ideal position.
f.follow_up: 6 months of healing before second-stage surgery
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Learning curve; outcomes may differ for less experienced clinicians; further clinical and histological trials needed

f.population: Eight mongrel dogs with standardized buccal dehiscence-type defects at implants in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: DBBM with or without autogenous bone chips and with or without collagen membrane
f.comparison: DBBM alone vs the other graft/membrane combinations
f.main_result: Autogenous bone chips and the collagen membrane increased bone formation around DBBM particles; wound protection early may be critical.
f.funding_coi: Funded by a grant from Geistlich Pharma AG; materials provided by Straumann and Geistlich; one author consults for Straumann

f.population: 21 included articles on barrier membrane characteristics
f.intervention: Barrier membranes for GBR (criteria an ideal membrane should fulfil)
outcomes: membrane criteria: biocompatibility, space maintenance, occlusiveness, handling, bioactivation
f.main_result: Ideal GBR membranes need biocompatibility, space maintenance, occlusive function, easy handling and bioactivation-friendly properties; biocompatibility matters most.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: 37 patients needing implants with bony defects in posterior maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Defects grafted with bovine bone mineral and covered with PEG hydrogel membrane
f.comparison: Collagen membrane (control)
f.main_result: Mean vertical defect fill was 5.63 mm (PEG) versus 4.25 mm (collagen); fills 94.9% and 96.4%; more soft tissue complications with PEG.

f.population: 58 of 72 original patients with implants placed with or without simultaneous GBR
f.intervention: Implants with simultaneous GBR using DBBM and collagen or e-PTFE membrane
f.comparison: Implants fully surrounded by bone without GBR (control)
f.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 93.2% (control 94.6%, collagen 91.9%, e-PTFE 92.6%), not significantly different.
f.sample_size: 265 implants in 72 patients originally; 58 patients examined

f.population: Human peri-implantitis lesions (>10) in 6 included studies
f.intervention: Regenerative surgical treatment of peri-implantitis
f.main_result: Weighted mean radiographic bone fill was 2.41 mm and PD reduction 3.06 mm after at least 36 months.
f.limitations: Limited long-term evidence; hard to discern grafting material from new bone

f.population: Clinical studies of implants in augmented ridges or with simultaneous peri-implant grafting
f.intervention: Peri-implant hard-tissue augmentation prior to or with implant placement
f.main_result: Augmentation procedures seem to give stable peri-implant tissues, but long-term buccal bone stability is assessed by few studies; the performance of meta-analysis was impossible.
f.limitations: Heterogeneous outcome measures, methods, grafts and implants prevented meta-analysis

f.intervention: Collagen-based biomaterials for tissue engineering

f.main_result: No decisive evidence that computer-assisted implant surgery is superior to conventional procedures in safety, outcomes, morbidity or efficiency; accuracy is cumulative-error dependent and lowest with bone-supported guides.
The accuracy, efficacy and complication rate of computer-guided implant treatment remain within acceptable clinical limits, provided each step of the 6-step digital workflow is verified.

Identifying the etiology (lip, crown, altered passive eruption, vertical maxillary excess) is the key step because it dictates the treatment: crown lengthening, lip repositioning, Botox or orthognathic surgery.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.main_result: Periodontists can treat gummy smile and short tooth syndrome with a biological approach (re-exposing the CEJ) or a restorative approach; misdiagnosing altered eruption risks esthetic and periodontal failure.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.main_result: The authors propose an adult classification of gummy smile and short tooth syndrome causes, used with an outside-in diagnostic process, to predict outcomes and determine treatment.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: Patients with gummy smile (authors' clinical experience)
f.intervention: Hyaluronic acid filler injections (RD Dynamic Restructuring) guided by the Mercado-Rosso classification
f.main_result: Treatment maintains 70-80% of its effectiveness after 10 months, with retreatment suggested at 10 and 18 months.
f.funding_coi: Medical writing and publication fees funded by Teoxane SL; Dr Mercado received a Teoxane grant
f.limitations: A first step: the classification should be validated and treatment approaches evaluated in a cohort of patients.

f.main_result: Gummy smile has soft-tissue to hard-tissue origins, so the clinician must distinguish them to choose the strategy that meets patient expectations.
f.funding_coi: Editorial-board relationships of some authors with the journal

f.population: Partially edentulous patients receiving at least one posterior implant
f.intervention: Permanent abutment placed at implant placement (no disconnection)
f.comparison: Healing abutment with two disconnection/reconnection cycles before definitive prosthesis
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss at 6 months was 0.13 mm (test) vs 0.28 mm (control), not significantly different; mucosal dimensions did not differ.
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by Straumann USA; no conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 20 patients with a single missing tooth in the anterior maxilla (FDI 13-23)
f.intervention: Fixed implant-supported provisional crown with soft tissue conditioning (dynamic compression technique) for 6 months before the final crown
f.comparison: Final crown inserted directly without a provisional phase
f.main_result: Combined modPES+WES was 15.6 (group 1, with provisional) vs 12.2 (group 2); modPES differed significantly (P=.018), WES did not; bone loss was similar.
materials_brands: Straumann Bone Level Implant RC SLActive
f.funding_coi: Financial support from Straumann Group; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small sample size

f.population: 22 periodontally healthy patients with a single failing tooth in the aesthetic zone (15-25), thick gingival biotype, intact buccal bone wall
f.intervention: Flapless single immediate implant (NobelActive) with bovine bone particles in the buccal gap and immediate non-functional screw-retained provisional crown; CTG when early complications appeared
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss was 0.12 mm at 1 year and 0.19 mm at 5 years, but mid-facial recession rose from 0.28 to 0.53 mm and 8 of 17 implants showed aesthetic complications.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; Nobel Biocare provided free materials; authors declare collaboration agreements with implant companies

f.intervention: Immediate loading of dental implants and the role of primary stability
f.main_result: Good primary stability is the core issue for immediate loading; it depends on bone density and quality, implant shape, design, surface and surgical technique.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest and no external funding
f.limitations: Further research needed in poor bone, multiple implants and augmentation situations.

f.population: Stainless-steel master model of a mandible with 5 implant analogs; 16 stone casts
f.intervention: 4 implant impression techniques (tapered unsplinted, squared unsplinted, squared splinted with acrylic, squared with lateral extension)
f.comparison: the 4 techniques compared against each other and the master model
outcomes: dimensional accuracy of implant positions on casts (Deviation Index)
f.main_result: Maximum distortion difference between techniques was only 0.31% (P=.022), clinically negligible.
f.sample_size: 4 casts per technique, 5 implants per cast

f.population: Sintered pellets of mica glass ceramic with 0-20 wt.% yttria-stabilised zirconia (laboratory specimens)
f.intervention: Addition of 3 mol% YSZ (5-20 wt.%) to fluorophlogopite mica glass ceramic
f.comparison: Pure mica glass and commercial IPS e.max Press lithium disilicate
f.main_result: With 20 wt.% YSZ: hardness 9.2 GPa, elastic modulus 125 GPa, indentation toughness 3.6 MPa·m1/2 and solubility about 30 µg/cm2, within ISO limits.
f.sample_size: At least 5 specimens per composition (10 for solubility)
f.funding_coi: Wellcome Trust DBT India Alliance fellowship; Department of Biotechnology, Government of India

f.population: 75 potential implant sites in the posterior mandible from CT scans of 34 patients; used to build finite-element models
f.intervention: Finite-element models with low/high cancellous-bone density, crestal cortical-bone density and thickness, loaded with 200 N oblique load on a Straumann implant
f.comparison: Low vs high bone-density and thin vs thick cortical-bone models
outcomes: maximum von Mises equivalent strain in crestal cortical bone
maximum von Mises equivalent strain in cancellous bone
f.main_result: Maximum strains in low-density cancellous-bone models were 1.56-2.62-fold (cortical) and 3.49-5.31-fold (cancellous) higher than in high-density models.
f.sample_size: 75 implant sites in 34 patients (CT); finite-element models
materials_brands: Straumann threaded implant, 4.1 mm x 10 mm

f.population: Patients treated with dental implants at one specialist clinic in Malmo, Sweden; bruxers vs non-bruxers
f.intervention: Dental implant placement; exposure variable was bruxism
f.comparison: Bruxers versus non-bruxers
f.main_result: Bruxism was a significant risk factor for implant failure (HR about 3.4; failure 13.0% in bruxers vs 4.6% in non-bruxers).
f.funding_coi: Funded by Region Skane research funds, Swedish Research Council, Folktandvarden AB and CNPq; no conflicts declared

f.population: 138 patients (147 implants) with peri-implantitis
f.intervention: Reconstructive surgery using bone substitute material
f.comparison: Access flap surgery (control)
outcomes: composite outcome (implant not lost, no BOP/SOP, PPD <=5 mm, <=1 mm recession)
PPD, BOP, buccal keratinized mucosa, buccal recession
f.main_result: Composite success was 16.4% (test) vs 13.5% (control), not significant; buccal recession was lower in the test group (0.7 vs 1.1 mm).
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation Large Clinical Grant; several authors report honoraria/grants from Dentsply Sirona, Straumann, Geistlich etc.
f.limitations: No blinding to group allocation was performed.

f.population: 141 subjects needing single anterior maxillary or first premolar tooth replacement
f.intervention: Single implants with conical interface (OsseoSpeed TX), immediately provisionalized
f.comparison: Flat-to-flat (NobelSpeedy) and platform-switched (NanoTite Certain PREVAIL) interfaces
outcomes: plaque index and bleeding on probing
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss at 5 years was -0.16 mm (conical), -0.92 mm (flat-to-flat) and -0.81 mm (platform-switched) (P<.0005); mucosal changes were minimal in all groups.
f.funding_coi: First author receives research grants and honorarium from Dentsply Implants

f.population: 60 included studies: 18 in vitro, 5 animal, 6 case reports, 31 clinical studies on I-PRF
f.intervention: Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (I-PRF) in regenerative dentistry
f.main_result: Of 60 included studies, I-PRF showed anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and regenerative effects on wound, periodontal, bone, cartilage and pulp tissue, and faster orthodontic tooth movement; periodontal parameters in vivo lack consensus.
f.funding_coi: Funding stated as none; part of the research supported by NIDCR/NIH grants; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: Only English-language studies included; further randomized clinical trials recommended.

f.population: 95 patients with posterior partially edentulous maxilla or mandible sites
f.intervention: 6 mm (4.0 x 6) implants
f.comparison: 11 mm (4.0 x 11) standard-length implants
f.main_result: At 3 years MBL was 0.27 mm (6 mm) vs 0.44 mm (11 mm) apical to platform, favoring short implants; survival 96% vs 99%, not significant.
f.funding_coi: Fully sponsored by Dentsply Sirona Implants; two authors received lecture honoraria

f.population: 50 edentulous or to-be-edentulous patients needing an implant-supported cross-arch prosthesis
f.intervention: Immediately loaded cross-arch prostheses on four to eight roughened-surface implants (iRES Shape 1BC)
f.comparison: Machined/turned surface implants (iRES iPerio), 25 patients
f.main_result: At 1 year no prosthesis failed; two machined implants failed in one patient; marginal bone loss -0.64 mm (rough) vs -0.68 mm (turned), no significant difference.
f.funding_coi: I-RES, the implant manufacturer, donated implants and components; no interference declared
f.limitations: Small sample size (pilot) and baseline imbalance in implant length and number of implants per patient.

f.intervention: Alteration of occlusal vertical dimension (reasons, five areas of concern, methods of establishing it)
f.main_result: The author concludes there are several correct approaches; altering vertical dimension does not harm the TMJ or produce muscle pain with an ideal occlusal scheme, muscle activity returns to baseline after 3-4 months, and stability is unknown.

f.population: Y-TZP zirconia cubes (10 mm) veneered with five veneering ceramics (in vitro specimens)
f.intervention: Zirconia surface treatments (polishing, sandblasting, silica-coating), liner application, and regeneration firing before veneering
f.comparison: Polished zirconia surface without liner or regeneration firing
f.main_result: Shear strength ranged 23.5±3.4 to 33.0±6.8 MPa with no clear correlation to surface treatment; sandblasting did not improve bonding and regeneration firing reduced it.
f.sample_size: 10 specimens per combination of veneering ceramic and treatment
materials_brands: Veneering ceramics: Cerabien ZR, IPS e.max, Triceram, Vintage ZR, VM9
f.funding_coi: Vita Zahnfabrik manufactured the Y-TZP cubes; ceramic materials supplied by manufacturers

f.population: Polished 3Y-TZP zirconia disks (9 mm diameter, 2 mm thick)
f.intervention: Hydrofluoric acid etching at 5, 20 and 40% concentration for varying times, with analysis of reaction products
f.comparison: Non-etched control surface
f.main_result: HF 40% gave the fastest, most uniform roughening; fluoride precipitates formed on the surface, so cleaning is essential, and roughness evolution slowed after about one hour.
f.sample_size: One cleaned sample per condition in the preliminary study; 3 (AFM) and 10 (WLI) samples per experimental point
f.funding_coi: European Commission 7th Framework Programme (Marie Curie ITN), Spanish MINECO and Government of Catalonia
f.limitations: Authors note polishing is not part of commercial implant processing and effects of precipitates on bonding and patient health are unknown.

f.population: 100 polymer-infiltrated ceramic crowns (Vita Enamic) cemented on one-piece zirconia implants (ceramic.implant CI)
f.intervention: Cementation with 13 cements (temporary, glass-ionomer, self-adhesive, adhesive resin) with or without manufacturer ceramic primer
f.comparison: Cement types against each other, with versus without ceramic primer
f.main_result: Retention was highest for Panavia 21 (605 N) and Panavia F 2.0 (318 N); other resin cements 222-270 N, above glass-ionomer (196 N) and temporary cements; primer helped only Panavia SA.
f.sample_size: 100 crowns on 100 implants, n=5 per group; shear n=6, diametral tensile n=10
materials_brands: Panavia F 2.0, Panavia 21, Panavia SA, Panavia V5
f.funding_coi: Vita Zahnfabrik supported the study with materials; one author is a Vita laboratory manager

f.intervention: Proposed 'esthetic width' concept for metal-ceramic restorations: margin positioning, reduced metal framework with extended porcelain shoulder, pontic and interdental design
f.main_result: Reduced frameworks with porcelain shoulders avoid the umbrella effect; ridge-lap pontics and interdental mini-wings are recommended for collapsed anterior ridges and flattened papillae.

f.population: Patients with trigeminal neuralgia in primary and secondary care
f.intervention: UK (Royal College of Surgeons of England) guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of TN: first-line carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, MRI, neurosurgery, multidisciplinary care
f.main_result: Guidelines advise prompt diagnosis after excluding dental causes, early first-line medication, and multidisciplinary care with long-term outcomes collection.
f.funding_coi: Dr. Bahra consulted for Pfizer; Dr. Zakrzewska for Biogen and Noema Pharma
f.limitations: Guidelines depend on accurate phenotyping; surgical efficacy data come from nonrandomized single-intervention studies.

f.population: Patients with a single missing first molar and intact, vital abutments (40 FPDs)
f.intervention: Zirconia occlusal veneer FPDs with two preparation designs (D1, D2) in 3Y-TZP or 5Y-PSZ
f.comparison: Four groups: D1/D2 x 3Y-TZP/5Y-PSZ compared with each other
f.main_result: No debonding or recurrent caries; two D1/5Y FPDs fractured completely (4 and 17 months) and one D2/5Y cracked at 1 month; no significant group differences.
materials_brands: DDcubeX2 (3Y-TZP) and DDBioZX2 (5Y-PSZ) zirconia, Dental Direkt
f.funding_coi: No funding reported; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Cannot be placed immediately after extraction, no provisional FPD possible, complex preparation limits routine use, demanding isolation.
